A kinetic-theory identity with phase-appropriate carriers, a quark--gluon plasma above T_0 and a chiral pion gas below, reproduces the same pattern, and lattice speed-of-sound data can be shown to be consistent as well. The bottom-up VQCD in the deconfined phase supports a negative slope for large temperatures; the slope crossover is not resolvable from the available ζ_\parallel/s, η_\parallel/s plots.

papers.title_en: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
papers.abstract_en: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, Néel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.

papers.title_en: Exact Infrared Triangle in Gravity with Long-Range Interactions
papers.abstract_en: Einstein gravity coupled to massless matter exhibits universality in the infrared. In the presence of long-range interactions we show that a novel superrotation charge conservation is equivalent to the massless limit of the classical logarithmic soft graviton theorem, and we propose a formula for the corresponding tail to the displacement memory. These results, which extend earlier work on gravity coupled to massive matter in a qualitatively different way, are exact in the gravitational coupling and reveal that long-range gravitational dressings resum. We also compute higher-order corrections to the known superrotation charge which are exact in the gravitational coupling and would correspond to a 1-loop exact correction to the Cachazo-Strominger subleading soft graviton theorem.

papers.title_en: Searching for Massive Scalar Fields with non-minimal Curvature Couplings in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Ringdown Signals
papers.abstract_en: We search for massive scalar fields with non-minimal curvature couplings using the loudest ringdown signals observed by LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA. We find that current ringdown observations do not provide informative constraints on the scalar-field mass. We nevertheless constrain the coupling length scale for scalar fields satisfying $Mμ<1$, where $μ$ is the scalar-field mass, yielding marginalized 90$\%$ credible upper limits of 60.4 km and 59.8 km for dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar Gauss-Bonnet couplings, respectively.

papers.title_en: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract_en: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

papers.title_en: FastBox: A lightweight Python package for rapid cosmological 21cm intensity mapping simulations
papers.abstract_en: FastBox is a Python package for generating fast, physically realistic simulations of cosmological signals in three-dimensional co-moving boxes, with the primary focus of its application being 21cm intensity mapping (IM) experiments. It provides a framework for producing cosmology-dependent Gaussian and log-normal density fields, as well as modelling the effects of redshift-space distortions and linear biasing, among others. Models of instrumental systematics are incorporated, including radiometer noise and beam convolutions. Diffuse and point source foreground models are included, along with a number of foreground filtering strategies such as PCA, ICA, and transfer function correction via mock signal injection. Lastly, estimators are provided for power spectra, the two-point correlation function, and the equilateral bispectrum. The same underlying density field can also be Poisson-sampled into a discrete galaxy catalogue, so that 21cm and galaxy tracers are simulated from common initial conditions and their cross-power spectrum can be measured. Simulation grids may be cubic or anisotropic, with independent side lengths and cell counts along each Cartesian axis. FastBox is designed as a lightweight but realistic test-bench for the development and validation of end-to-end cosmological analysis pipelines.

papers.title_en: An analytic diffusion model for viewing-angle effects in explosive transients
papers.abstract_en: The tight observed relation between the peak bolometric luminosity, $L_{\mathrm p}$, and the width ratio $L_{30}/L_{\mathrm p}$ of Type Ia supernovae, with $L_{30}$ the luminosity 30 d after explosion, makes viewing-angle effects a useful test of explosion models. We develop an analytic diffusion model for homologously expanding asymmetric ejecta with uniform density and grey opacity, based on a Green's-function solution and an Eddington surface-emission prescription, and obtain angle-dependent light curves for a displaced spherical source and for oblate ejecta. We validate them against Monte Carlo (MC) radiative transfer and derive geometric approximations to the peak-luminosity anisotropy. For a displaced spherical source, the quasi-steady approximation, equivalent to stationary diffusion in frozen ejecta, gives $L_{\mathrm p}(θ)/L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}\simeq1+(17/8)z_{\mathrm{off}}\cosθ$, where $z_{\mathrm{off}}$ is the displacement in units of the ejecta radius, $θ$ the viewing angle from the displacement axis, and $L_{\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{avg}}$ the angle-averaged peak. This dipole is $\mathord{\approx}10$ per cent below the finite-time value in the tested configurations. For oblate ejecta, the leading term is quadrupolar and is set by a single shape parameter. Effective models of 19 off-centre sub-Chandrasekhar explosions recover the MC peak times, peak luminosities, and width ratios to median errors of 3, 4, and 6 per cent, and the extent in $L_{\mathrm p}$ of the MC tracks, but underestimate the width-ratio variation with viewing angle by a factor of 2 to 3. An oblate construction captures the scale of peak luminosity variations in six equal-mass white-dwarf collisions. The model tracks remain inconsistent with the observed distribution, and for asymmetric models the transverse viewing-angle variation adds to the tension.

papers.title_en: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
papers.abstract_en: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.

papers.title_en: A First-Order Gauge Approach to de Sitter General Relativity
papers.abstract_en: We propose a first-order gauge formulation of de Sitter relativity in which the pseudo-radius l(x) is promoted to a spacetime field, locally breaking SO(4,1) to SO(3,1). Here, l(x) is a geometric compensator and dl(x) the associated order parameter. This modifies the Strong Equivalence Principle: the local vacuum follows the matter distribution instead of remaining fixed, while the propagating degrees of freedom of General Relativity are unchanged. At fixed l(x), the action is SO(3,1)-gauge invariant, but varying l(x) destroys covariance under the full translational sector of SO(4,1). Through the Inonu-Wigner contraction, abstract generators become explicit spacetime transformations, yielding nonlinear Killing vectors in both the macroscopic l tends to infinity and microscopic l tends to 0 limits. The generalized Noether theorem gives a unified energy-momentum current coupling the standard tensor to the proper conformal matter current. It vanishes identically without matter, causing the asymptotic extinction of local vacuum energy and the decay of the background to Minkowski spacetime. Independent variations yield the coupled de Sitter field equations, and we algebraically prove their equivalence to the tensorial splitting on the coordinate manifold. Gauge Bianchi identities further show that Lambda(x) is an intrinsic source of spacetime torsion, consistently identifying it with the local order parameter of the symmetry breaking. The cosmological constant problem is therefore recast, not numerically solved: deriving the decay of Lambda(x) from early-universe densities to its observed value remains future work.

papers.title_en: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
papers.abstract_en: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.

papers.title_en: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NISP spectroscopy of gravitational arcs and multiple images
papers.abstract_en: Applications of strong gravitational lensing in astrophysics and cosmology critically depend on building reliable strong lensing models, which require accurate measurements of on-sky positions of multiple images and of the redshifts of the background sources from which they originate. In this context, Euclid is a unique facility, as it simultaneously provides high-resolution multi-band photometric imaging and slitless spectroscopy for an unprecedentedly large sample of gravitational lenses, most of which are newly discovered. In this work, we exploit Euclid slitless spectroscopic data to determine the redshifts of four spatially extended lensed sources, and to reconstruct emission-line images. Specifically, two of the target sources are lensed into giant arcs by the massive galaxy clusters SPT-CLJ0411$-$4819 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.424$, where "d" denotes the lensing deflector) and Abell 2280 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.326$). The third system is a quadruply imaged active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidate strongly lensed by a massive galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.68$, while the fourth is a galaxy-scale Einstein ring produced by a lens galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.235$. This work represents a proof of concept for the exploitation of Euclid slitless spectroscopic data in the study of strong gravitational lensing, providing one of the first determinations of spectroscopic redshifts for strongly lensed features from NISP spectra. These results demonstrate the feasibility of applying the same methodology to the very large sample of gravitational lenses that Euclid has started to discover and is expected to identify over the course of the mission.

papers.title_en: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): VIS processing and data products
papers.abstract_en: This paper describes the characteristics of the Euclid visible imager (VIS) data delivered as part of the Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). This data set contains 42092 calibrated frames. Validated nominal exposures cover 2092 deg$^2$ of sky. We outline the minor changes made to the VIS processing function (PF) since previous releases. For the wide survey, the photometric and astrometric accuracy of the reference stellar sample $(18.5 < I_{\rm E} < 19.8)$ is excellent. The internal and external astrometric dispersions are 0.08 and 0.18 mas, respectively, at the quadrant level, and 3.4 and 5.6 mas at the source level. The corresponding internal and external photometric dispersions are 0.76 and 1.4 mmag at the quadrant level, and 11 and 25 mmag at the source level. We characterise remaining astrometric and photometric systematic effects: focal-plane-dependent variations; time-dependent photometric offsets; and colour-dependent centroid shifts. The noise floor in the deepest VIS images appears to be set by the extended diffuse light of faint galaxies. Globally, the DR1 VIS data meet pre-launch mission requirements and the 42092 images it contains provide our first substantial look at the sky as seen by VIS.

papers.title_en: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk
papers.abstract_en: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.

papers.title_en: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) C: Lens modelling pipeline overview
papers.abstract_en: Galaxy-scale strong lenses provide precise measurements of galaxy mass distributions, magnified views of distant galaxies, and a competitive cosmological probe. Historically, such studies have been limited to hundreds of lenses, with automated modelling methods proving difficult to scale. We present automated lens modelling of 15 072 strong-lens candidates from Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), over an order of magnitude larger than any previously modelled sample. Using PyAutoLens-JAX, we perform three fits with multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE), pixelised, and Sérsic representations of the source, adopting an isothermal ellipsoid mass model with external shear. These fits provide foreground lens-light subtraction, adaptive Delaunay source reconstructions, and deblended photometry. More than 20 expert inspectors visually assess the resulting models, and each model is assigned the classification on which at least 75% of its inspectors agree. Of the 6073 grade A (secure) lens candidates, inspectors classify 4098 (67.5%) as successfully modelled, 580 (9.6%) as failures, 317 (5.2%) as multi-galaxy lenses, 15 (0.2%) as double-source-plane lenses, and 7 (0.1%) as unsure if lens, while 1032 (17.0%) reach no consensus and 24 (0.4%) have incomplete models. For the 8999 grade B (probable) candidates, the modelling success rate falls to 43.1%, primarily reflecting an increase in cases without consensus (37.6%), rather than a comparable increase in agreed failures (12.9%). Successfully modelled grade A and B systems have a median effective Einstein radius of 0.85 arcsec and a median total $I_E$-band source magnification of 8.1. We publicly release the successful lens models, their inferred properties, and magnified-source reconstructions through the ECLIPSE catalogue, demonstrating automated modelling at Euclid sample sizes and enabling population-level strong-lensing science.

papers.title_en: Subsystem Flow: Quantum Error Correction, Petz Recovery, and Ergodic Inclusions
papers.abstract_en: In quantum error correction (QEC), the goal is to engineer an encoding that protects logical information against the erasure of a physical subsystem. In local many-body quantum systems, by contrast, nature provides a subsystem inclusion $\mN\subset \mM$ in a fixed reference state $\ketΩ$. Asking whether the inclusion admits a reference-preserving code that protects subsystem $\mN$ against erasure of the complement is equivalent to asking whether $\mN$ is preserved under the modular dynamics of $\mM$ in this state (modular autonomy). We define the subsystem flow, which measures the departure from this error correction regime. Away from autonomy, the infinitesimal flow quantifies relative-entropy loss, while the history algebra and persistent core describe which observables the modular orbit generates and retains. We call an inclusion ergodic when modular orbits generate everything and retain nothing. Analytic continuation of subsystem flow yields Petz recovery maps and a family of positive inclusion parent Hamiltonians. We show that, in general, evolving with these parent Hamiltonians allows $\mN$ to leave $\mM$, and in some cases, it can generate the entire $\mM\vee\mM'$. Inclusions with a common cyclic and separating vector generate everything, and standard inclusions of factors, such as those of nested subregions in QFT, are ergodic. Moreover, the $L^2$-nuclearity property implies that the spectrum of parent Hamiltonians is discrete. We define a dissipative semigroup by repeating the Petz recovery map, whose fixed-point algebra is the modular persistent core and whose spectrum is gapped under the assumption of $L^2$-nuclearity. We conjecture that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of inclusion parent Hamiltonians can be used to define local spectral measures of quantum chaos.

papers.title_en: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
papers.abstract_en: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.

papers.title_en: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) A: Strong lens catalogue overview
papers.abstract_en: We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.

papers.title_en: Measuring the growth index in the $w_0w_a$CDM background
papers.abstract_en: We produce a measurement of the growth index, $γ$, which is used to parametrize the scale-independent growth of linear matter perturbations on sub-horizon scales, for the $w_0w_a$CDM background model. In 2023, assuming the $Λ$CDM background, the value $γ=0.633^{+0.025}_{-0.024}$ was obtained, excluding the General Relativity value of $γ=0.55$ at $3.7σ$ statistical significance. In 2025, an analysis of baryon acoustic oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopy Instrument (DESI) demonstrated a preference for a dynamical dark energy over the cosmological constant model, $Λ$, ranging from $2.8-4.2σ$, depending on the external datasets used. Therefore it is important to determine how the $γ$ measurement is modified in the context of dynamical dark energy and verify whether the tension with the expected theoretical value persists. Considering data from Planck cosmic microwave background anisotropies, $fσ_{8}$, baryon acoustic oscillation from DESI and supernova Ia luminosity distances from Phanteon+, we find $γ_{w_0w_a}=0.633\pm0.024$, essentially the same value found for the $Λ$CDM background. This result excludes the General Relativity value for the $w_0w_a$CDM background evolution at $3.4σ$ level. We also show that the $γ$ posteriors across many datasets combinations are consistent with each other and that main driver of the "$γ$ tension" is the $fσ_{8}$ dataset.

papers.title_en: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
papers.abstract_en: Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 πf(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.

papers.title_en: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) D: Photometric redshifts and the first census of strong lenses in the galaxy evolution framework
papers.abstract_en: The Euclid mission is revolutionising the study of strong gravitational lenses by providing high-resolution imaging over an unprecedented survey area, increasing the number of known lenses by two orders of magnitude compared to previous surveys. Characterising this sample of lens-galaxies requires accurate measurements of their physical properties. However, standard catalogue photometry often blends the light from the foreground lens and the lensed background source, limiting the reliability of derived galaxy parameters. We present a homogeneous catalogue of photometric redshifts and physical properties for 9538 galaxy-scale strong lenses identified in Euclid's DR1 strong-lens sample. We use deblended multiwavelength photometry obtained from the lens modelling of Euclid and ground-based images with PyAutoLens. The photometric redshifts of the lens galaxies are estimated using the template-fitting code Phosphoros. The stellar masses, SFRs, stellar ages, and metallicities are inferred through SED fitting with Prospector, adopting a flexible non-parametric SFH and a Salpeter IMF. The robustness of the inferred parameters is assessed through comparisons with spectroscopic redshifts and external galaxy surveys. The sample of lenses spans a broad redshift range of $0.13\lesssim z_{\rm phot} \lesssim 1.98$, with a median $z_{\rm phot} = 0.68^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$. The sample is dominated by massive quiescent galaxies with a $M_\ast$ range $[10^{10},\,10^{12.1}]\,M_\odot$ and a median $\log_{10}(M_\ast/M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$. This catalogue represents one of the first large-scale characterisations of strong-lens galaxies in the Euclid era. By combining deblended photometry with homogeneous photometric redshift and SED-fitting analyses, it provides a foundation for studies of galaxy evolution, lens-galaxy scaling relations, and the connection between stellar and total mass in strong lenses.

papers.title_en: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.

papers.title_en: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
papers.abstract_en: We present the discovery of new secondary delayed radio flares from two tidal disruption events (TDEs), AT2019ehz and AT2019eve from observations ranging 1-18 GHz using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. For AT2019ehz, we find a secondary flare in radio emission began at 1545 days post-disruption, 770 days after the first radio flare detected at 775 days post-disruption, and for AT2019eve the secondary flare was detected at 1594 days post-disruption, 825 days after its initial radio detection at 769 days post-disruption. Through spectral modeling of the multi-frequency observations, we extract physical parameters of the new flares to constrain the origin of the rebrightening. We find the secondary flare of AT2019ehz is likely produced by a second outflow launched at roughly 1000 days. For AT2019eve, the secondary flare reveals unexpected spectral evolution with a self-absorbed peak increasing from 1325 to 2173 days post-disruption, which is not well explained with most models of expanding outflows and instead suggests a more complex physical geometry. This inconclusive origin of AT2019eve highlights the need for more complex models to explain observed TDE radio evolution.

papers.title_en: Dual-species atom interferometry for axion dark matter
papers.abstract_en: Atom interferometers are sensitive to oscillations of the masses and transition frequencies of atoms, which can be induced by axion dark matter. The main limitation is the sensitivity to gravity gradient noise (GGN). We propose a dual-species atom interferometry sequence that provides a suppression of GGN by up to three orders of magnitude and a sensitivity enhancement via the mass difference of the two atoms. We show that, under realistic experimental assumptions, a 10m-baseline dual-species atom interferometer is more sensitive to the axion gluon coupling than a 100m single-species gradiometer. Including a comprehensive noise analysis, we demonstrate that the Very Long Baseline Atom Interferometer (VLBAI) in Hannover with a baseline of 10m can probe the axion decay constant at levels almost competitive with leading laboratory constraints. The proposed 100m-baseline Atom Interferometer CERN Experiment (AICE) can extend this sensitivity by up to two orders of magnitude, surpassing laboratory constraints for axion masses of $10^{-19}\;\text{eV}/c^2 \lesssim m_a \lesssim 3\times10^{-15}\;\text{eV}/c^2$.

papers.title_en: Scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia: do they bind?
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the existence of molecular two-glueball bound states, so-called glueballonia, in pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory. We mainly concentrate on the scalar and pseudoscalar channels, thus studying scalar-scalar and scalar-pseudoscalar bound states, respectively. Near the onset of binding, when a bound state first appears just below threshold, a nonrelativistic framework is justified. We employ an attractive scalar-exchange Yukawa potential together with a smeared contact term contribution and determine the critical attraction required for binding. For two scalar glueballs, we use the scalar dilaton effective theory to determine the parameters of the non-relativistic potential: the Yukawa interaction is generated by t- and u-channels involving the exchange of one scalar glueball, while the repulsion emerges by the s-channel annihilation and contact interaction. Using lattice-YM input to fix the dilaton parameters, we find that the attraction is strong enough: the scalar glueballonium binds, and the result is quite robust with respect to parameter variations. In a minimal scalar-pseudoscalar extension, the Yukawa attraction is again given by the t-channel scalar glueball, while the crossed u-channel pseudoscalar exchange induces an attractive local contribution, making the pseudoscalar glueballonium also bind in pure gauge. Importantly, both the scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia are stable in the YM vacuum. Next, we briefly comment on the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar, scalar-tensor, and tensor-tensor channels: all these channels are attractive too and could form bound states, which, however, would be unstable in pure YM due to decay into two lighter glueballs. Finally, as a cross-check, our formalism confirms that Higgs-Higgs bound state does not form.

papers.title_en: Band geometry, Anderson's theorem, and vortex nucleation in unconventional 2D superconductors
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by the recent discovery of chiral superconductors in 2d materials, we study the effects of disorder on superconductivity in materials with non-trivial band geometry. First, we show how Anderson's theorem and the conventional Abrikosov-Gorkov description of disorder-induced pair breaking are modified by the structure of the normal-state Bloch functions. We apply these results to twisted MoTe2 and show that a BCS pairing mechanism for the observed superconductor is in tension with the measured normal state residual resistivity. Second, we study whether random potential disorder can nucleate superconducting vortices in a chiral time- reversal-breaking superconductor. We show that, for a superconductor stabilized by the usual BCS mechanism, weak disorder does not induce a vortex glass phase, in contrast to superconductivity formed from an anyon fluid.

papers.title_en: Cosmological Dressing Rules for Massive Scalars
papers.abstract_en: The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation of de Sitter correlation functions comes in different guises including harmonic analysis and dressed flat space correlators. We observe that these are equivalent spectral representations of the same Sturm-Liouville problem. Starting from the latter we derive dressing rules for scalar fields of arbitrary mass with auxiliary propagators in the form of Euler integrals that are accessible to flat space diagrammatic tools.

papers.title_en: Cosmological correlators and kinematic flow on complex Hartle-Hawking saddles
papers.abstract_en: The Lorentzian gravitational path integral over homogeneous and isotropic metrics in a closed universe with positive cosmological constant is dominated by complex saddle points, such as the Hartle-Hawking saddles. We ask how to compute cosmological correlators on such complex backgrounds, and how they respond to the shifts of the kinematic variables---the kinematic flow---without tracking the bulk time evolution explicitly. We, specifically, study a conformally coupled scalar test field with a cubic interaction around these saddles. We find that the wave function coefficients can be written as discrete spectral sums with the summands containing the corresponding coefficients in the Einstein static universe, which are obtainable in analogy with the polytopes program for flat spacetime. Whereas the wave function coefficients of the flat FLRW case are given by integrals over shifted kinematics, the discrete spectrum on the three-sphere for Hartle-Hawking saddles produces sums. We identify the coefficients, which depend on the final hypersurface through a phase fixed by its size, with Srivastava-Daoust multi-variable hypergeometric functions. They satisfy recursion relations for any number of sites, under which the sums collapse into rational functions. For the one- and two-site Feynman-Witten tree diagrams, we derive difference equations in the kinematic variables which close on a finite set of sums, giving a discrete kinematic flow. The transformation matrices are upper triangular with rational elements, and satisfy a consistency condition which makes the flow path independent. We then obtain the two-, three- and four-point cosmological correlators. At the late-time conformal boundary, we derive an explicit difference equation for the four-point function.

papers.title_en: Toward the minimal set of states in axion superradiance
papers.abstract_en: Observational searches for black hole superradiance require predicting the growth and evolution of quasi-bound states on astrophysical timescales. For axions (and most light spin-0 particles), self-interactions efficiently redistribute energy and angular momentum from the fastest-growing superradiant states into higher-order, more weakly bound states, and do so on short timescales. This has made it difficult to compute even the most mundane of observables across large regions of parameter space. In this work we extend the study of self-interacting systems, following the evolution of nearly 300 coupled quasi-bound states. We evolve a $10\,M_\odot$ black hole over a Salpeter timescale, and $10^4$ and $10^8\,M_\odot$ black holes over a Gyr, identifying for each axion mass the minimal set of states required to describe the evolution of the black hole and the shape of the superradiant cloud. In most cases the evolution converges as increasingly weakly bound states are added; we identify no less than 203 distinct quasi-bound states that play a role in establishing this convergence. In small regions of parameter space, however, we find no converged solution, and show that broad resonant features and nearly degenerate scattering rates redistribute mass to bound states with principal quantum numbers $n \gtrsim 45$. We further show that the cloud can extend to radii orders of magnitude larger than usually assumed, that gravitational-wave level transitions can prevent the growth of superradiant states, and that both the gravitational-wave spectrum and the interaction with the environment are far richer than previously appreciated.

papers.title_en: Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
papers.abstract_en: Frequency-dependent radio time delays have been measured in Sgr A* light curves, with higher-frequency emission generally leading lower-frequency emission. These lags have been interpreted in terms of an organized jet-like outflow, expanding plasma components, or magnetic-flux eruptions, although their origin and recurrence remain uncertain. We aim to search for and quantify frequency-dependent radio time delays in a new high-cadence Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observation of Sgr A*. Using the improved broad 12-37 GHz frequency coverage, we measured the timing of the dominant variability feature and compared the resulting lag-wavelength slope with previous measurements. Sgr A* was observed with the VLA on 28 May 2022 in the Ku, K, and Ka bands over a 6-hour track. We extracted both band-averaged and 2 GHz subband light curves and measured the delays using a peak-time method and a locally normalized cross-correlation function. The light curves show one broad variability feature, with the maximum occurring progressively later at lower observing frequencies. Both timing methods recover a positive lag-wavelength relation, with a slope of order 40 min/cm. This value agrees with time lag results reported over more than 15 years from the first VLA observations at 22-43 GHz to later multifrequency VLA and ALMA campaigns. The sign and magnitude of the estimated delay are consistent with outward propagation through an optically thick synchrotron-emitting region. The recurrence of comparable delays over almost two decades suggests that frequency-dependent radio lags are a persistent feature of Sgr A* variability. Broadband, multi-epoch VLA monitoring of Sgr A* provides a useful probe of its radio variability, but robust lag measurements require high cadence and improved (u,v) coverage of both Sgr A* and the surrounding extended emission such as by combining different VLA configurations.

papers.title_en: $α'^2$-corrections to the bosonic string from an action-level double copy map
papers.abstract_en: The low-energy effective action of the bosonic string contains higher-derivative corrections of the form Riem$^2$ and Riem$^3$ to the Einstein--Hilbert action, together with the associated Kalb--Ramond couplings. We construct an action-level double copy description of these corrections up to cubic order in the fields. Two ingredients are required: a higher-derivative gauge-theory Lagrangian, which up to field redefinitions is controlled by a single $F^3$ coupling, and a deformation of the color-to-kinematics replacement of the structure constants by the corresponding three-momentum tensor. We show that no higher-derivative gauge-theory operator can produce the Riem$^3$ vertex with the standard replacement rule, and that the matching conditions for the gauge-theory coupling and the deformation of the map admit a unique solution, a double root, which renders the cubic action left--right symmetric, of the form $(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)\otimes(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)$. Without further input, the resulting map reproduces the cubic $\mathrm{Riem}\,H^2$ coupling of the bosonic string at order $α'$, the absence of six-derivative cubic Kalb--Ramond couplings at order $α'^2$, and the absence of interactions odd in the Kalb--Ramond field. The comparison is performed in transverse-traceless gauge, up to field redefinitions.

papers.title_en: Non-Bloch Topology of Frustrated Non-Hermitian Flat Bands
papers.abstract_en: Frustrated lattices with exactly flat bands and compact localized states provide an ideal setting to uncover the topology of flat bands, leading to intriguing physics in two dimensions. Extending from Hermitian to non-Hermitian systems, however, band structures are drastically changed by the non-Hermitian skin effect, which is less well understood beyond one dimension. Here, we construct a broad class of two-dimensional frustrated non-Hermitian lattice models with exactly flat bands which can be naturally described in a non-Bloch band theory. Using non-Hermitian breathing Kagome and checkerboard models as illustrations, we reveal how flat bands acquire a basis-independent skin effect induced by the other bands; in the breathing Kagome model it appears exactly when the flat band enters the area spanned by the periodic-boundary spectra of the dispersive bands. A flat band becomes singular when its eigenvectors hold immovable discontinuities at band crossings. Such singularity in non-Hermitian systems is sensitive to boundary conditions and unprotected by band flatness. Non-Bloch topology underlying is uncovered in a bulk-boundary correspondence with the formation of a singular band touching in the bulk and a robust flat band skin mode on the boundary. We present a geometric approach to construct this boundary skin mode from a macroscopic sum of compact localized skin modes and trace its topological origin to two linearly independent noncontractible loop states on a non-Bloch torus. To characterize the correspondence, an invariant is proposed based on biorthogonal polarization of the zero-energy corner mode. Breaking exact flatness, we further realize nearly flat non-Bloch Chern bands.

papers.title_en: Cosmological Signals from Finite-Lifetime Domain Wall Networks
papers.abstract_en: We study cosmological perturbations sourced by metastable domain wall (DW) networks. Using the unconnected segment model, we derive analytic expressions for the scalar and tensor power spectra in the long-wavelength regime, finding a fixed ratio between their amplitudes during the scaling regime. These spectra grow as the network evolves, driven by the increasing correlation length and slower redshifting of the wall energy density relative to radiation, and peak at a scale set by the network's collapse time. Comparing the scalar spectrum with observational constraints, we derive bounds on the DW energy density at collapse, which we apply to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and axion models. When these bounds are saturated, the resulting CMB $B$-mode signal can be comparable to or larger than the inflationary signal for a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.03$, potentially bringing it within reach of future CMB polarization experiments.

papers.title_en: The Dark Side of the Periodic Table: Theory and Signatures of Nuclear Atomic Dark Matter
papers.abstract_en: We study the theory and signatures of a Mirror Twin Higgs (MTH) scenario in which stable twin neutrons constitute most of the dark matter (DM), while a subdominant component of twin elements survives as nuclear atomic dark matter (naDM). This framework offers a solution to the $matter~coincidence~problem$ ($Ω_{\rm DM}\simeq5Ω_b$), as the twin $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry can correlate the visible and DM mass scales and their number densities. We analyze twin nucleon freeze-out and the onset of twin Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) to estimate the total naDM abundance, and determine which elements in the dark periodic table could be populated. An appreciable but subdominant naDM component generally requires a fractional nucleon mass splitting near the percent level, with twin-BBN creating heavy elements up to twin carbon. Strong twin neutron-proton scattering allows nearly all of the dark matter, not only the atomic sub-component, to participate in $dark~acoustic~oscillations$ (DAO) at early times, giving rise to a characteristic two-stage DAO signature that may be detected with future cosmological probes. Interactions between the twin and visible sectors, including the irreducible Higgs portal, make this scenario a well-motivated target for future directional direct-detection searches, and the naDM sub-component is expected to exhibit highly exotic astrophysics. We outline a supersymmetric twin Froggatt-Nielsen realization in which spontaneous $\mathbb{Z}_2$ breaking in the flavon sector can generate the required fermion spectrum and Higgs potential.

papers.title_en: Crystalline Equivalence Principle for Anomalies
papers.abstract_en: We develop a microscopic characterization of crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems in (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions with a combination of crystalline and finite unitary internal symmetry. We construct anomaly indices of symmetry operators and derive their cocycle conditions and coboundary ambiguities. For generalized crystalline symmetries combining permutations of onsite Hilbert spaces with quantum cellular automata, anomaly indices take values in $H^3(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ and $H^4(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ respectively, where $\widetilde Γ$ is the total group of crystalline and internal symmetries, and the coefficient twist $r$ accounts for spatial orientation reversal. When crystalline symmetries act solely by permuting onsite Hilbert spaces, the anomaly classes restrict trivially to the spatial subgroup. These results establish a crystalline equivalence principle for bosonic anomalies at the microscopic level, without assuming a continuum description or emergent Lorentz invariance. We prove that a nontrivial total anomaly index obstructs any symmetric invertible phase. The framework incorporates modulated symmetries where spatial symmetries permute internal symmetries. Our results reproduce LSM and SPT--LSM constraints, with the latter illustrating how spectral-sequence differentials can trivialize candidate LSM anomaly indices.

papers.title_en: Cosmic Ray Heating of the Early IGM: Realistic Galaxy Populations, Reduced Efficiency, and 21-cm Signatures
papers.abstract_en: Cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated by the first supernovae could heat the intergalactic medium (IGM) before reionization. Previous 21-cm simulations, assuming a kinetic-energy power-law spectrum and simplified galaxy populations, found that CR heating can rival X-ray heating from high-mass X-ray binaries, imprint a distinct signature on the 21-cm power spectrum, and flatten the absorption trough of the global 21-cm signal. Here we model CR heating in 21cmFAST with: (i) the momentum power-law spectrum predicted by diffusive shock acceleration; (ii) Coulomb losses off free electrons; and (iii) injection from data-informed populations of atomic-cooling and molecularly cooled galaxies. We find that CR heating is about an order of magnitude weaker than previously estimated because a momentum power law places little energy in the sub-relativistic protons ($\lesssim 40$ MeV) that supply 99% of the heat. For our fiducial spectral slope, at the hard end of those inferred for Galactic supernova remnants, and for matched efficiency, this reduces the heating by a factor of $\approx 12$, and together with a more realistic galaxy model, by a factor of $\approx 28$ at $z = 15$. At the efficiencies that supernovae can supply, CR heating is weaker than standard X-ray heating, and the global signal alone cannot tell the two apart. Distinguishing CR from X-ray heating with the 21-cm power spectrum requires CR efficiencies a few times higher than those expected from local observations. At such efficiencies, CR heating yields up to $\approx 55\%$ more power than X-ray heating at matched global signal (median over scales), compared with only 3-6% at a locally motivated efficiency. A flattened absorption trough, like the one claimed by EDGES, requires efficiencies over two orders of magnitude above the local ones, beyond plausible Population III supernova budgets.

papers.title_en: Swing Surfaces in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract_en: We study holographic entanglement entropy in the flat limit of AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, and clarify the relation between Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces and the swing surfaces proposed for flat-space holography. We show that the ordinary RT formula does not admit a well-defined flat-space limit and connect this to subtleties of the state-operator map in the flat limit. We then construct an AdS$_3$ uplift of the swing prescription and develop its corresponding information-theoretic interpretation through two complementary approaches. First, we show that the swing surface length computes the mutual information between suitably chosen nearly null boundary intervals in a special class of pure CFT states. The gravity interpretation of this result involves scattering processes which take place deep inside of the AdS$_3$ bulk. Second, we reduce the problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation for swing surfaces to the more general problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation of black hole inner horizons in holography.

papers.title_en: Einstein Reconstruction Scheme: Metric Reconstruction by Direct Inversion of the Einstein Operator
papers.abstract_en: We propose a metric reconstruction scheme that computes the metric directly from the linearized Einstein equations for noncompact sources. Working in a traceful radiation gauge, we hierarchically solve four Einstein transport equations, with the remaining six enforced by suitable homogeneous data. Unlike previous Newman-Penrose approaches, we show how the homogeneous data are fixed, thereby closing the full set of Einstein equations. We conclude by relating our scheme to existing sourced reconstruction methods, thus establishing a connection between the Newman-Penrose and Hertz-potential approaches.

papers.title_en: Learning Quantum Hamiltonians from the Dynamical Structure Factor
papers.abstract_en: Identifying the microscopic interactions governing a quantum system is essential for developing predictive theories of materials and validating quantum technologies. Despite considerable progress, learning Hamiltonians from realistic experimental data remains a challenge. Motivated by neutron scattering and quantum simulations, we study the problem of learning a quantum Hamiltonian from the dynamical structure factor (DSF), which captures two-point correlation data in quantum magnets. We show that the DSF encodes sufficient information to efficiently reconstruct broad classes of quantum Hamiltonians. Our approach exploits simple relations between low-order spectral moments of the DSF and microscopic couplings, giving rise to three complementary Hamiltonian tomography protocols based on the high-temperature expansion, strong-field polarization, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, respectively. The framework we introduce establishes practical and robust Hamiltonian learning from common experimental data, with potentially immediate application to neutron scattering experiments.

papers.title_en: Universal Theory of Strange and Bad Metals from Spatially Random Interactions with Underdamped Quantum-Critical Bosons
papers.abstract_en: One of the most important challenges in condensed matter physics is understanding the macroscopic properties of strange metals, particularly why their resistivity remains linear in temperature over several decades. We propose that a (2+1)d theory of fermions coupled to underdamped quantum-critical bosons through a spatially disordered interaction provides this long-sought-after theoretical explanation. The key novelty of our work is to establish the appropriate separation of scales so that the bosons are underdamped. Using this framework, we obtain two distinct forms for the fermionic self-energy: a conformal-limit solution, $Σ\sim\sqrtω$, and a marginal Fermi-liquid solution, $Σ\simω\log(1/ω)$, corresponding to regimes above and below the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit, respectively. These solutions produce Planckian scattering, exhibit exact $T$-linear resistivity, $ω/T$ scaling in the optical conductivity, as well as $\sim T\log(1/T)$ heat capacity at low temperatures. Moreover, our theory naturally unifies strange- and bad-metal phenomena within a single framework, suggesting that we are now approaching a new epoch in understanding the physics of strongly correlated matter.

papers.title_en: Exploring a Correlation Between AGN Black Hole Mass and X-ray Luminosity
papers.abstract_en: The traditional method to measure Type-1 Active Galactic Nuclei central black hole masses ($M_{BH}$) is the reverberation mapping (RM) technique. Motivated by the desire to find a less observationally expensive method (than RM) to estimate $M_{BH}$, we have explored a purported correlation between X-ray luminosity and $M_{BH}$. For this we have compiled a sample of 35 AGN with RM $M_{BH}$ estimates that were detected in the eROSITA All-Sky Survey public data release. Using a sample that is larger than that of J. A. Mayers et al. 2018 and has a cleaner selection function, we confirm their XMM-Newton based result of a positive correlation. However, the scatter on the scaling relation remains too high ($σ_\mathrm{int}=0.50^{+0.08}_{-0.06}$) to make this a practical method to predict $M_{BH}$ for a given X-ray detected Type-1 AGN. That said, our findings can be used to improve mock X-ray skies generated from large volume hydrodynamical cosmological simulations. Such mocks are a necessary ingredient for cluster cosmology and preparation for future missions such as NewAthena.

papers.title_en: Potts Order Preempts Emergence of 2-Form U(1) Spin Liquidity in Three-Dimensional Spin Vorticity Models
papers.abstract_en: Three-dimensional (3D) spin vorticity models (SVMs) have been proposed to realize an exotic 2-form U(1) classical spin liquid (CSL), characterized by a zero-curl constraint, string excitations, and deconfined fluctuating membranes. A previous numerical study [PRB 111, 064417 (2025)] uncovered a puzzle in the pyrochlore lattice SVM: despite exhibiting pinch points characteristic of a U(1) spin liquid, it also develops weak all-in--all-out (AIAO) order. Here, we show that the emergence of the 2-form CSL in 3D SVMs is preempted by an intrinsic instability towards entropy-driven height locking. We establish this by resolving the ground state constraints using a height mapping, which we further relate to a 3-state Potts antiferromagnet. This identifies the pyrochlore's weak AIAO order as permutationally symmetric sublattice (PSS) order, albeit with an exceptionally weak locking strength. We extend the SVM to lattices of corner-sharing octahedra and cubes, where we identify the alternative broken-sublattice-symmetry (BSS) order, a hidden order without magnetic Bragg peaks coexisting with collective paramagnetism. All three models undergo a 3D Ising transition consistent with a symmetry-allowed locking potential in the coarse-grained height theory. The spin liquid persists over intermediate length and temperature scales, but a critical Coulomb ground state ensemble fails to materialize, its correlations cut off by the finite locking length. These findings illustrate how microscopic constraints can determine the ultimate stability of emergent gauge theories in frustrated spin systems.

papers.title_en: Improved constraints on axion inflation with the new code AxioGen: an efficient generator of curvature perturbations
papers.abstract_en: Axion inflation, in which a pseudoscalar inflaton couples to a $U(1)$ gauge field via a Chern-Simons interaction, has garnered significant interest due to its rich phenomenology. The power spectrum and bispectrum for this model are often parametrized by functions known as $f_2$ and $f_3$, respectively. Previous work computed $f_2$ and $f_3$ using an approximation for the gauge field mode functions. While these approximate solutions are fairly accurate ($\mathcal{O}(10\%)$) for large values of the model parameter $ξ$, which controls gauge field particle production, our recent work has shown them to be quite inaccurate for smaller values of $ξ$. We present new fitting functions for $f_2$ and $f_3$ that are significantly more accurate than those previously used. We use these functions to place new constraints on $ξ$ and also set lower bounds for the energy scale of the axion gauge field coupling for $φ^{1/3}$ and $φ^{2/3}$ inflationary potentials. Additionally, we present a new public code to efficiently generate realizations of the primordial curvature perturbation for axion inflation in the weak backreaction regime. This code enables numerical computation of higher order correlators and provides a novel path to initial conditions for large-scale structure formation.

papers.title_en: The Incidence of Large Ionized Bubbles at Redshift 13
papers.abstract_en: Ionized bubbles around the first galaxies connect early galaxy growth, ionizing photon escape, intergalactic-medium topology, Ly$α$ visibility, 21~cm structure, and reionization timing. We model the incidence of galaxy-driven ionized bubbles at $z\approx 13$ using JWST UV luminosity functions, taking the Ly$α$ source reported by Witstok et al. as a benchmark for the relevant scale. We quantify regions with comoving radius $R\ge 2.5$~cMpc through their sky surface density $Σ_{\ge 2.5}$. For our continuously active fiducial case, using the Donnan et al. UVLF with $f_{\mathrm{esc}}=0.2$, $\logξ_{\mathrm{ion}}=25.5$, $f_{\mathrm{active}}=1$, and $C=3$, we find $Σ_{\ge 2.5}\simeq 8.10\times 10^{-3}$ arcmin$^{-2}$ per $Δz=1$. For $f_{\rm active}=0.2$ or $f_{\rm time}=0.2$ with 10~Myr mean on-times, the incidence falls by factors of 4.1 and 2.9, respectively; longer correlated episodes strengthen the tail. Merging overlapping spheres raises the fiducial incidence by $9.5\%$. The simulations show that Witstok-sized regions can arise in UVLF-calibrated galaxy-driven models. This is a population-level statement, and the specific Witstok source may still require unusual effective ionizing efficiency, recent fading or burstiness, or a non-stellar ionizing contribution.

papers.title_en: Isolated Critical Points for Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications of M-theory
papers.abstract_en: We consider Scherk-Schwarz compactifications of M-theory (toroidal compactifications with a non-trivial spin structure) in various dimensions and find isolated critical points of the potential on the moduli space. We demonstrate this by identifying the unbroken duality group and finding isolated points on the moduli spaces which are fixed by elements of the unbroken duality group. We work out concrete examples involving compactifications down to $d=8,6, 5$ and $4$ spacetime dimensions. We also conjecture a duality covariant anomaly cancellation condition for M-theory on $T^n$ orbifolded by discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ symmetries acting as phases on the charge lattice. This anomaly cancellation condition generalizes the level matching requirement for perturbative string orbifolds.

papers.title_en: The three-loop QCD helicity amplitudes for $V$+jet production at hadron colliders in full color
papers.abstract_en: We compute the three-loop Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) corrections to the production of a vector boson $V=Z,W^\pm,γ^*$ and a jet in quark-antiquark annihilation and its kinematic crossings, retaining full dependence on the number of colors. By expressing the infrared-finite remainders in terms of a small set of rational and special functions, we find that the amplitudes live in a strongly restricted function space, compared to the full space of the related Feynman integrals. We provide fast and reliable evaluation in all kinematic regions using numerical transport.

papers.title_en: Improved delensing of CMB $B$-modes with upcoming SO and LSST Year-1 mock dataset: Impact of photometric redshift errors
papers.abstract_en: In the era of high-precision Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropy measurements, detection of primordial gravitational waves (PGWs) is one of the main goals of current CMB experiments. Detection of a divergence-free ($B$-mode) component in CMB polarisation will provide direct evidence of inflationary PGWs in the early universe. However, weak gravitational lensing of CMB photons due to intervening mass distribution of the Universe distorts the primordial polarisation patterns, introducing an additional lensing-induced $B$-mode signal. Removing these lensing-induced $B$-modes is essential for improving constraints on the amplitude of PGWs. In this work, we present a multi-tracer delensing analysis using simulations of the Rubin Observatory LSST galaxy catalogue and Simons Observatory (SO) CMB maps. We use realistic photometric redshift errors for LSST mock catalogue and high complexity Galactic foregrounds for CMB simulations. By adopting a tomographic multi-tracer approach that combines the CMB and LSST mock data, we achieved a 10-20% higher delensing efficiency compared with using CMB data alone. Our analysis removes approximately 60% of the lensing-induced $B$-mode power. We find that photometric redshift errors in the mock galaxy catalogue introduce biases in the inferred galaxy bias and $σ_{8,0}$ parameters. However, these uncertainties do not produce a significant systematic bias in the inferred tensor-to-scalar ratio.

papers.title_en: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
papers.abstract_en: We searched DEAP-3600 data for neutrino signals coincident with gravitational waves from compact object mergers observed by the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA collaborations (LVK). While mergers involving neutron stars are expected to produce neutrinos, these have never been detected. The DEAP-3600 experiment is sensitive to electron neutrinos as recently observed through charged current neutrino absorption on its $^{40}$Ar target. Between 2016 and 2020, the detector recorded data during seven compact merger events involving neutron stars that were observed gravitationally by LVK. Upon examination, there is no statistically significant evidence of neutrinos from any of the mergers analyzed. Exclusion limits are set on the electron neutrino fluence, e.g. from GW170817 in the mono-energetic model at $6.8\times10^{12}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$ ($1.8\times10^{10}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$) for 10 MeV (100 MeV) neutrinos.

papers.title_en: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

papers.title_en: Integrable Singularity Black Holes without Inner Horizons in Asymptotically Safe Inspired Gravity and NFW Dark Matter Effects
papers.abstract_en: We investigate an alternative ultraviolet (UV) structure for Renormalization Group improved (RG) black holes within a phenomenological framework inspired by asymptotically safe gravity. In several regular RG constructions, regularity at the origin is associated with a dS core and an additional inner horizon, raising issues of spacetime predictability and possible mass inflation instabilities. Motivated by this problem, we relate the RG scale to the radially weighted effective quantum gravitational source entering the volume integrand of the quantum corrected Ricci scalar. This prescription yields a Bessel type running Newton coupling with $G_I(r)\sim r$ in the UV, rather than the usual $G(r)\sim r^3$ behavior, and supports an integrable central singularity. The inner branch is matched through the Israel Darmois conditions to an exterior RG solution with $G_{II}\to G_0$ in the infrared, where $G_0$ is the Newton constant. Within the numerical range investigated, the resulting geometry has a single event horizon and no additional inner horizon. We then incorporate an NFW dark matter distribution coupled to the same running coupling. Since $ρ_{\rm NFW}\sim r^{-1}$ while $G_I(r)\sim r$ near the origin, the effective matter contribution entering the field equations remains finite, producing a cored effective behavior without modifying the NFW profile by hand. The gravitational decoupling algorithm keeps the quantum gravitational and dark matter sectors separately conserved within the same geometry. For the configurations considered, the NFW sector shifts the event horizon while preserving the single horizon structure. Thus, the same running coupling governs both the integrable UV black hole geometry and the softening of the central gravitational response of the NFW source.

papers.title_en: Sub-MeV gamma-ray lines from an endothermic interpretation of the LZ recoil candidate
papers.abstract_en: Endothermic upscattering of heavy dark matter offers a compelling interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil candidate recently reported by LUX-ZEPLIN, with a characteristic recoil energy $E_R \propto δ$, where $δ$ is the mass splitting between the dark matter states. Cosmological and experimental constraints motivate the depletion of the primordial heavier state, which can be regenerated in the Galactic halo. We show that, if the heavier state decays radiatively, the same mass splitting sets the energy of a gamma-ray line, $E_γ\simeq δ$. For our benchmark, this leads to a sub-MeV line within the projected reach of the Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI), scheduled for launch in 2027. The confirmation of the LUX-ZEPLIN candidate event as a dark matter signal would therefore motivate dedicated searches for sub-MeV gamma-ray lines, with COSI providing a timely opportunity to test this interpretation.

papers.title_en: How to find regular black-hole islands in the swamp
papers.abstract_en: An infinite tower of higher-curvature corrections is expected to lead to regular black-hole solutions. We assume that this regular behavior does not abruptly arise, but gradually builds up with each successive order of the effective field theory of gravity. In addition, we assume that the effective field theory comes with a single scale of singularity-resolving new physics. We translate this assumption into a monotonicity requirement for deviations of the metric functions from a Schwarzschild black hole. Under these assumptions, conditions can be formulated which trace the increase of ``less singular'' black-hole behavior on and outside of the black-hole horizon within the regime of validity of the effective field theory. These conditions constrain the effective field theory coefficients. To exemplify this construction, we motivate five specific conditions and find a corresponding island of black hole regularity conditions at order eight in the effective field theory. We also explore whether string theory as well as asymptotically safe gravity lie on this island.

papers.title_en: Probing chiral topological order of the Kitaev honeycomb on a trapped ion processor
papers.abstract_en: Kitaev's honeycomb model is a paradigmatic exactly solvable system hosting a quantum spin liquid with non-Abelian anyons and topologically protected edge modes, offering a platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, real candidate Kitaev materials invariably include complex secondary interactions that obscure the realization of spin-liquid behavior and demand novel quantum computational approaches for efficient simulation. Here we report quantum simulations of a 22-site Kitaev honeycomb lattice on a trapped-ion quantum processor, without and with non-integrable Heisenberg interactions that are present in real materials. We develop efficient quantum circuits for ground-state preparation, achieving high accuracy with energy errors equivalent to an effective temperature $\approx 0.2$ (in units of the Kitaev interactions), consistent with the experimentally relevant spin-liquid regime. Starting from these states, we apply controlled perturbations and measure time-dependent spin correlations along the system's edge. In the non-Abelian phase, we observe chiral edge dynamics consistent with a non-zero Chern number, a hallmark of chiral topological order, which vanishes upon transition to the Abelian toric code phase. Extending to the non-integrable Kitaev-Heisenberg model, we find that weak Heisenberg interactions preserve chiral edge dynamics, while stronger couplings suppress them, signaling the breakdown of topological protection. These simulations establish edge-mode dynamical simulations on quantum computers as a staple technique to understand the topological and chiral phases of matter in Hamiltonians beyond integrability.

papers.title_en: Strong Lensing Tomography: Double and pseudo multi-source plane strong gravitational lensing to constrain dark energy
papers.abstract_en: Tomographic measurements of gravitational lensing with different lens and source redshift distributions contain crucial information about the universe's relative expansion rate, and hence dark energy. While this technique is well-established in weak lensing, its application to strong lensing has traditionally focused on Double Source Plane Lenses (DSPLs). However, DSPLs are exceedingly rare and fundamentally limited by the Mass-Sheet Degeneracy (MSD), a systematic uncertainty underexplored in previous literature. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Pseudo Double-Source Plane Lenses (PDSPLs): pairs of independent single-source plane lenses with self-similar deflectors. This generalizes the DSPL formalism to the $\sim 10^5$ galaxy-galaxy lenses expected from LSST, Euclid, and Roman. Unlike true DSPLs, PDSPLs are free from the intermediate source mass problem by construction, eliminating the associated secondary MSD and the need for multi-plane ray tracing. We incorporate the deflector MSD into a hierarchical population model to forecast dark energy constraints in Flat $w_0w_a$CDM, showing that MSD severely degrades constraints from small DSPL samples and motivates our PDSPL statistical approach. Assuming unbiased Gaussian photo-z errors of $σ_z/(1+z)=0.03$, the mock LSST Y10 photometric sample yields $σ(w_0)\sim0.45$, constraining the population-mean MSD parameter and deflector power-law slope to $\sim2\%$. A prior $Ω_m\sim\mathcal{N}(0.3,0.05)$, representing combination with external cosmological probes such as CMB, BAO, or SNe Ia, improves this to $σ(w_0)\sim0.29$, comparable to Stage III weak lensing. The statistical advantage over smaller spectroscopic subsets (e.g., 4MOST) assumes unbiased photo-zs. Real-data use requires spectroscopic photo-z calibration and validation of how paired deflectors' mass-profile differences affect Einstein-radius ratios.
authors: the LSST Dark Energy Science Collaboration

papers.title_en: Harmonic superspace and Kaluza-Klein reduction
papers.abstract_en: We extend the Kaluza-Klein reduction procedure to the framework of harmonic superspace and apply it to the construction of off-shell superfield formulations of supersymmetric gauge multiplets. The reduction is implemented by a deformation of the harmonic derivatives by mass terms, while ensuring that manifest off-shell supersymmetry and Grassmann analyticity are preserved at all stages. As a first application, we reduce the free \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Maxwell theory and obtain an off-shell superfield description of the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive vector supermultiplet. The resulting formulation naturally incorporates an analytic Stückelberg-type gauge symmetry. We then reduce linearized \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Poincaré supergravity and derive the unconstrained harmonic-superspace action for the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive supergravity multiplet. The technical simplicity of the procedure stems from the structure of gauge theories in harmonic superspace, where the gauge symmetry is naturally encoded in analytic prepotentials and harmonic derivatives. The approach presented in this paper opens a direct route to gauge-invariant off-shell superfield formulations of massive higher-spin $4D,\mathcal{N}=2$ BPS multiplets. Furthermore, the resulting theories can be reformulated in $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ superspace, opening the way to gauge-invariant off-shell descriptions of $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ massive higher-spin theories.

papers.title_en: Radiative stability of species-separated Kaluza--Klein spectra in warped geometry
papers.abstract_en: Species-dependent fifth-direction lightcones, generated by scalar-gradient operators, can separate gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein (KK) scales in a warped extra dimension, as recently shown by Randall and Riojas. In this work, we study whether this separation survives quantum corrections. Quark loops can only move the gluon speed within the interval spanned by the bare speeds. Gluon exchange pulls the quark speed toward the gluon speed, with a one-loop coefficient strongly enhanced by fifth-component exchange when the gluon is the slow species. We set the size of this effect using the strong-coupling estimates for a light-gluon benchmark, where a $5.5$~TeV gluon sits below quark partners at $10.74$~TeV. Within the effective theory, the Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes then correct the quark speed at order one. That correction is several times larger than the mass ordering can absorb, so the light-gluon ordering has no perturbative protection. The reverse benchmark, with slow quarks and a heavy gluon, keeps its ordering roughly ten times more robust.

papers.title_en: Quantum and classical thermal equilibrium for probabilistic classical fields
papers.abstract_en: The time evolution of the probability distribution for classical fields can be described by the quantum formalism. For free classical fields the free quantum field theory arises as a subsystem. Different probability distributions for classical fields correspond to the classical thermal equilibrium with the Rayleigh-Jeans divergence or the quantum thermal equilibrium with the Planck spectrum. The selection of the Rayleigh-Jeans or Planck spectrum is not a question of fundamental concepts. It becomes an issue of dynamical selection once interactions are present. We compare the momentum dependence of the classical energy and field correlations for the classical and quantum equilibrium. This permits to decide which equilibrium is selected as a result of asymptotic dynamics by numerical simulations of the probabilistic classical fields including interactions. For free probabilistic classical fields we construct a general ``classical-quantum map'' between the classical probability distribution and the density matrix of the quantum field theory.

papers.title_en: Relaxation of Quantum Observables in a 4D Black Hole that forms from Collapse of a Null Shell
papers.abstract_en: The vacuum polarization and luminosity are computed in a four-dimensional spacetime where a spherically symmetric null shell contracts to form a black hole. This is done by computing the contribution of the spherically symmetric modes of a massless minimally coupled scalar field to the quantities $\la φ^2 \ra_{\rm in} - \la φ^2 \ra_U$ and $L_{\rm in} - L_U$. Here the subscript ``in'' denotes the {\it in} vacuum state for the null shell spacetime and the subscript ``U'' denotes the Unruh state in Schwarzschild spacetime. The computation is done outside the null shell and outside the event horizon where the spacetime geometry is the Schwarzschild geometry. It is found that, as expected, these differences approach zero at late times. However, they do so significantly more slowly than in the two-dimensional case where there is no scattering of the mode functions. In both cases, the difference is dominated by a quasinormal mode at intermediate times and a tail term at late times that decays quartically in time.
