For the luminosity difference, an analytic calculation verifies the late-time result for the tail term.

papers.title_en: Dressed Fock Spaces in Gauge Theory and Gravity
papers.abstract_en: Four-dimensional gauge and gravitational theories exhibit long-range interactions that require asymptotic particles to be dressed by clouds of soft photons and gravitons. Faddeev-Kulish dressings render scattering amplitudes infrared-finite, but the resulting multi-particle states do not factorise into tensor products of dressed one-particle states. We show that this loss of Fock-space factorisation is not fundamental, but reflects an inappropriate choice of infrared variables. The real soft divergence is reproduced by the Goldstone modes of asymptotic symmetries, while the Coulomb phase is reproduced by new zero modes of the radiative fields that we introduce here. In these variables, infrared-finite dressed multi-particle states admit the usual Fock-space factorisation into single-particle dressed states.

papers.title_en: Population inference of eccentric binary black holes using asymptotic constants of motion
papers.abstract_en: In standard gravitational-wave population analyses of compact binaries, source parameters are defined at a reference frequency. For quantities that evolve during the inspiral, this means constructing a population of systems at different evolutionary stages, which complicates the astrophysical interpretation of the results. The past-time infinity, or zero-frequency, limit provides a mathematically well-defined reference where all sources enter the population fit on equal footing. This approach was first proposed for spin tilts, which evolve due to spin precession but converge to constant values as binaries are back-propagated. The orbital eccentricity also evolves throughout the inspiral and approaches unity in the zero-frequency limit for all binaries, making it unsuitable as a common reference point for population analyses. On the other hand, the Newtonian orbital angular momentum is an asymptotic constant of motion of the relativistic two-body problem and remains finite in this limit. In this paper, we make use of this known asymptotic behavior to reformulate eccentric population inference in terms of orbital angular momentum rather than eccentricity and demonstrate this approach on simulated gravitational-wave data. Our work constitutes the first example of eccentric population inference using only asymptotic constants of motion. Importantly, after the inference has been performed using this consistent reference, the results can be propagated to any preferred frequency for comparison with astrophysical predictions.

papers.title_en: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
papers.abstract_en:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups, given one named hypothesis that is a theorem of that library, so that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.05.

papers.title_en: Eccentricity detectability in Extreme Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.abstract_en: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) consist of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a massive black hole and are among the primary targets for the future space-based gravitational-wave detector LISA. Their orbital eccentricity carries valuable information about their astrophysical origins, making its detection particularly important. However, increasing eccentricity has competing effects on detectability: it makes eccentric waveforms easier to distinguish from circular ones, but also redistributes signal power across multiple harmonics, reducing the power captured by single-harmonic searches. In this work, we quantify this trade-off within a semi-coherent framework for a source with fixed total SNR of $50$. Eccentricity becomes distinguishable from zero for final eccentricities $e_f \gtrsim 0.05$, while single-harmonic sensitivity declines beyond $e_f \simeq 0.1$. In noise-free analyses, including enough harmonics to recover at least $50\%$ of the total SNR avoids this degradation, but adds statistical freedom when calibrating detection thresholds. We apply the framework to two astrophysical EMRI populations, showing how these competing effects interact with their eccentricity distributions under simplified assumptions. The balance among eccentricity-driven distinguishability, harmonic power loss, and the statistical cost of additional harmonics is an important consideration for future EMRI search developments.

papers.title_en: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
papers.abstract_en: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^μ_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.

papers.title_en: AI-Assisted Extraction of Follow-up Observations from GCN Circulars in Astro-COLIBRI
papers.abstract_en: We present a new Astro-COLIBRI component that converts free-text GCN Circulars into structured, event-linked follow-up records and combines them with reports submitted directly by the community. A continuously running listener associates new Circulars with transient events, applies deterministic pre-analysis, and invokes a schema-constrained large language model to extract photometry, contacts, redshifts, and related metadata. The records are normalized into a common event-level database and exposed through the web and mobile interfaces as report summaries, contact tools, optical-afterglow context figures, and downloadable CSV or VOTable products. All 1,775 Circulars of an operational evaluation corpus covering the first half of 2026 completed the workflow without failures. An internal human audit of 210 Circulars found 223 of 231 assessed reports (96.5%) fully confirmed, each of the eight remaining ones containing at least one incorrect field, predominantly associated with observation timing and facility attribution. Extracted redshifts agree with three published compilations for 91.7 to 99.3% of the events they share, every disagreement tracing to a limit, a candidate-host estimate, or a later-refined value rather than to a misread Circular. The extraction also recovers 90 to 97% of the redshifts those compilations list for bursts it processed. Applied to the GCN archive since 2016, the pipeline yields 68,393 observations from 26,811 reports across 5,787 transient events, and now runs in real time on new Circulars. The reusable parsing and normalization pipeline is released as the open-source Python package astro-colibri-circular-parser.
papers.journal_ref: Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific 138, 114505 (2026)

papers.title_en: The Vacuum Displacement Principle: Theoretical Framework and Local Phenomenology
papers.abstract_en: We present a modified gravitational framework in which the standard Einstein field equations are sourced by a classical matter sector coupled to a Higgs-type scalar field $χ$ modeling a dynamic vacuum substrate. By introducing a phenomenological covariant coupling we implement a physical displacement principle where massive baryonic matter drives the vacuum field away from its vacuum expectation value. We show that this coupling leads to a field-dependent modulation of a particle's inertial rest mass alongside a spatial fifth force, yielding localized violations of the Einstein Equivalence Principle while preserving universal free fall for fundamental point masses. In the weak-field, non-relativistic limit, this interaction manifests as a Yukawa-type correction to the Newtonian potential. We test the viability of this framework against local gravitational constraints, including planetary perihelion precession and Eötvös parameter limits. Finally, we model the steady-state, non-relativistic spherical accretion of dust, demonstrating that the competing effects of vacuum-induced mass modulation and fifth-force acceleration yield distinct density and velocity profiles.

papers.title_en: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
papers.abstract_en: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($θ_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($τ_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $γ$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.

papers.title_en: Quasars as a self-sufficient probe of the distance duality relation
papers.abstract_en: The distance duality relation links luminosity and angular diameter distances under standard photon propagation. It is usually tested by combining distances from different probes, which requires matching their redshifts and assuming sky isotropy. Self-sufficient probes, which measure both distances for the same object, avoid the first requirement and make the second testable. We assess whether quasars can serve as such probes, combining luminosity distances from the UV--X-ray relation with angular diameter distances from spectroastrometry and reverberation mapping (SARM). As a proof-of-concept, we apply the test to the quasar Mrk~509 and find $η\equiv d_{\rm L}/[(1+z)^2d_{\rm A}] = 0.50^{+0.61}_{-0.27}$, consistent with no violation at $0.8σ$. We then forecast the number of quasars needed to detect a constant and a linearly redshift-dependent violation, motivated by the findings of Teixeira et al. (2025) with potential implications for the Hubble tension and dark energy. A constant violation, $α_0=-0.075$, equivalent to a recalibration of the SNIa distance scale, could be detected at $3σ$ with 274--840 quasars. Since SARM distances, unlike BAO, do not rely on early-time physics, this would separate an early-time origin of the Hubble tension from a SNIa miscalibration or a distance duality violation. The redshift dependence is harder to detect: 1000 quasars would exclude $η=1$ at $3.4$--$6.6σ$, but detecting the dependence itself requires $2.6\times10^4$--$8\times10^4$. GRAVITY+ could bring quasar tests of a constant violation within reach.

papers.title_en: A Holographic Model for Soft Photons and Gravitons in Four Dimensions
papers.abstract_en: We construct a two-dimensional action on the celestial sphere that describes the infrared sector of Abelian gauge and gravitational theories in four dimensions. In particular, we use the holographic model to reproduce (1) antipodal matching conditions for the superphaserotation and supertranslation Goldstone modes in four dimensions, (2) leading soft photon and graviton theorems, and (3) infrared factorization of amplitudes with generic dressed $in$ and $out$ states. Using (3), we reproduce the infrared divergences that plague the standard undressed amplitudes, and show that amplitudes involving Faddeev-Kulish dressed states are infrared finite. As a corollary, we use our holographic model to construct an infinite class of dressed states that give rise to infrared finite scattering amplitudes.

papers.title_en: Highly spinning binary black holes: promise and pitfalls for parameterized tests of general relativity
papers.abstract_en: Highly spinning binary black holes exhibit complex inspiral dynamics and offer a powerful opportunity to probe gravity in a stronger-field and more dynamical regime than non-spinning binaries. Gravitational-wave signals from such systems enable stringent parameterized tests of deviations from the source dynamics predicted by general relativity. We show that highly spinning, mass-asymmetric binaries can provide enhanced sensitivity to deviations entering at higher post-Newtonian orders, which remain comparatively poorly constrained. Using NR simulations from the SXS catalog, we first recover the injected signals within general relativity using $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPHM-SpinTaylor}$, $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPNR}$, and $\texttt{SEOBNRv5PHM}$, finding model-dependent biases in the inferred masses, spins, and spin orientations. We then analyze the same signals with the $\texttt{IMRPhenomXPHM}$-based inspiral parameterized test of general relativity framework, TIGER, and find that these waveform-systematic biases can lead to apparent deviations from general relativity, which become significant for loud signals. Our results highlight that highly spinning binaries offer powerful tests of higher-order post-Newtonian deviations, but waveform inaccuracies can lead to false signs of new physics.

papers.title_en: Can we constrain cosmology with compound gravitational lenses?
papers.abstract_en: Compound lensing in double-source-plane lenses (DSPLs) introduces multiple mass-sheet transformations that bias the inferred distance ratios $β$ used to constrain cosmology. We present the recovered $β$ from lens models of simulated compound lenses and explore the systematic biases that arise from a mass-sheet transformation in the first source plane. We examined simulated observations based on SDSS J0946+1006, in which we varied the matter distribution of source 1. We found a strong correlation between the stellar-to-halo mass and the recovered $β$. We produced a simulated catalogue of DSPLs detectable by the Euclid telescope to see if the same systematic propagates to a more varied population. But at Euclid's resolution, the properties of source 1 were poorly constrained, and any correlated bias was lost in the statistical uncertainty. We inferred $w_0$ and $Ω_{\rm m}$ for a flat $w$CDM cosmology from our $β$ posteriors for our combined sample. We found the cosmology biased when using the full mock Euclid sample, but reduced the bias substantially using a limited, well-modelled ''gold'' sub-sample, bringing it to within $\sim2σ$ and $\sim1σ$ of the ground-truth cosmology for simulated Euclid and Hubble Space Telescope imaging, respectively. Therefore, we must eliminate systems with unreliable lensing information, and for extreme compound lensing, the model complexity must be sufficient to reproduce the lensing observations. DSPLs remain a promising cosmological probe that could provide independent and complementary constraints to existing probes.

papers.title_en: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
papers.abstract_en: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.

papers.title_en: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
papers.abstract_en: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto

papers.title_en: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
papers.abstract_en: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.

papers.title_en: Weak ergodicity breaking captured from short-time dynamcis and graph theory
papers.abstract_en: We study the onset of weak ergodicity violations in closed quantum many-body systems and focus on cases in which they occur through a transition that is controlled by a model parameter, a scenario called a weak ergodicity-breaking transition. This situation is realized in the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the quantum sun model, which we investigate here. Our analysis is based on representing quantum systems in Fock space and examining the short-time dynamics of density autocorrelation functions. From these, we extract proxies for decay rates for each individual basis state. As a first main result, we show that the distribution of such decay rates captures known weak ergodicity-breaking transitions in both models. As a second main result, we establish a connection between the decay rates of density autocorrelations and graph-theoretical measures. Concretely, we demonstrate that moments of the distribution of the recently introduced graph-energy centrality also detect the weak ergodicity transitions, which is inherited from the behavior of the decay rates. While most numerical tools are limited to small system sizes, the quantities studied in our work can be calculated analytically for large systems of many hundreds of sites and in some cases, even in the thermodynamic limit.

papers.title_en: $^{55}$Mn-NMR/NQR study on the kagome metal Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$: Re-examining the possibility of spin-singlet paired state
papers.abstract_en: Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ is a Mn-based kagome metal that has been proposed to be close to a ferromagnetic instability. Recent $^{55}$Mn nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) study suggested the emergence of a spin-singlet paired state below $\sim$10 K. To clarify its low-energy magnetic and electronic properties, we performed $^{55}$Mn NMR and nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR) measurements on single-crystalline Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$. From the detailed NMR/NQR spectrum measurements and the DFT calculations, a quadrupolar frequency of $ν_{\rm Q}$ = 4.6$\sim$4.8 MHz and an asymmetry parameter of $η$ = 0.45$\sim$0.48 as well as the principal axes of electric field gradient EFG for the Mn site were determined. The temperature dependence of Knight shift ($K$) shows a similar temperature dependence of the DC magnetic susceptibility $χ$ except for the low-temperature region below $\sim$ 50 K where $K$ is almost constant while $χ$ keeps increasing, which suggests that the increase in $χ$ at low temperatures is not intrinsic. $^{55}$Mn spin-lattice relaxation rate divided by temperature ($1/T_1T$) is found to be nearly constant, confirming the metallic state of Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$ from a microscopic point of view. Furthermore, no peak in $1/T_1T$ is observed near 10 K, and neither the Knight shift nor the linewidth shows any reductions at low temperatures. These results suggest no clear signature for the spin-singlet pairing around 10 K in Sc$_3$Mn$_3$Al$_7$Si$_5$.

papers.title_en: A Toy Model for Topological Entanglement Features in 1+1D Integrable Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract_en: In this paper we investigate an entanglement measure, the Rényi entropy, in a 1+1D integrable quantum field theory known as the Federbush model. This is a deformation of the theory of two massive Dirac fermions by means of a bilinear term in the $U(1)$ currents that couples the two fermion species. This deformation gives rise to $S$-matrix elements which are coupling-dependent phases, distinct from -1. These non-trivial phases can be seen as encoding anyon-like statistics. From this viewpoint, the Federbush model is a toy model for topological features of entanglement in one space dimension. In this paper we show that, a standard computation based on form factors of branch point twist fields leads to the conclusion that these topological features play no role when computing most known measures of entanglement at equilibrium in the ground state. This conclusion applies also to the post-quench dynamics at first order in perturbation theory, after a small quench of the topological parameter.

papers.title_en: Toward Self-Driving Multi-reference Calculations: Belief-Aware Orbital Selection
papers.abstract_en: We reformulate active-orbital selection as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), analogous to decision-making in autonomous driving and robot control, and couple it with quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) to emulate expert-like selection of active orbitals. The three popular types of orbital information, i.e. occupation numbers, orbital composition, and orbital entanglements, can be used separately or jointly. QUBO constructs complete candidate spaces under fixed electron and orbital counts, while the POMDP selects successive calculations, updates its belief from each completed result, and thereby corrects and refines the active orbitals. This belief-aware sequential procedure enables continuous active-space selection rather than one-shot threshold-based filtering, so the space can adapt as the calculation proceeds. We demonstrate the approach for valence-space construction in small molecules, spectral calculation of metal compound TiF$_3$, and active-space refinement of 1,2-dioxetanone around conical intersections. Because selection learns from calculations on the molecule of interest without requiring a pre-existing training set, it is suited to following the entire course of complex chemical reactions.

papers.title_en: Spin Structure Factor of the classical Ising Model on the Centered Pyrochlore Lattice
papers.abstract_en: We present the spin structure factor of the Ising model on the centered pyrochlore lattice. Generalizing Henley's method [Phys. Rev. B 71, 014424] to the case of inequivalent center and vertex spins, we obtain spin correlation functions that are in excellent agreement with Monte Carlo results and can capture sharp and broadened pinch points, also at finite temperature. Our approach can be extended to other centered lattice structures in classical frustrated magnetism.

papers.title_en: An azimuthally resolved study of sloshing cold fronts in three nearby galaxy clusters
papers.abstract_en: We present a detailed analysis of sloshing cold fronts in a sample of three nearby galaxy clusters (Abell 496, Abell 2029, and Abell 1644) observed with the $Chandra$ X-ray Observatory. Cold fronts manifest as sharp edges in the X-ray surface brightness of the intracluster medium (ICM) in galaxy clusters. In the residual X-ray surface brightness maps, where the global ICM distribution has been subtracted, cold fronts generated by gas sloshing are observed at the boundaries of the spiral excesses. We perform a systematic and comprehensive study of the surface brightness edges along the spiral excesses. We find the deficit of the thermal pressure radially inward of the brightness edges, in contrast to stripping cold fronts that typically exhibit higher thermal pressure in brightness edges. Assuming that the non-thermal pressure support entirely comes from the gas motions, we estimate the velocity dispersions across the edges and do not find statistically significant azimuthal variations along the sharpest edges. With an assumption that the non-thermal pressure support is completely attributed to the magnetic pressure, we derive the upper bounds on the strength of magnetic fields, yielding $6\,μ\mathrm{G}$, $15\,μ\mathrm{G}$, and $5\,μ\mathrm{G}$ for Abell 496, Abell 2029, and Abell 1644, respectively. We discuss several systematic uncertainties in characterizing the sloshing cold fronts and find that the choice of spectral extraction regions has an effect for subtle cold fronts observed with shallow X-ray data.

papers.title_en: Model of the instrumental polarization induced by a rotating HWP with anti-reflective sub-wavelength structures for CMB polarimetry
papers.abstract_en: Future CMB polarization experiments require precise control of instrumental systematics in the search for primordial $B$-mode polarization. A rotating half-wave plate (HWP) provides effective polarization modulation, but its non-ideal electromagnetic response can generate HWP-synchronous instrumental polarization. In this work, we characterize the response of a multi-layer sapphire HWP with anti-reflective sub-wavelength structures (SWS) using rigorous coupled-wave analysis. For three asymmetric SWS models, we find no substantial differences in the transmittance, polarization efficiency, or instrumental-polarization response that can be attributed to the type of SWS asymmetry. The fourth-harmonic instrumental polarization relevant to CMB polarization reconstruction is typically of order $10^{-4}$ in the CMB bands, which is expected to be mitigated. We further evaluate an actually fabricated SWS geometry, whose asymmetry enhances the retardance, and compare its response with that of an idealized model having the same type of asymmetry. Comparison of the realistic SWS with the idealized model shows that higher transmittance tends to be associated with lower instrumental polarization. These results suggest that improving the total transmission, including the effect of the fabricated SWS profile, may be more important for reducing HWP-induced instrumental polarization than tuning the SWS asymmetry itself.

papers.title_en: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
papers.abstract_en: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(ρ)=1+a^2/(4ρ^2)$. Through the Plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=μ_r=n(ρ)\,\mathbb{1}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(ωa/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $πa^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.

papers.title_en: Triple-Massive-Exchange Bispectrum of Quasi-Single-Field Inflation
papers.abstract_en: The triple-exchange bispectrum of the scalar quasi-single-field inflation model has resisted analytic evaluation across its full parameter space since its advent, despite rapid progress in cosmological collider physics. In this Letter, we solve it for general mass and mixing strength as a convergent double series, by applying the Mellin-Barnes representation directly to the mixed propagator between the massless and massive modes. The result is exact, non-perturbative, and physically transparent; the method is broadly applicable.

papers.title_en: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
papers.abstract_en: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate numerical comparisons, some protocols reach a given tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. To examine the limits of preparation, we consider critical states that already carry a slow scalar field and exterior charge. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of $O(\varepsilon^4)$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient connects this reserve to the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow tail on the normal side. This limited reserve constrains how quickly the existing field can be removed. For releases that suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge, the preparation time grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$ under horizon regularity and uniform radial control. Charge transport constrains the same covariant scalar flux that produces horizon entropy, raising the minimum flux cost and strengthening the time bound.

papers.title_en: Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations
papers.abstract_en: Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $Λ$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $Λ$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $Λ$CDM at $2σ$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$α$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.

papers.title_en: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
papers.abstract_en: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.

papers.title_en: Chaotic Dynamics around a Hairy Black Hole in Horndeski Gravity
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the chaotic dynamics of a spinning test particle in a static, spherically symmet- ric hairy black hole (BH) in Horndeski gravity, using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations closed by the Tulczyjew-Dixon condition. Bound orbits are identified by fixing the angular momen- tum and setting the energy according to the effective potential, so that the accessible parameter range is bounded by a critical hair parameter, hcrit, which varies non-monotonically with the spin. We analyze the resulting chaotic behavior using Lyapunov exponents, Poincare sections, and re- constructed attractors. We find that the response of these indicators to scalar hair is orbit- and spin-dependent rather than universally monotonic. An analysis of orbital frequency ratios shows that, at physically maximal spin (S = 1), an approaching 2:1 azimuthal resonance overlapping a persistent 1:1 polar lock amplifies chaos, while the hair-driven erosion of potential saddles tends to suppress it. At non-physical spin (S = 1.5), the Lyapunov exponent decreases monotonically. Gravitational waveforms constructed via the quadrupole formula inherit the same state-specific pattern: the correlation between the two polarization modes varies non-monotonically with h, in step with the Lyapunov exponent. These results show that chaotic indicators respond to scalar hair in an orbit- and resonance-dependent manner rather than through simple monotonic suppres- sion, and identify the spin-dependent resonance structure as an essential ingredient for interpreting chaos around hairy black holes.

papers.title_en: Machine-accelerated extraction of experimental superconducting parameters for physical insight and prediction across thousands of materials
papers.abstract_en: New superconductors could unlock next-generation technologies from nuclear fusion to lossless electronics. Machine learning can predict candidate superconductors but lacks validated experimental training data beyond the critical temperature. Here we present AutoSuperCon, a database of eight superconducting parameters, containing 20354 entries for 6793 superconductors. The data were extracted from over 47000 arXiv preprints using a large language model and validated against reference datasets ($R^2 = 0.96$ with NIMS SuperCon). Using AutoSuperCon, we show that median gap ratios rise from 3.6 in conventional superconductors to 6.4 in cuprates, 28% of upper critical fields exceed the Pauli limit, and critical temperatures lie below a ceiling proportional to the superfluid density. Further, we train composition-based predictors for the critical temperature ($R^2_{\log}=0.83$) and the upper critical field ($R^2_{\log}=0.69$), boosted by transfer learning. Within known superconducting families, composition alone is sufficient to screen candidates for both parameters. AutoSuperCon thus enables physical insight and data-driven discovery across thousands of superconductors.

papers.title_en: Matter Swapping between Two Branes: Conditions for a Local Type IIB D3-D7-D3 Mechanism of Charged-Fermion Mixing via E3 Instantons
papers.abstract_en: Effective infrared two-sheeted descriptions of fermion mixing between braneworlds have emerged in several distinct realizations and lead to testable matter-swapping effects, motivating low-energy searches and cosmological applications. The recurrence of the same low-energy fermion operator motivates investigating whether this structure can also arise from a D-brane mechanism. We investigate the conditions under which a local Type IIB D3$_+$-D7-D3$_-$/E3 configuration can generate perturbatively forbidden interbrane mixing. Assuming the required charged zero-mode spectrum, neutral instanton measure and non-vanishing charged disk amplitudes, we derive an E3-induced chiral mass term with scalar and pseudoscalar components. The latter reproduces the characteristic mixing structure of the two-sheeted fermion operator, while D7 Wilson transport supplies the gauge-invariant relative connection between the two brane sectors. We establish the corresponding gauge matching for transitions between stationary states at resonance. This yields a conditional matching to the two-sheeted operator within the effective field theory. A separate orbifold example checks the charged zero-mode representations and the compensating instanton charge. Whether all the required instanton ingredients coexist with two independent massive D3-D7 matter sectors at separated endpoints in a single local configuration remains open. We outline a model-building roadmap toward such a configuration and its compact phenomenological embedding. Such an embedding requires electromagnetic sequestering of the two fermion sectors and a sufficiently light non-uniform D7 gauge mode mediating a long-range relative interaction. In such a compactification, the mixing parameter $g$ would be determined by microscopic instanton data and matter-field normalization, providing a connection to low-energy constraints.

papers.title_en: Defect-induced stabilization of Wigner negativity and parity-protected phase-locking
papers.abstract_en: We show that a parity-preserving delta-shaped potential, mimicking the presence of a localized defect, reduces the continuous $U(1)$-symmetry of a quantum van der Pol oscillator to the discrete $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetry. This mechanism guarantees protected even-parity stationary quantum coherences, resulting in the generation of non-classical steady-states characterized by Wigner function negativity. Thanks to a non-trivial interplay between the defect and non-linear dissipative channels, this kind of negativity entails parity-protected quantum phase locking, meaning that the oscillator's energy levels simultaneously lock into two opposite phases. Finally, we present a realistic experimental proposal involving the motional state of ultracold alkaline-earth-like atoms in optical tweezers, where the localized defect is engineered via state-selective contact interactions, while the non-linear dissipative channels are driven by Raman sidebands.

papers.title_en: Schwinger-Unruh Interplay and Mode-Resolved Entanglement of Charged Scalar Fields in Rindler Spacetime
papers.abstract_en: We study pairwise and cross-horizon correlations of a charged scalar field in Rindler spacetime in the presence of parallel electric and magnetic fields. The transverse magnetic field produces Landau levels, while the longitudinal mode problem follows the charged-scalar Rindler construction with the effective mass $M_n^2=m^2+(2n+1)|qB|$. For a specified global vacuum in the negative-frequency sector, we obtain the outgoing four-mode Gaussian state and calculate logarithmic negativity and quantum mutual information for selected mode pairs. We find that the cross-wedge antiparticle-particle pair is entangled only when $q_2<\tanh r_U$. It can therefore become separable although its mutual information remains nonzero. The intra-wedge particle-antiparticle pair remains entangled for nonzero Schwinger squeezing. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. Using the Gaussian Schmidt decomposition, we show that the entanglement across the complete right--left wedge partition is carried by a pair of collective modes, even when the selected outgoing cross-wedge pair becomes separable. We discuss the Landau-level dependence and the limits of these mode-resolved conclusions, without identifying the vacuum-dependent mixing parameter with a detector temperature.

papers.title_en: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
papers.abstract_en: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $Ω^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $Ω^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges. Lastly, we obtain the axial vortical effect conductivity for the free massive spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field.

papers.title_en: Conformal boundary rigidity from null geodesic travel times
papers.abstract_en: The gravitational field of a distant, isolated system is manifested by the conformally invariant Weyl tensor. Thus the conformal structure far from the system encodes the system's gravitational mass. It also encodes the causal structure, thereby linking it to the mass. For asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, this link led to a novel positive mass theorem of Page, Surya, and the second author \cite{PSW} which did not rely on any traditional energy condition. Here we ask whether that theorem has a rigidity case. Specifically, we consider all null geodesics in an asymptotically AdS spacetime that depart from the Penrose conformal infinity, travel through spacetime, and return to conformal infinity. If all such geodesics from a given point refocus at an antipodal point at infinity, is the spacetime conformal to anti-de Sitter space? It is easy to answer the question if the asymptotically AdS spacetime either (i) obeys the null energy condition in 3 or 4 spacetime dimensions, or (ii) is static (in any dimension), and we give simple proofs in those cases. We then answer the question in the case of globally stationary, asymptotically AdS spacetimes, by applying the theory of magnetic geodesics on the Riemannian manifold-with-boundary obtained by quotienting by the stationary Killing vector field. The question has an analogue for asymptotically flat spacetimes, which we also discuss.

papers.title_en: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
papers.abstract_en: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2)$.

papers.title_en: Dressed Newton-Cartan geometry and Euclidean thermal configurations in 3D
papers.abstract_en: We report a new class of solutions of three-dimensional Galilean Anti-de Sitter gravity. The theory can be formulated as a topological gauge theory invariant under the doubly extended Newton-Hooke group in three dimensions. The solution can be interpreted as a dressed Newton-Cartan geometry, which is endowed with four conserved charges: energy, angular momentum, spin and rest mass. Interestingly, the magnitude of the spin turns out to be bounded from above by the rest mass. The Euclidean continuation of the solution exhibits well--defined thermal properties in terms of its gauge theoretical description. Temperature, angular velocity and other chemical potentials are obtained from suitable regularity conditions associated with the topology of a solid torus.

papers.title_en: AI for BMN Strings
papers.abstract_en: With the assistance of AI (Artificial Intelligence) tools, we revisit some mathematically well-formulated problems from our previous studies of BMN (Berenstein-Maldacena-Nastase) strings on type IIB string theory pp-wave background. These mathematical problems have important physical implications, relating to the computations of higher-genus critical superstring amplitudes, possible estimate of the cosmological constant. We make significant progress on some problems, while others remain unresolved.

papers.title_en: Slow Macroscopic Rotations of Neutron Stars With a Deformed Effective Surface
papers.abstract_en: The macroscopic model for a neutron star (NS) as a finite perfect fluid at the equilibrium is extended to rotating deformed systems by incorporating the linear perturbation expansion over a small frequency $ω$ near the Schwarzschild gravitational metric within the effective-surface (ES) approach. The NS angular momentum $I$ and moment of inertia (MI) for a slow stationary azimuthal rotation around the symmetry axis is calculated by using the Kerr metric approach in spheroidal coordinates, and compared with the spherical results. The gradient surface terms of the macroscopic NS energy density $\mathcal{E}(ρ)$ (Equation of State) are taken into account along with the volume ones at the leading order of the leptodermic parameter $a/R \ll 1$, where $a$ is the ES crust thickness and $R$ is the NS effective radius. The analytical macroscopic NS MI expressions, $Θ= dI/dω= \widetildeΘ/(1-\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi})$, have been obtained in terms of the statistically averaged MI, $\tildeΘ$, and its time and azimuthal-angle $t,\varphi$ correlation, $\mathcal{T}_{t\varphi}$, as sums of the volume and surface components. The MI $Θ$ is changed significantly as function of the effective radius $R$ and deformation parameter because of a strong gravity. We found the additional narrower constraints for the NS radius due mainly to the $t,\varphi$ correlations and surface contributions and NS surface deformation. The adiabaticity conditions for application of the linear perturbation theory is carried out for several neutron stars with a strong gravity and relatively large rotation periods.

papers.title_en: Emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in hybrid Al/InAs heterostructures
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the microwave electrodynamics of a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures. Using lumped-element resonators with inductor wires oriented relative to an in-plane magnetic field, we directly probe the superfluid stiffness via the kinetic inductance. As the field increases, the resonance frequency exhibits a non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution that cannot be explained by orbital pair breaking alone. We show that this behavior is consistent with the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which selectively suppress the supercurrent response depending on the direction of the magnetic field. Microscopic calculations of the stiffness tensor capture the observed anisotropy driven by the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects. Our results establish microwave stiffness measurements as a sensitive probe of anisotropic gapless superconductivity in hybrid systems.

papers.title_en: Stellar evolution and axion-like particles: new constraints and hints from globular clusters in the GAIA DR3 data
papers.abstract_en: Axion-like particles (ALPs) are hypothetical pseudoscalar bosons, natural in extensions of the Standard Model. Their interactions with ordinary matter and radiation are suppressed, making it challenging to detect them in laboratory experiments. However, these particles, produced within stellar interiors, can provide an additional mechanism for energy loss, potentially influencing stellar evolution. Prominent methods for searching for such effects involve measuring the properties of red giants and helium-burning stars in globular clusters (GCs). Here we use published catalogs of stars selected as members of seven GCs on the basis of parallaxes and proper motions measured by Gaia (Data Release 3). Making use of previously derived theoretical relations and the new data, we find the upper limit on the ALP-electron coupling, g_{ae}<1.3*10^{-13} (95% CL), and an indication (2.6 sigma) to nonzero ALP-photon coupling, g_{aγ}=(6.6+1.3-1.8)*10^{-11} GeV^{-1}. Given the precision of contemporary observational data, it is imperative to refine ALP constraints through more sophisticated analyses, which will be explored in detail elsewhere.

papers.title_en: Decoupling of large-scale, adiabatic inflationary perturbations from enhanced small-scale modes at one-loop
papers.abstract_en: We reconsider back-reaction from large amplitude, short-scale perturbations onto a long wavelength adiabatic mode. In a loop expansion of the long-mode power spectrum, this back-reaction appears first at 1-loop. Due to the separation between the long and short scales, the separate universe method provides a simple and efficient framework for this computation. In this paper, building on our earlier work, we employ a $δN$ formula for the long mode, which captures the effect of short scales. We show that back-reaction at 1-loop is due to either (i) non-linearity of the $δN$ formula, or (ii) 1-loop corrections to the initial conditions. We argue that contributions of type (ii) cannot themselves be described within the separate universe framework, but their properties can be constrained using soft theorems and a ''multi-point propagator'' expansion. When applied to a band of enhanced short-scale perturbations that crossed the horizon during inflation, our result shows that the loop correction decouples from their detailed properties. Furthermore, the back-reaction we obtain is scale-invariant. Its magnitude is model-dependent, but is degenerate with effects from modes that were still sub-horizon at the end of inflation. In this scenario (but not necessarily in all scenarios), we conclude that the effect is not observable.

papers.title_en: Learning to stabilize nonequilibrium phases of matter with active feedback using partial information
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in quantum computing experiments have enabled new pathways for feedback control. Here, we investigate the role of information in interactive quantum many-body dynamics to engineer out-of-equilibrium phases of matter. To this end, we train reinforcement learning agents to prevent entanglement spreading in (1+1)-dimensional stabilizer circuits with up to 128 qubits. We find that, above an information threshold, agents learn stochastic near-optimal strategies that prevent the system from reaching volume-law entangled states and instead stabilize area-law scaling. These strategies rely on bottlenecks that divide the system and cap the entanglement in the steady state. Crucially, learned strategies are inherently out of equilibrium, require real-time active feedback, and could not be reproduced by simple human-designed control rules. This work establishes the foundations for information-driven individual control of many interacting quantum degrees of freedom, demonstrating the capabilities of reinforcement learning to stabilize and uncover novel critical properties of many-body nonequilibrium steady states.

papers.title_en: 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: matching $A(k)$ in ABJM free energy
papers.abstract_en: The function $A(k)$ appearing in the large $N$ expansion of free energy of ABJM theory on $S^3$ is known exactly from localization. An earlier calculation of the 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, based on the standard KK spectrum on $S^7$, did not reproduce it. We identify a missing 1-loop supergravity contribution as that of the 3-form field fluctuations built from square-integrable harmonic 2-forms on Euclidean $\mathrm{AdS}_4$ tensored with $S^7$ modes, which are not captured by the KK spectrum. Adding it to the KK tower contribution expressed in terms of superconformal characters and applying the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ projection, the total expression simplifies, and its evaluation in a zeta-function prescription reproduces the expression for $A(k)$. We also apply a similar approach to the 3d ADHM theory whose M-theory dual is the orbifold $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_p$, which has singularity along the fixed locus $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^3$, supporting a 7d $SU(p)$ vector multiplet. Adding the localized KK modes of this multiplet to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-projected supergravity spectrum gives a 1-loop free energy that reproduces the ADHM localization counterpart of $A(k)$.

papers.title_en: Engineering many-body tunneling dynamics of one-dimensional bosons with finite-core power-law interactions
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the many-body dynamics of a one-dimensional Bose-Josephson junction of ultracold bosons in a box-like potential with a central barrier, interacting via finite-core power-law interactions $V_α(r)=g/(r^α+d^α)$, where $d$ sets the short-distance scale and $α$ controls the spatial dependence. Using the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method for bosons (MCTDHB), we explore how the interaction profile and strength, barrier, and initial population imbalance shape tunneling dynamics. At weak interaction, increasing $α$ drives a crossover from Josephson oscillations to dephasing and recurrent rephasing, demonstrating the importance of the interaction kernel's spatial structure. A higher barrier suppresses recurrences, whereas a larger initial imbalance promotes relaxation toward nearly vanishing population imbalance. Increasing interaction strength progressively suppresses population-transfer fluctuations, particularly at larger $α$. The two-mode extended Bose-Hubbard model captures the dynamics when the lowest orbital in each well dominates, but loses accuracy as additional orbitals become populated. In the strongly interacting regime, many-body spatial structures develop and several natural orbitals are needed for converged dynamics, placing the system beyond a two-mode description. Our results establish the interaction profile and strength, barrier, and initial state as distinct control parameters for coherent, dephasing, recurrent, and suppressed many-body tunneling of one-dimensional bosons. The ability to tailor soft-core interactions via Rydberg dressing offers a promising route to exploring interaction-engineered tunneling in ultracold atoms.

papers.title_en: Ultraviolet Structure of the Gravitational-Wave Response in a Time-Dependent Scalar Medium
papers.abstract_en: We study the real-time linear response of gravitational waves in an FLRW background with a scalar field of general time-dependent effective mass. In the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we develop an adiabatic regularization scheme for unequal-time correlation functions and use it to extract the ultraviolet structure of the one-loop response. The leading divergence reproduces the familiar $\Box ^2h_{ij}$ structure, whereas the time-dependent background induces additional local divergences proportional to $\Box h_{ij}$, $\partial_τh_{ij}$, and $h_{ij}$. These are renormalized by local counterterms associated with the Weyl-squared term, a time-dependent Ricci-scalar term, a time-dependent cosmological constant, and the Ricci-scalar-squared term $R^2$. The same counterterms also remove the ultraviolet divergences of the background tadpole stress tensor and agree with the known covariant counterterm results. In a flat-background Mathieu oscillator example, replacing the adiabatic vacuum by the instantaneous vacuum leaves these counterterms unchanged but introduces an initial-surface divergence, which is absorbed into the initial data rather than the bulk counterterms.

papers.title_en: Quantum geometric ferromagnetism by singular saddle point
papers.abstract_en: We propose ferromagnetism that occurs in electrons at a saddle point with band touching, which we call the singular saddle point. At the singular saddle point, the divergent quantum metric induces ferromagnetic correlation, and the logarithmic divergence of the density of states ensures ferromagnetism within Stoner theory. This is a prototypical example of quantum geometric ferromagnetism. The two-dimensional $t_{2g}$-orbital model accommodates the ferromagnetism by this mechanism, which is continuously connected to the exactly proven flat-band ferromagnetism.

papers.title_en: Cumulant dynamics of the ferromagnetic dipolar XY model
papers.abstract_en: We study the second-order truncated cumulant dynamics for the preparation of dynamical states in the dipolar ferromagnetic XY model on the square lattice for system sizes up to linear size L = 60. The observations lead to a transparent picture in which a coherent region of finite extent and finite magnetization forms, which is possible even for diabatic but sufficiently slow ramps. These two scales are functions of the ramp constant, the initial entropy of the system, and time. Our findings put strong requirements on future experiments addressing dipolar XY equilibrium physics in bigger system sizes.

papers.title_en: Holographic dual of the 2d Ising model
papers.abstract_en: We propose a holographic dual of the 2d Ising model on a torus as the Turaev-Viro TQFT on a solid torus. The bulk spacetime is divided into the ``core'' region and the ``sandwich'' region. The core region prepares a defect state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on the topological boundary $\mathbb{D}$. The sandwich region computes the Turaev-Viro state sum $\langle\mathcal{D}|Π|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ between the state $|\mathcal{D}\rangle$ on $\mathbb{D}$ and the state $|\mathcal{F}\rangle$ on the physical boundary $\mathbb{B}$. The fusion diagram (or string-net) $\mathcal{F}$ on $\mathbb{B}$ is given by the Aasen-Fendley-Mong construction. There is also a ``bedding surface'' $\mathbb{S}$ between $\mathbb{D}$ and $\mathbb{B}$, and the height variables (or Ising spins inside/outside of the domain wall) are naturally living on $\mathbb{S}$. The bulk spacetime is discretized by the 2-skeleton $P$ which interpolates $\mathcal{D}$ and $\mathcal{F}$. When the defect $\mathcal{D}$ is absent, the 2-skeleton $P$ ends on the bedding surface $\mathbb{S}$ and $P$ is interpreted as the bulk worldsheet of the string-net $\mathcal{F}$.

papers.title_en: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
papers.abstract_en: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.

papers.title_en: LHAASO's Peanut source is a laboratory for studying magnetic fields in the Milky Way
papers.abstract_en: Recently, the LHAASO Collaboration reported gamma-ray emission from the Peanut-shaped source (Peanut), which extends over $4.5^\circ$ parallel to the Galactic plane at $b=-17.5^\circ$. The source is associated with the millisecond pulsar PSR J0218+4232, located at the eastern edge of the Peanut, at a distance of 3 kpc from the Earth and 0.9 kpc from the Galactic plane. Its location and bright gamma-ray emission above 25 TeV make it a natural laboratory for studying the Galactic magnetic field (GMF) in the transition region between the Galactic plane and halo. We interpret the observed emission as inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by electrons propagating along the large-scale GMF, accounting for turbulence through two models: Kolmogorov and Goldreich-Sridhar (GS). These models correspond to diffusive and ballistic particle propagation, respectively. While the GS case naturally provides conditions for one-sided gamma-ray emission, in the Kolmogorov case assumptions of one-sided particle injection and magnetic mirror at the source are necessary. We find that, in the Kolmogorov scenario, the Peanut's hotspots are likely associated with magnetic bottling, whereas in the GS scenario, they are related to magnetic field line geometry. Both models yield constraints on the GMF at the location of the Peanut.

papers.title_en: From $3\times2$pt to $4\times3$pt: calibrating galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments with galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra
papers.abstract_en: Combining galaxy clustering and weak gravitational lensing beyond two-point statistics offers a way to extract additional cosmological information while calibrating astrophysical nuisance parameters. We investigate this approach by combining 1-loop power spectra with tree-level bispectra, including all auto- and cross-bispectra of galaxy clustering and weak lensing, a combination that we refer to as $4\times3$pt by analogy with the well-known $3\times2$pt analysis. Modelling two- and three-point statistics consistently, with galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments described by the TATT model, we perform Fisher forecasts of dark energy constraints for a Euclid-like survey, with conservative scale cuts. When combined with CMB data, adding $4\times3$pt bispectra to the $3\times2$pt improves the dark energy figure of merit by about $30\%$, a gain that remains stable when using the three, four or five lowest redshift bins of our ten. To extend the analysis to ten tomographic bins, we compress the bispectra into skew-spectra, which improve the figure of merit by $20\%$ with the CMB and by $37\%$ without. We show that most of this improvement comes from the calibration of second-order galaxy bias parameters by three-point statistics, mainly by the galaxy-auto and the GGL bispectra. We also find that baryonic feedback is correlated with second-order intrinsic alignment parameters once the amplitude of the matter power spectrum is constrained by the CMB, and that bispectra reduce this correlation by calibrating intrinsic alignments, almost entirely through the GGL bispectra, a mechanism that could become more valuable with more flexible baryonic feedback models. These results demonstrate the potential of combined galaxy clustering and weak lensing bispectra to improve cosmological constraints from stage-IV galaxy surveys through the calibration of galaxy bias and intrinsic alignments.

papers.title_en: Numerical Thermodynamics of AdS Black Holes with Higher-Order Mass Corrections
papers.abstract_en: Inspired by noncommutative geometry and quintessence, we construct a new class of asymptotically anti-de Sitter black hole solutions characterized by a higher-order mass deformation term $\frac{aM^{n-1}}{r^n}$ involving two parameters, $a$ and $n$. Due to analytical difficulties, we approach the underlying thermodynamics through parallel programming simulations using CUDA codes. By considering models with $n=3$, $n=4$, and $n=5$, we numerically study certain thermodynamic properties, including the stability, the $P$-$v$ criticality, and the phase transitions.

papers.title_en: Radiation from scattering on multiple shockwaves
papers.abstract_en: It is well known that radiation produced by scattering an electron off multiple sources depends on the length of the mean free path between these scatterings. When this is sufficiently small, the spectrum is suppressed due to destructive interference, a famous result known as the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) effect. This is usually modelled approximately, with scattering centres treated linearly (e.g., as screened Coulomb potentials), high-energy probes and soft emitted photons. In this paper, we consider a scenario where multiple scatterings can be computed exactly: charged probe scattering on multiple null electromagnetic shockwaves. Here, the amplitudes for elastic scattering and single photon emission can be determined exactly, for arbitrary kinematics, in terms of the shock profiles in the transverse plane. We use these amplitudes to compute the radiation density (doubly-averaged over shock locations in the transverse plane and lightfront time) in the regimes of independent and interfering scatterings. For shock profiles which are radially symmetric in the transverse plane (including the ultraboosted Coulomb field), we recover the known LPM suppression, albeit with more general kinematics. In addition, our setup allows us to consider the source-free case of multiple scattering on impulsive/ultra-short plane waves, where we find much stronger suppression of the spectrum in the LPM regime.

papers.title_en: Origin of the Fe K$α$ red excess in IC 4329A with XRISM and multi-wavelength spectroscopy
papers.abstract_en: We present high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy of the bright local Seyfert 1 galaxy IC 4329A obtained with \textit{XRISM}/Resolve, supported by simultaneous \textit{NuSTAR} data and quasi-simultaneous optical/near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. Resolve separates the Fe K$α$ line into a narrow core and a broad component exhibiting a red excess. We examined three scenarios for this red excess: (1) a redshifted X-ray broad line region (xBLR), (2) relativistic disk reflection, and (3) an unshifted xBLR partially absorbed by a mildly ionized absorber. All three models reproduce the X-ray spectra equally well. Our optical (H$β$) and NIR (Pa$β$) spectroscopy shows that the broad lines are redshifted by $v \sim +640\text{--}1050\text{ km s}^{-1}$, close to the solution of the redshifted xBLR model ($v_{\rm shift} = +1700_{-800}^{+1700}\text{ km s}^{-1}$). Motivated by this, we constructed a hybrid model in which the xBLR shares the velocity structure of the optical/NIR BLR and the remaining red excess is attributed to a relativistic disk line, which also provides an acceptable fit. The inferred xBLR radius is $R_{\rm BLR} \sim (3\text{--}6) \times 10^3\ R_g$ ($\sim 12\text{--}22$ light-days). From the narrow Fe K$α$ core in the hybrid model (${\rm FWHM} = 870_{-280}^{+260}\text{ km s}^{-1}$), we estimate a torus distance of $R_{\rm torus} \sim 0.9_{-0.4}^{+1.0}$ pc ($\sim 1100$ light-days), close to the dust sublimation radius. Furthermore, two ultra-fast outflow (UFO) absorption features are identified with $v_{\text{wind}} \sim -0.30c$ and $-0.24c$, both confirmed at $>99\%$ confidence.

papers.title_en: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
papers.abstract_en: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

papers.title_en: On JT boundary algebras
papers.abstract_en: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.

papers.title_en: Multifractal collective order : Application to multifractal superconductivity in dodecagonal quasicrystals
papers.abstract_en: Conventional descriptions of collective ordering often assume spatially uniform order parameters, although the underlying electronic states can exhibit strong spatial inhomogeneity or multifractality. Here, we demonstrate that deterministic aperiodic geometry can instead stabilize multifractal collective order. We formulate a general diagnostic applicable to superconducting, magnetic, and charge channels, combining direct scaling analysis of the order parameter with three criteria: its spatial hierarchy must be dictated by the underlying geometry, emerge in the leading ordering instability, and persist in the self-consistent ordered state below a single mean-field ordering onset. We demonstrate that superconductivity on the experimentally resolved Ti network of a dodecagonal oxide quasicrystal satisfies all three criteria. The resulting condensate exhibits multifractal scaling over the resolved range of spatial scales, retaining its hierarchical structure throughout the ordered phase and channeling flux-induced equilibrium currents along geometry-locked rings.

papers.title_en: Spectra and Central Charges of Gauged Curvature Squared Supergravities in Five Dimensions
papers.abstract_en: We study the spectra and the central charges of off-shell gauged five-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supergravity extended by the Weyl squared, Ricci tensor squared and Ricci scalar squared invariants, and by their Gauss-Bonnet combination. Working exactly in the couplings and keeping all auxiliary fields, we organize the spectra around the maximally supersymmetric AdS$_5$ vacuum into supermultiplets. With the Ricci scalar squared invariant, the spectrum gains a long vector multiplet and is free of ghosts in a finite range of the coupling, while with the Weyl squared or Ricci tensor squared invariant, it gains a long spin-2 multiplet and always contains ghosts or instabilities. The Gauss-Bonnet combination adds no new modes: around its supersymmetric vacuum, the quadratic action is a rescaled copy of that of the two-derivative theory, and this fixes the spectrum of the Ricci tensor squared extension. We also compute the central charges $a$ and $c$ and the flavor central charge exactly in the couplings. The vacuum equation is $a$-maximization, and the kinetic terms of the massless graviton and vector multiplets are proportional to $c$ and to the flavor central charge, so that the critical points, where the massive spin-2 multiplet becomes degenerate with the graviton multiplet, are zeros of $c$. Finally, around supersymmetric AdS$_3\timesΣ_2$ backgrounds of the Gauss-Bonnet extension, the two-dimensional central charges are reproduced by $c$-extremization, while the spectrum is generically not unitary and contains towers of states whose energies stay bounded at large Kaluza-Klein levels. In part of the parameter space, the tower of spin-2 multiplets has positive norm, so that the spectrum has no finite density of states.

papers.title_en: Kerr-NUT Thermodynamics: Misner Strings and Nut Charges
papers.abstract_en: Using the thermodynamic approach introduced in e-Print: 2206.09124 [hep-th] to the case of Kerr-NUT solution, we demonstrate the existence of a new conserved quantity that is dual to the angular momentum, in the same way that the nut charge "n" is dual to the mass "m". This quantity exists regardless of the presence of the Kerr rotation parameter $a$, but only affects its thermodynamics when $a\neq 0$. The thermodynamic quantities calculated together with the two charges $N_{c}=cn$ and $N_{n}=n$ lead to consistent thermodynamic relations. That is, the first law, Smarr's and Gibbs-Duhem relations are all satisfied.

papers.title_en: A ménage à quatre without strings attached
papers.abstract_en: When two D-branes with eight mixed Dirichlet-Neumann directions cross, a fundamental string is created. This is the Hanany-Witten (HW) effect. In supergravity, the string shows up as an electric NSNS B-field sourced by the RR fields of the two branes. We show that two brane pairs, each of which would create an HW string on its own, can combine into a quadruple bound state with no HW strings attached. We explicitly construct a background with the fluxes of such a D0-D8-D4-D4' quadruple. Requiring no HW strings imposes a quadratic relation among the fluxes. We also realize this bound state as a supersymmetric solution of the non-Abelian DBI action of the D8-branes, whose Killing spinors match those of the bulk supergravity solution. The fluxed D8 stack acts as a domain wall between two supersymmetric D0-D8-D4-D4' backgrounds.
