By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.

papers.title_en: Deflating the Spacetime-Matter Dichotomy
papers.abstract_en: In this paper we analyse scalar-tensor theories-specific instances of which include mainstream inflation and dark energy models-in light of the spacetime-matter dichotomy. We argue that it is difficult to categorise the scalar fields as either a pure aspect of the spacetime structure or a pure form of matter, by focusing on the Jordan vs Einstein frames of these theories. We present and evaluate various interpretational options available, concluding that the spacetime-matter dichotomy becomes untenable in this context. At the same time, the ontological and conceptual category of spacetime can be decoupled from that of gravity, with the latter remaining viable in the context of scalar-tensor theories.

papers.title_en: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract_en: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title_en: Science Prospects for the Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory: SWGO
papers.abstract_en: Ground-based gamma-ray astronomy is now well established as a key observational approach to address critical topics at the frontiers of astroparticle physics and high-energy astrophysics. Whilst the field of TeV astronomy was once dominated by arrays of atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes, ground-level particle detection has now been demonstrated to be an equally viable and strongly complementary approach. Ground-level particle detection provides continuous monitoring of the overhead sky, critical for the mapping of extended structures and capturing transient phenomena. As demonstrated by HAWC and LHAASO, the technique provides the best available sensitivity above a few tens of TeV, and for the first time access to the PeV energy range. Despite the success of this approach, there is so far no major ground-level particle-based observatory with access to the Southern sky. HESS, located in Namibia, is the only major gamma-ray instrument in the Southern Hemisphere, and has shown the extraordinary richness of the inner galaxy in the TeV band, but is limited in terms of field of view and energy reach. SWGO is an international effort to construct the first wide-field instrument in the south with deep sensitivity from 100s of GeV into the PeV domain. The project is now close to the end of its development phase and planning for construction of the array in Chile has begun. Here we describe the baseline design, expected sensitivity and resolution, and describe in detail the main scientific topics that will be addressed by this new facility and its initial phase SWGO-A. We show that SWGO will have a transformational impact on a wide range of topics from cosmic-ray acceleration and transport to the nature of dark matter. SWGO represents a key piece of infrastructure for multi-messenger astronomy in the next decade, with strong scientific synergies with the nearby CTA Observatory.

papers.title_en: Holography for an AdS$_5$ to Hyperscaling-Violating Flow via Dimensional Reduction from 8d Einstein-Matter Gravity
papers.abstract_en: We construct a classical eight-dimensional Einstein--matter model whose reduction on a three-torus admits an AdS$_5$ ultraviolet vacuum and a hyperscaling-violating infrared solution. Neutral scalar winding maintains the ultraviolet vacuum, while its disappearance allows the infrared geometry to become locally AdS$_8$. The same reduction fixes the running gauge coupling, charged scalar mass and interactions. We derive the vacuum conditions, the radial evolution equations and the infrared spectrum. Scalar and vector superfluid orders are then compared using exact ultraviolet zero modes and analytic infrared eigenvalue identities. The scalar and vector instabilities in the infrared coincide at a unique scalar mass above the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound. Their nonlinear competition is governed by a quartic free energy that includes electric response and the change between fixed chemical potential and fixed density. For the interpolating geometry, we identify the conditions under which the two orders can appear together and form a locally stable phase.

papers.title_en: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
papers.abstract_en: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

papers.title_en: Can torsion mimic a cosmological constant? A one-parameter logarithmic $f(T)$ extension of $Λ$CDM
papers.abstract_en: We study a modified teleparallel gravity model of the $f(T)$ type. We propose a new functional form for in order to obtain a geometric origin to the $ΛCDM$ behavior in an appropriate limit. A perturbative expansion around the $ΛCDM$ regime is carried out, and the model's cosmic dynamics are calculated inside the flat FLRW background. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using multiple observational datasets, such as Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernova compilations (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, to constrain the model parameters. The findings show that the suggested $f(T)$ model accurately replicates the observed accelerated expansion and is statistically consistent with current cosmological observations. The model stays close to the $ΛCDM$ scenario while permitting tiny dynamical adjustments, as evidenced by the extra parameter $γ$, which quantifies deviations from the conventional cosmological model, being limited to values near zero.

papers.title_en: Calibration of CMB Polarisation Using Cross-Experiment Correlations
papers.abstract_en: Parity-violating physics in the Universe can generate correlations between the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) $E$- and $B$-modes, but detecting such signals requires extremely accurate calibration of instruments. We describe a data-driven method to calibrate the relative polarisation angle between CMB experiments using cross-correlations of observations over a common sky region. Unlike standard self-calibration approaches, this method does not assume vanishing isotropic cosmic birefringence or primordial $EB$ correlations when estimating the relative misalignment angle, and therefore preserves sensitivity to parity-violating physics. As a proof of concept, we forecast the performance of this method using the Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) as a calibrated reference. If they can be calibrated to an uncertainty of $0.08^\circ$, as anticipated from the SO wire grid calibration system, we show that the SO Large Aperture Telescope and Planck could be calibrated to uncertainties of $0.10^\circ$ and $0.17^\circ$, respectively, at $\sim 145$ GHz. This approach relies on the availability of at least one well-calibrated instrument, and provides a complementary path to improving polarisation calibration across experiments, enabling more robust searches for parity-violating physics in the CMB, such as cosmic birefringence.

papers.title_en: Nonreciprocal Josephson Dynamics of a $\mathcal{PT}$-Symmetric Atomtronic SQUID
papers.abstract_en: We investigate non-Hermitian Josephson dynamics in an atomtronic quantum interference device (AQUID), formed by a ring Bose Einstein condensate with balanced atomic gain and loss regions and two moving optical barriers. The balanced gain and loss profile establishes a parity time symmetric potential while breaking spatial inversion symmetry, providing the essential ingredients for nonreciprocal Josephson transport. The dynamics are monitored nondestructively through the phase quadrature spectrum of an optomechanical cavity driven by Laguerre Gaussian beams coupled to the condensate. We demonstrate that increasing the local gain and loss strength softens the parity time symmetric collective mode towards an exceptional point, as verified by Bogoliubov de Gennes analysis. The associated coherent population exchange produces an additional characteristic splitting in the cavity output spectrum. For linearly translating barriers, non-Hermiticity provides an additional control parameter for tuning the critical current. When the barriers undergo simultaneous translation and rotation, the rotation induced phase modifies the interference between counter propagating currents, offering further control over the nonreciprocal response. Under periodic barrier modulation, we find more pronounced Shapiro steps in the current voltage characteristics due to the intrinsic parity time symmetric collective mode. Finally, we propose an alternative Hermitian realization using a tilted optical lattice, providing an experimentally accessible route to engineering biased transport and population transfer. Our results establish parity time symmetric atomtronic SQUIDs as a versatile platform for controlling nonreciprocal Josephson transport and collective excitations in driven quantum fluids.

papers.title_en: DustER: Dust Extinction with Photometric Red Galaxies
papers.abstract_en: We present DustER, a new method for reconstructing dust reddening maps from photometric galaxy survey data. DustER uses red galaxies as "standard crayons". That is, it relies on the mean color of red-sequence galaxies being independent of their position in the sky. Given the galaxy's redshift, the difference between a galaxy's observed color and its expected color measures the reddening by dust along the galaxy's line of sight. When using photometric galaxy survey data, the method must rely on photometric redshifts, which, combined with selection effects, bias the recovered dust maps. DustER uses a novel approach to characterize and correct for these biases by leveraging the known statistical properties of the distribution of dust around the Milky Way. Testing on simulations, we find that the recovered dust maps are contaminated by large-scale structure. However, when we use the DustER map to deredden and select red-sequence galaxies, we find the resulting two-point function is not contaminated by dust.

papers.title_en: Reducing Massive Scattering Amplitudes to Normal Form
papers.abstract_en: Local amplitude reduction is a crucial tool in effective field theory (EFT) calculations. While polynomial normal forms reproduce the massless y-basis, massive amplitudes require reduction rules that preserve little-group tensor contractions. We generalize Gröbner-basis reduction to covariant tensor identities, determining leading monomials in their contraction contexts and generating the higher-degree rules induced by mass determinants. Using three-, four-, and five-point replacement catalogs, we demonstrate symbolic-mass amplitude reductions and reproduce the independent three- and four-vector operator bases, providing traceable normal-form reductions for local EFT matching and syzygy analysis.

papers.title_en: Short-term optical monitoring of quadruply imaged quasars
papers.abstract_en: We present two case studies to demonstrate that short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quadruply imaged quasars (quads) reveal their astrophysical potential. Using the Liverpool Telescope and the third facility of the Two-meter Twin Telescope (TTT3), we monitored the quads QSO 2237+0305 and PS J0147+4630 in the gr bands between July 2025 and January 2026. For QSO 2237+0305, the resulting light curves revealed microlensing variability over a timescale of ~150 days. The g-band difference light curve between images A and B was then used to reliably constrain the half-light radius of the g-band source within the 3.5-16 lt-day range (1σ confidence level). For PS J0147+4630, we derived new constraints on the AB and AC time delays from the r-band light curves of the ABC images in an arc-like configuration, obtaining 2σ uncertainties of ~2 days. These constraints were used to shed light on the lensing mass distribution. Overall, our results validate the design of short-term optical monitoring campaigns of quads as valuable astrophysical tools in the era of large-scale surveys. The proof of concept relies on observations with ground-based 2mclass telescopes that lack sophisticated systems to correct for optical distortions caused by atmospheric turbulence, and we indicate the astro-photometric properties of the targets and the monitoring strategies needed to achieve success with these telescopes. Additionally, this work represents the first validation of the TTT3 facility for precision photometric monitoring of gravitationally lensed quasars.

papers.title_en: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
papers.abstract_en: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.

papers.title_en: The fraction of periodic SN Ib/c light curves
papers.abstract_en: Periodic luminosity modulations have been recently identified for the stripped-envelope supernovae SN 2022jli and SN 2022esa, motivating a systematic search for a similar behavior in a larger sample. Such modulations may indicate the explosions arise in binary progenitor systems. We perform the first systematic search for periodic modulation in a sample of 34 Type Ib/c supernovae with high quality photometry from the Zwicky Transient Facility. We develop and apply a statistically rigorous pipeline for detecting periodic modulation in light curves. The pipeline successfully recovers the previously reported periodic undulations of SN 2022jli and SN 2022esa, and identifies SN 2020sgf as an additional promising periodic candidate. Injection-recovery simulations are used to quantify the survey sensitivity as a function of period and modulation amplitude. Comparing the observed detections with recent population synthesis models shows that, under the adopted assumptions, models predicting intrinsic periodic fractions of order ~20% are consistent with the observations. Given that this inference rests on only three dual-band detections out of 34 candidates, we regard this fraction as illustrative rather than a precise measurement. Our results suggest that periodically modulated SN 2022jli-like events may represent a non-negligible sub-population of stripped-envelope supernovae rather than being exceptionally rare events, while demonstrating a methodology suitable for future wide-field transient surveys.

papers.title_en: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
papers.abstract_en: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $ω_α$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $λ_α$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_α$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.

papers.title_en: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
papers.abstract_en: Topological Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes in more than two spatial dimensions offer features useful for fault-tolerant quantum computation, such as transversal non-Clifford gates and single-shot decoding, but a systematic understanding of them is still lacking. One approach is to decouple a code: map it to a stack of higher-form toric codes by a finite-depth local CSS-preserving Clifford circuit, possibly after adding ancillas. For translation-invariant $p$-ary CSS codes, where $p$ is prime ($p=2$ for qubits), we require the circuit to commute with the translations of a superlattice. In two dimensions, such a decoupling exists once these translations act trivially on every anyon type. In higher dimensions, excitations are sorted by their dimension into superselection layers, which can remain glued together even when translations act trivially on each layer. We show that this gluing is the only remaining obstruction: a code can be decoupled on a superlattice exactly when, after coarse-graining to it, translations act trivially on every layer and the gluing vanishes. Moreover, for a code with finitely many excitation types in each layer and $m$ nonzero layers, once translations act trivially on every layer, further coarse-graining by a factor of $p^{m-1}$ in every direction removes the aforementioned gluing. Physically, the same criterion determines when the code encodes the maximal number of logical qudits on a finite torus. Finally, we give an explicit algorithm that constructs the decoupling as a circuit of SUM (qudit CNOT) and SWAP gates.

papers.title_en: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
papers.abstract_en: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $γ$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. Ground-based Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) have driven this revolution over the past two decades. In this plenary review, presented at the 9th Heidelberg International Symposium on High-Energy Gamma-Ray Astronomy (Gamma 2026), I provide a synthesis of recent breakthrough physics discoveries achieved by current IACT arrays (H.E.S.S., MAGIC, and VERITAS) alongside early scientific achievements from the Large-Sized Telescope prototype (LST-1) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Key highlights include the definitive establishment of recurrent novae as transient cosmic-ray proton accelerators via RS Ophiuchi; spatially resolved multi-TeV emission from the relativistic jet termination shocks of microquasars; the discovery of a 20 TeV pulsed radiation component from the Vela pulsar, challenging established magnetospheric emission paradigms; precision measurements of the Galactic Center diffuse ridge spectrum favoring a high-energy cutoff; the detection of distant flat-spectrum radio quasars at $z \sim 1$ (OP 313 and PKS 0346-27), providing tight cosmological constraints on the Extragalactic Background Light; multi-wavelength afterglow detections of $γ$-ray bursts including GRB 221009A; and world-leading joint indirect dark matter limits from dwarf spheroidal galaxy and Galactic Center halo analyses. Together with algorithmic advances in deep learning reconstruction and the ongoing construction of CTAO, these milestones demonstrate the enduring vitality and future trajectory of ground-based $γ$-ray astrophysics.

papers.title_en: From Growth to Devices: Oxygen-Controlled Superconductivity in BSCCO Thin Films
papers.abstract_en: Realizing device-compatible high-$T_c$ superconductors requires simultaneous control of oxygen stoichiometry and tolerance to nanofabrication. Here, we investigate sputtered Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_{n-1}$Cu$_n$O$_{2n+4+δ}$ (BSCCO) thin films and establish a direct link between annealing conditions, oxygen incorporation, and superconducting transport. By independently varying the annealing temperature and duration, we identify an optimal annealing condition of $860\,^{\circ}$C for 3\,h, which yields the highest superconducting transition temperature and the narrowest transition among the investigated samples. X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and X-ray photoemission spectroscopy reveal a non-monotonic evolution of lattice oxygen, which governs hole doping in the CuO$_2$ planes and produces the characteristic dome-like dependence of $T_c$ on doping concentration. We further translate these optimized films into micro-devices to assess fabrication-induced effects, via micro-bridges as well as a planar Josephson junction. We demonstrate devices fabricated via both lift-off and focused ion beam (FIB) patterning methods -- proving the fabrication compatibility of these films. Importantly, we demonstrate their air-stability for extended periods of time (2 months). The combined insights offer practical guidelines for integrating cuprate thin films into superconducting electronics and quantum device architectures.

papers.title_en: Spectral-Timing Evolution of the Black Hole X-ray Binary LMC X-3: An XPoSat View
papers.abstract_en: LMC X-3 is a persistent black hole high-mass X-ray binary and serves as an important laboratory for studying accretion disk evolution across different spectral states. We present a spectral-timing analysis of XPoSat/XSPECT observations of LMC X--3 obtained during 2024 and 2025. Using broadband X-ray light curves, hardness diagnostics, power spectral analysis, and spectral modeling, we investigate the long-term evolution of the source across multiple epochs. LMC X-3 exhibits significant changes in both its spectral and timing properties between the two observing campaigns. Hardness-intensity and hardness-rms diagrams reveal a clear separation between the 2024 and 2025 observations and even within the 2024 observations. Overall, it indicates a transition from a relatively harder and more variable state to a brighter, softer, and less variable state. Power spectral analysis shows enhanced broadband variability during the 2024 observations, while the 2025 observations are characterized by weaker variability. Spectral modeling of the combined XSPECT observations indicates an increase in the thermal disk temperature from 0.8 to 1.17 keV, accompanied by a ~5 times increase in X-ray flux between the two epochs. The observed reduction in fractional rms variability with increasing source brightness and decreasing spectral hardness is consistent with more contribution from a stable thermal accretion disk. Taken together, the spectral and timing diagnostics provide a self-consistent picture of accretion-state evolution in LMC X-3, demonstrating the capability of XSPECT to probe long-term variability and accretion processes in bright black hole X-ray binaries.

papers.title_en: A self-supervised machine learning approach to identify instrumental systematics in 21cm Cosmology
papers.abstract_en: The primordial sound waves in the baryon-photon plasma are imprinted on the large-scale galaxy distribution as Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO), serving as a cosmological standard ruler to constrain dark energy and the Hubble parameter. The upcoming 21cm intensity-mapping arrays are designed to map the 21cm emission across large volumes and measure the BAO scale. However, radio interferometers suffer from instrumental systematics that can hinder detection of the cosmological 21cm signal by leaking bright foregrounds into the signal-dominated modes. This work aims to demonstrate that a self-supervised model can predict the instrument systematic state (here, the amplitude of a spectral ripple in the beam width) in interferometric visibilities and potentially disentangle the instrument from the sky without a forward model. Based on the fact that an instrument stays the same as the sky rotates in a drift-scan observation, and that the same sky is observed under different instrument states, we train a convolutional autoencoder to compress the information in the simulated visibilities and separate this information into instrument-only and sky-only latent vectors. The result shows excellent prediction of the unknown instrument systematic for 15 held-out instrument states with $R^2 = 0.9975$ with a linear probe, against $R^2 = -3.55$ for a random-encoder baseline. The instrument-latent carries no detectable sky signal, as measured with a total-power sky proxy, for any held-out test data. The sky-latent vector and instrument-latent vector show partial separation but not complete disentanglement, identifying sky-latent purity as the primary open problem. The results show the ability of the model to recognize the systematic and show a promising path towards an ML-based foreground cleaning pipeline. Full instrument-sky disentanglement constitutes the natural next step.

papers.title_en: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery
papers.abstract_en: Context. Anti-glitches are rare and enigmatic timing anomalies. High-cadence monitoring has revealed radiatively quiet anti-glitches in several pulsar populations, but radiatively loud anti-glitches and their links to magnetospheric activity remain poorly understood. Aims. We characterize a new, large anti-glitch in the magnetar 1E 2259+586 and compare its phenomenology with other magnetars. Methods. We analyze timing, flux, pulse-profile evolution, and spectra using EP, NICER, and IXPE X-ray observations. Results. We report a 2025 anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586, the largest in this source, with $Δν\approx-1.174(7)\times10^{-7}$ Hz and $Δν/ν\approx-8.19(4)\times10^{-7}$. Unlike its 2019 anti-glitch, this event was radiatively loud: the persistent X-ray flux roughly doubled (~106% increase), followed by a recovery exceeding 320 days. The pulse profile changed modestly but significantly: the valley between the main and secondary peaks became shallower and then recovered with the flux. Spectral properties also changed, and Fermi-GBM detected a short soft gamma-ray burst near the event. These features resemble the radiatively loud 2012 anti-glitch. Conclusions. 1E 2259+586 is unique among magnetars: its anti-glitch rate is comparable to normal spin-up glitch rates, and its anti-glitches can be radiatively loud or relatively quiescent. The fractional anti-glitch amplitudes appear to increase monotonically; further verification is needed. Regular monitoring of 1E 2259+586 is essential for understanding anti-glitch mechanisms.

papers.title_en: Stellar Scalar Monopoles from Gauss--Bonnet Curvature beyond Four Dimensions
papers.abstract_en: Above four dimensions every static, spherically symmetric star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole at first order in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling, given by an interior integral weighted by the energy density plus radial pressure. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of the coupling for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini black hole at the same order. The charge is fixed by the lapse-weighted Gauss--Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically when space is three-dimensional.

papers.title_en: Barriers to dequantization of near-term molecular electronic structure methods
papers.abstract_en: We prove classical simulation hardness, under the generalized $\mathsf{P}\neq\mathsf{NP}$ conjecture, for quantum circuit families with applications in near-term molecular electronic ground and excited state estimation. The proof exploits a connection to particle number conserving matchgate circuits with fermionic magic state inputs, which are shown to be universal for quantum computation under postselection, and are therefore not classically simulable in the worst case, in either the strong (multiplicative) or weak (sampling) sense. We apply these results to non-orthogonal quantum eigensolvers designed for near-term hardware by ruling out sample-based dequantization strategies to additively approximate the off-diagonal matrix elements between orbital-rotated correlated reference states that satisfy an irreducible fermionic magic property, which combines anticoncentration in any orbital basis with an average-case multiplicative approximation hardness conjecture for the associated matrix polynomials. We apply this complexity analysis to two choices of ansatz that incorporate both static and dynamic correlations to model the electronic eigenstates of molecular systems. These are linear combinations of orbital-rotated matrix product states, which are preparable in linear depth, and linear combinations of states prepared by generalized unitary coupled cluster with singles and doubles or unitary cluster Jastrow circuits of polynomial depth, for which computing the expectation values of local fermionic observables up to a constant additive error is $\mathsf{BQP}$-complete. We discuss the implications for achieving practical quantum advantage in resolving the electronic structure of catalytic systems composed from multivalent transition metal atoms using near-term quantum hardware.

papers.title_en: Yang-Lee edge singularity at $\mathcal{O}(\partial^4)$ from the functional renormalization group: revised analysis
papers.abstract_en: We determine the critical exponents of the Yang-Lee edge singularity as continuous functions of dimension using the functional renormalization group, retaining all operators at second and fourth order in the derivative expansion. At fourth order, we obtain $η=-0.153(7)$, $-0.352(9)$ and $-0.575(9)$ in $d=5$, $4$ and $3$, respectively, in agreement with the six-loop $ε$ expansion. In three dimensions, these results give $σ=0.076$ and $ν_c=0.359$. We locate the zero of the edge exponent at $d_σ=2.65(1)$, also consistent with the six-loop estimate. Continuing the fixed point through $d_σ$, we obtain $η=-0.795(21)$ and $ω=1.90(6)$ in $d=2$, compared with the exact values $-4/5$ and $2$. For the complex Yang-Lee fixed point, convergence of the field expansion depends crucially on its reference point. Expansions about $φ=0$ fail to converge with the smooth regulator used here, whereas expansions about the running imaginary field value at which the mass vanishes converge down to $d=1.3$. This representation preserves the exact relation between the thermal eigenvalue and the field dimension, and hence the hyperscaling identity $θ_h+θ_t=d$, at every field-truncation order. We trace the large violations reported in earlier works to the omission of the expansion-point motion when linearizing the flow, rather than to the truncation itself.

papers.title_en: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
papers.abstract_en: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. However, coefficients inferred from CR distributions averaged over cloud to Galactic scales leave local magnetic structure unresolved. We use the magnetic-field structure of NGC 1333 and its embedded protostellar core IRAS 4A to estimate local CR scattering rates and effective diffusion coefficients, $D(E)$, and examine their variation with environment and scale. We analyse JCMT/POL-2 maps of nine NGC 1333 regions and ALMA Band 7 maps of two IRAS 4A regions. We estimate plane-of-sky field strengths and derive fluctuation spectra from polarisation-angle structure functions. Where these spectra are sufficiently constrained, we apply quasi-linear gyro-resonant theory to calculate CR pitch-angle scattering rates and $D(E)$. The measured fluctuations constrain CR scattering over proton energy intervals of approximately 0.24-5.3 PeV in NGC 1333 and 10-57 TeV in IRAS 4A. Within these intervals, $D(E)$ spans approximately $3\times10^{28}$-$10^{31}\,{\rm cm^2\,s^{-1}}$. Scattering varies substantially between regions and is stronger where the magnetic-field angular dispersion is greater. Extrapolation to common energies suggests scattering in IRAS 4A is one to two orders of magnitude stronger than its surroundings. Within the directly probed intervals, the scattering mean free paths exceed the individual region sizes. The inferred diffusion coefficients therefore characterise local scattering conditions. A cloud-scale diffusive regime requires CRs to sample multiple regions with different scattering rates. Dust polarisation observations therefore provide constraints on CR scattering in clouds, connecting scattering to cloud-scale transport at energies accessible to $γ$-ray observatories.

papers.title_en: Disorder-Induced Logarithmic Spreading and Localization of Quantum Fluctuations
papers.abstract_en: Disorder can localize quantum particles, even in the presence of interactions, but its influence on quantum fluctuations beyond mean--field dynamics remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the propagation of quantum fluctuations in weakly interacting disordered bosonic systems by comparing the Bose--Hubbard model with the Gross--Pitaevskii equation. We find that, in contrast to ballistic spreading in the disorder--free system, quantum fluctuations exhibit logarithmic spreading at intermediate times under both random and quasiperiodic disorder, before eventually saturating. The spreading rate decreases algebraically with increasing disorder strength, and this behavior persists across different particle numbers and extends to two dimensions. Using a time--dependent Bogoliubov--de Gennes framework, we identify the localized mean--field wavefunction as a time--dependent pairing background that generates quantum fluctuations. The exponential suppression of fluctuation--generation rates with distance provides a physical mechanism for the logarithmically advancing fluctuation front. Our results reveal a distinct regime of disorder--controlled quantum--fluctuation dynamics and establish disorder as a means of controlling their spreading.

papers.title_en: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
papers.abstract_en: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

papers.title_en: Quantum droplets and condensates in an optical lattice coupled to a dissipative cavity: Collective excitations and non-equilibrium dynamics
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by recent experiments on light-matter interacting systems, we investigate a dilute Bose gas and self-bound quantum droplets in a one-dimensional optical lattice coupled to a lossy cavity mode. Using a classical-field approach, we determine the stationary states and collective excitations of this non-equilibrium system. Apart from the usual Bogoliubov modes, we identify a polariton-like gapped excitation, the frequency of which softens as a precursor of the density ordering transition. Moreover, its relaxation time diverges as the critical point is approached, signaling the non-equilibrium nature of this transition. Dynamically, this polariton-like mode can be probed by inducing cavity field fluctuations, which in turn generates spatio-temporal oscillations of both the condensate and droplet states. In the droplet regime, we also analyze the bound modes which bear the characteristics of such non-equilibrium self-bound state. In addition, we uncover solitonic non-equilibrium states, including condensate with kink-like configuration and double-droplet state, and investigate their robustness following a sudden quench. Remarkably, although these states become unstable beyond a critical coupling, they continue to manifest in the dynamics, akin to the scarring phenomena. Our results demonstrate that dissipative cavity coupling provides a versatile route for exploring rich non-equilibrium dynamics of condensates and quantum droplets within experimentally accessible settings.

papers.title_en: Floquet mobility edges and transport in a periodically driven generalized Aubry-André model
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the effect of a periodic electric field drive on the generalized Aubry-André model, also known as the Ganeshan-Pixley-Das Sarma (GPD) model, which is well known as a host of mobility edges. Our study of the Floquet spectrum of the driven GPD model uncovers the emergence of two distinct Floquet mobility edges, a delocalized--localized (DL) edge in the bounded regime, and a multifractal--localized (ML) edge in the unbounded regime. By mapping the high-frequency effective Hamiltonian to the static GPD model via a Bessel-renormalized hopping, the driven mobility edge formulae follow directly, with drive-induced localization arising naturally at specific values of the driving parameters, where the effective tunneling is coherently suppressed. Combined with numerical diagnostics such as the fractal dimension and inverse participation ratio, we demonstrate that these mobility edges can be effectively controlled by the amplitude and frequency of the electric field drive. Furthermore, the dynamical study of the periodically driven GPD model demonstrates superdiffusive to almost ballistic transport in the bounded regime corresponding to the DL edges, whereas subdiffusive transport is observed in the unbounded regime associated with the ML edges. We also analyze deviations from the high-frequency effective description by explicitly examining the low-frequency driving regime, where significant and counterintuitive deviations in both spectral properties and transport behavior are observed. Our study highlights the interplay of a quasiperiodic potential and a periodically varying electric field drive as a powerful mechanism to engineer mobility edges and control transport in systems with rich spectral features.

papers.title_en: Thermodynamic signatures of a nearby quantum critical endpoint in UTe$_2$ under intense magnetic field
papers.abstract_en: Several unconventional superconducting phases have been discovered in the vicinity of metamagnetism in the heavy-fermion paramagnet UTe$_2$ under magnetic field. To describe the mechanism of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity, a challenge is to characterize the quantum critical magnetic properties at the metamagnetic transition. In this work, we investigate the thermodynamic properties of UTe$_2$ under magnetic fields up to 60~T applied in the crystallographic $\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{c}$ plane. Magnetization and magnetostriction experiments have been performed under magnetic fields tilted by an angle $θ\lesssim42^\circ$ from $\mathbf{b}$ toward $\mathbf{c}$. They support that a quantum critical endpoint at the field angle $θ_{QCEP}\simeq(70\pm10)^\circ$ and magnetic field $μ_0H_{QCEP}\simeq(75\pm10)$~T terminates the metamagnetic transition line. A pseudo-gap in the magnetic susceptibility is related with the metamagnetic transition observed in magnetic fields for $θ<θ_{QCEP}$. The possible relation between the quantum critical endpoint and the development of magnetic-field-induced superconductivity is discussed.

papers.title_en: Implementation of a five-wave approximate Riemann solver for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics in AthenaK
papers.abstract_en: We present an implementation of an HLLD approximate Riemann solver for the AthenaK astrophysics code with support for full general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics via a tetrad frame transformation. Our implementation uses an initial guess for the HLLD iterative solve which eliminates the need for an additional conserved-to-primitive inversion, which greatly accelerates performance without affecting accuracy. Additionally, by coupling the method with a first-order flux correction, we are able to use the method reliably even when the magnetization exceeds $10^4$, which we achieve in a SANE accretion disk. Our SANE disk shows that HLLD leads to a more strongly magnetized funnel and more accurate horizon fluxes when compared with HLLE. We further apply the new HLLD implementation to an equal-mass binary neutron star merger. For our long-lived remnant, HLLD enhances the magnetic shear stresses in the outer layers and leads to weaker differential rotation. However, due to weaker gravitational wave emissions in the post-merger phase, the remnant is consistently less compact while producing more dynamical ejecta and a more massive disk. The cost of this new solver is relatively modest thanks to the improved initial guess: our accretion disk tests are only ${\sim}10-25\%$ slower than HLLE, and for our binary neutron star runs with a microphysical equation of state, we find that HLLD is only ${\sim}3\%$ slower than HLLE across all runs.

papers.title_en: Generalizations of Courant brackets in the T-dual description of a weakly curved string background
papers.abstract_en: When T-duality is realized as a canonical transformation, the standard Courant bracket is T-dual invariant, while the $B$- and $θ$-twisted Courant brackets are exchanged. We determine how these relations are modified for a closed bosonic string moving in a weakly curved background with a constant metric and a Kalb-Ramond field with linear coordinate dependence. We work to first order in its constant field strength. The T-dual background fields depend on a line integral of auxiliary worldsheet gauge fields, making the dual description nonlocal. We construct generalized charges whose parameters depend on this line integral and calculate their Poisson bracket algebra using the T-duality transformation laws and the canonical brackets of the initial theory. The resulting algebra yields a weakly curved generalization of the Courant bracket and its associated Courant algebroid. We establish an explicit isomorphism with the standard Courant algebroid by transporting the bracket, pairing, and anchor. Applying $B$- and $θ$-shifts to the dual currents, we obtain weakly curved generalizations of the respective twisted Courant brackets. We show that these brackets provide the T-dual realizations of the initial $θ$- and $B$-twisted Courant brackets, respectively, and identify the corresponding Courant algebroid isomorphisms.

papers.title_en: Wormholes and Averaging over N
papers.abstract_en: The gravitational path integral produces an asymptotic expansion in $G_N$, a fact which is puzzling in the case of observables that are expected to fluctuate wildly. Wormholes appear to compute ensemble averages of functions of such observables, though in typical constructions of AdS/CFT, there are no parameters to average over except, in some examples, a single integer $N$. We introduce a procedure that we call ``Mellin averaging'' to define a sort of asymptotic average of a function of $N$. We argue that Mellin averaging over $N$ may suffice to reproduce the apparent randomness seen in wormhole physics, provided that the dual theory admits an analytic continuation in $N$ and the relevant observables fluctuate on superpolynomially small scales in $N$. As a test case, we consider the spectral form factor in the regime where the double cone is believed to dominate the gravitational path integral and compare to a random matrix theory in which $N$ behaves as a continuous variable. We also describe some toy models of analytic continuation in $N$: a qubit model that can be analytically continued in $N$, and an explicit construction of a deterministic function of $N$ that simulates a sequence of independent draws from a Gaussian ensemble.

papers.title_en: Compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck low-$\ell$ data
papers.abstract_en: We present a compressed Gaussian likelihood for the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data, constructed from the SRoll2 likelihood which provides the tightest constraint on the reionization optical depth $τ$ to date. The non-Gaussian form of CMB low-$\ell$ TT and EE likelihoods makes them incompatible with Fisher matrix analyses that require an analytic Gaussian $χ^2$, such as the Fisher-bias formalism and Fisher forecasts. We show that the $χ^2$ of an offset log-normal likelihood takes a Gaussian form in the log-transformed power spectrum amplitudes, and can therefore serve as a proxy for the true Gaussian likelihood of this variable in Fisher matrix analyses, without any explicit change of variables. Building on this, we compress the SRoll2 likelihood into a small number of piecewise offset log-normal functions and validate it against the full SRoll2 likelihood via MCMC combined with Planck and ACT DR6 data, finding excellent agreement across all $Λ$CDM parameters and in extended cosmological models. We further demonstrate that Fisher matrix uncertainty estimates from our compressed likelihood agree well with the full MCMC posteriors. We release our compressed likelihood planck-gaussian-lowl, a lightweight Python package incorporating the compressed low-$\ell$ TT likelihood from previous work, allowing a straightforward incorporation of the Planck CMB low-$\ell$ data into any Gaussian-likelihood-based analysis. The package is publicly available at \href{https://github.com/nanoomlee/planck-gaussian-lowl}{github.com/nanoomlee/planck-gaussian-lowl}.

papers.title_en: NuSTAR view of the NGC 4151 corona: thermal balance and astroparticle constraints
papers.abstract_en: I present a comprehensive analysis of all publicly available NuSTAR observations of the nearby Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151 (2012--2024). The hard X-ray continuum is well described by thermal Comptonization in a hot corona, with electron temperatures $kT_{\rm e} \approx 40-125$ keV and optical depths $τ\approx 0.4-1.2$ (slab geometry). A clear anti-correlation between $kT_{\rm e}$ and $τ$ is observed, consistent with a thermostat behavior with constant Compton parameter $γ\approx 3.12$ calculated according to Sunyaev and Titarchuk (1980). Variability on timescales of hours constrains the size of the emitting region to $R \approx 250-1200 r_{\rm g}$, corresponding to moderate compactness values $\ell \lesssim 4$. The source occupies the same region of the compactness--temperature plane as other local Seyferts, with no evidence for pair runaway. I then explore two astroparticle implications. The IceCube neutrino excess reported toward NGC 4151 corresponds to $L_ν/L_X \approx 0.3\%$, an energetically negligible contribution that does not alter the observed coronal energy balance. An additional injection of pairs from the hypothetical X17 boson cannot produce significant changes, unless the injection rate exceeds the photoproduction one, but no anomalies were found in the present data set. The NuSTAR data thus provide no evidence for either a significant neutrino cooling channel or an X17-related pair injection in the corona of NGC 4151.

papers.title_en: Computational complexity of Berry phase estimation in topological phases of matter
papers.abstract_en: The Berry phase is a fundamental quantity in the classification of topological phases of matter. In this paper, we present a new quantum algorithm and several complexity-theoretical results for the Berry phase estimation (BPE) problems. Our new quantum algorithm achieves BPE in a more general setting than previously known quantum algorithms, with a theoretical guarantee. For the complexity-theoretic results, we consider two main cases. First, we prove $\mathsf{BQP}$-completeness when we are given a guiding state that has a large overlap with the ground state. This result establishes an exponential quantum speedup for estimating the Berry phase. Second, we prove $\mathsf{UQMA} \cap \mathsf{co}$-$\mathsf{UQMA}$-completeness when we have an $\textit{a priori}$ bound for the ground-state energy. Here, $\mathsf{UQMA}$ is the unique witness version of $\mathsf{QMA}$, and $\mathsf{UQMA} \cap \mathsf{co}$-$\mathsf{UQMA}$ precisely captures the complexity of BPE without the known guiding state. Remarkably, this problem is, to our knowledge, the first natural problem complete for $\mathsf{UQMA} \cap \mathsf{co}$-$\mathsf{UQMA}$. These results advance the role of quantum computing in the study of topological phases of matter and provide a pathway for clarifying the connection between topological phases of matter and computational complexity.

papers.title_en: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract_en: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

papers.title_en: Symmetric estimator for discrete self-energy of discrete many-body systems
papers.abstract_en: We derive a discrete spectral representation of the single-particle self-energy using a discrete evaluation of Kugler's symmetric improved estimator. Our construction can be used on both the real and the complex (Matsubara) frequency axis. It is guaranteed to remain causal at the numerical level, in contrast to standard approaches that may generate unphysical negative spectral weight or require additional broadening. Our representation can be used for any Hamiltonian; here we apply it to quantum impurity models and in dynamical mean-field theory. The latter is formulated with a discrete hybridization function throughout its self-consistency loop. In both cases and across various numerical methods, we obtain significantly improved accuracy for a range of impurity properties.

papers.title_en: On the stability of holographic confinement with magnetic fluxes
papers.abstract_en: We analyze the stability properties of a simple holographic model for a confining field theory. The gravity dual consists of an Abelian gauge field, with non-trivial magnetic flux, coupled to six-dimensional gravity with a negative cosmological constant. We construct a one-parameter family of regular solitonic solutions, where the gauge field carries flux along a compact circle that smoothly shrinks. The free energy of these solitonic backgrounds is compared to that of domain-wall solutions. This reveals a zero-temperature first-order phase transition in the dual field theory, separating confining and conformal phases. We compute the spectrum of bound states by analysing field fluctuations in the gravity background, after dimensional reduction on the circle. A tachyonic instability emerges near a turning point in the free energy. The phase transition prevents the realisation of this instability. Near the phase transition and beyond, in metastable and unstable regions, we find evidence that the lightest scalar may be interpreted as an approximate dilaton.

papers.title_en: Cosmological evolution with decaying dark matter: an integral-equation approach
papers.abstract_en: We present CLASSIER-DDM, an extension of the Boltzmann solver CLASSIER that implements the decaying dark matter (DDM) model via its integral-equation approach. The code handles generic two-body decays of a dark matter particle into two lighter decay products with arbitrary masses, naturally encompassing both massless (dark radiation) and massive (warm) decay products, with their perturbations evaluated via integral equations solved iteratively. We describe the numerical implementation in detail, including the background evolution, the iterative perturbation evolution, and a small-scale analytic approximation. A modest number of iterations is sufficient to achieve sub-$0.1\%$ convergence in the matter power spectrum and the CMB lensing power spectrum across the observationally relevant parameter space. We find that a hundred momentum bins for the decay product perturbations are sufficient to achieve $\mathcal{O}(0.1\%)$ accuracy in the matter power spectrum today up to $k \sim 3\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. The code achieves $\mathcal{O}(1\,{\rm min})$ runtimes per evaluation, requiring neither a Boltzmann hierarchy nor any fluid approximation, making parameter estimation with the DDM model numerically tractable. We also discuss the impact of DDM on cosmological observables, focusing on the case of two massive decay products. This work further establishes the integral-equation approach as a versatile and efficient framework for modeling non-cold relics in cosmological perturbation theory.

papers.title_en: Measuring the Evolution of Bulge, Disk and Colour Gradients in HST Observations of Galaxies with 3D Modelling
papers.abstract_en: We measure galaxy structural properties and colour gradients using HST images to trace the evolution of galaxy components. We develop and apply a physically motivated 3D bulge+disk modelling framework, jointly fitting the components in 2505 galaxies in GOODS-South across seven bands (bvizYJH) to $I_{\rm AB}=25.5$, accounting for different component ellipticities and inclination-dependent dust extinction. Extinction strongly affects structural parameters and colour gradients in $\sim$26% of the sample - primarily edge-on galaxies with central obscuration (B-band face-on optical depth $τ\simeq 4$) that reveal clear bulge components in the near-infrared. Despite irregular morphologies, the model captures observed colour gradients well. Bulges at $z \sim 1$ differ markedly from $z \sim 0$, with typical Sérsic index $n \sim 1.0$ and bulge-to-disc size ratio $R_{\rm e}/h_{\rm d} \sim 0.15$, suggesting most galaxies host pseudo-bulges formed via secular evolution. Galaxy ellipticity correlates strongly with disk scale-length. We trace bulge and disk evolution from $z \sim 0$ to $z \sim 2.5$: bulges are redder than disks (observed-frame) at $z < 1.4$, but colours converge at higher redshifts and fainter magnitudes. Redder galaxies show redder cores relative to their outskirts, and brighter galaxies have redder cores. These results provide new measurements of bulge and disk structural properties at $z \sim 1$ and observational constraints on their evolution, while also providing empirically motivated input distributions for assessing colour gradient systematics in weak lensing surveys.

papers.title_en: Steering and Local Tunneling Signatures of Majorana Corner Modes in Altermagnetic Josephson Junctions
papers.abstract_en: Dynamical manipulation of Majorana zero modes and their reliable distinction from topologically trivial states remain paramount challenges in topological quantum computation. Here, we propose a phase-biased altermagnetic Josephson junction as a versatile platform for generating and controlling Majorana corner configurations. Our platform utilizes the macroscopic superconducting phase difference and the Néel-vector orientation as independent control knobs to reshape the boundary mass. This allows the spatial configuration of Majorana corner modes (MCMs) to be selected at different corners of a fixed device geometry. This spatial reconfiguration yields a control-correlated conductance response. Across these configurations, the quantized zero-bias peak appears at the contacted corner in the ideal tunneling model when an MCM is present and is suppressed when it is absent. This correlation connects phase and magnetic control of corner configurations with local tunneling readout.

papers.title_en: Are neutrinos Majorana? Fixed-target and high-energy astrophysical searches decide
papers.abstract_en: The original version of this paper proposed a new approach to determining whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana fermions, a fundamental open question in particle physics. Conventional searches rely on neutrinoless double beta decay, but this electron-only channel suffers from blind spots. We propose a new, complementary probe to overcome this limitation. A heavy neutral lepton (HNL) triggers a high-energy shift in how the active neutrino flavors ($ν_e$, $ν_μ$, $ν_τ$) mix---but only if the neutrinos are Majorana. For GeV-scale HNLs, the upcoming beam-dump experiment SHiP can discover the HNL and measure how it mixes with the active flavors. However, the proposed signature of the Majorana nature of neutrinos does not exist. The reasons are explained here. The analysis has been superseded by Ref.~\cite{Barenboim:2026udr}. The original version is retained as v1 for the record.

papers.title_en: Two-component $γ$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
papers.abstract_en: With the advent of a new generation of observational experiments and the accumulation of data, an increasing number of cosmic-ray sources have been found to exhibit pronounced two-component structures in their gamma-ray spectra above GeV energies. To investigate whether these structures share a common physical origin, we conduct a statistical study of sources exhibiting such features using a two-component model of cosmic-ray sources and examine their gamma-ray emission mechanisms. We find that the ambient environment significantly affects the spectral morphology. Sources located in low-density environments but surrounded by dense molecular clumps exhibit two clearly separated spectral peaks. In contrast, sources embedded in dense environments with additional dense molecular clumps nearby retain two-component spectral features, but the components overlap more smoothly, with the high-energy component appearing primarily as a relatively broad shoulder rather than a distinct peak. Our results lend further support to a physical picture in which high-energy cosmic rays are predominantly supplied by local sources, whereas low-energy cosmic rays arise mainly from the collective contribution of sources in other regions of the Galaxy. We also calculate the neutrino spectra of these sources, providing theoretical predictions for future tests of the model through observations of point-source and diffuse neutrino emission.

papers.title_en: Nonunitary Quantum Criticality Driven by a General Boundary Condition: Exact Solution
papers.abstract_en: Nonunitary quantum critical phenomena remain largely unexplored, hindered by the scarcity of exactly solvable models and the numerical challenges in non-Hermitian systems. Here we demonstrate that a general boundary condition drives fundamentally new nonunitary boundary quantum criticality in an exactly solvable lattice model. The exact solution yields a closed-form expression for the boundary-induced equal-time correlation function. The algebraic long-distance behavior of the boundary-induced correlation is governed by the single-particle reflection amplitude at the Fermi level, whose anomalous amplification is forbidden in unitary scattering and therefore provides a direct scattering signature of the nonunitary boundary-critical regime. We use the biorthogonal entanglement entropy as a many-body probe of this boundary-critical behavior and find that it retains logarithmic scaling, while the associated effective central charge, continuously tunable by the boundary parameters, changes from real to complex. The real branch admits a unitary defect conformal field theory (CFT) description, whereas the complex branch lies beyond analytic continuation from the unitary theory. These results establish minimal boundary engineering as an exactly solvable platform for nonunitary boundary quantum criticality and provide a benchmark for broader studies of nonunitary critical phenomena.

papers.title_en: Particle-hole asymmetry and a fluctuating pair-density-wave state in a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice
papers.abstract_en: Whether a lightly doped Mott insulator on the square lattice supports robust $d$-wave superconductivity remains a central question in strongly correlated physics and in the microscopic theory of cuprate superconductivity. Experiments and numerical studies reveal a pronounced particle-hole asymmetry, pointing to a delicate competition among $d$-wave superconductivity, pair-density wave (PDW), stripe, charge-density wave (CDW), and antiferromagnetic correlations. Here we combine large-scale DMRG and finite-size PEPS to study the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at low doping, $δ\leq 0.1$, while tuning the next-nearest-neighbor hopping $t'$ from the electron-like ($t'>0$) to the hole-like ($t'<0$) regime. The electron-like side supports robust, nearly uniform $d$-wave pairing, whereas decreasing $t'$ induces a period-two plaquette modulation and ultimately produces, on the hole-like side, a charge-dominated state with a strongly suppressed static pairing amplitude. DMRG calculations on open strips and squares, together with PEPS calculations on open squares up to $16\times16$ sites, support this evolution. On squares with $C_4$-symmetric Hamiltonians, both methods find that the pair correlations of the hole-like state select the plaquette momenta $(π,0)$ and $(0,π)$ and decay within a few lattice spacings, while the dominant charge-density modulation forms a bidirectional checkerboard whose period extrapolates to about $4a_0$, close to that observed in lightly doped Bi-2201. These observations establish a fluctuating plaquette PDW in the lightly doped hole-like regime, in which local pairs carry finite momentum but lack phase coherence. Our results firmly establish particle-hole asymmetry as a central organizing principle for competing pairing tendencies in the lightly doped $t$-$J$ model.

papers.title_en: Cosmic String Networks with Time-Varying Tension: Field-Theory Simulations and an Analytic Model
papers.abstract_en: Cosmic string networks are predicted in some early-Universe scenarios, and in certain models, the string tension becomes a function of time. Here, for the first time, we perform numerical field-theory simulations of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension in an expanding Universe. We use a modified Abelian-Higgs model in which the tension varies as a power law of the scale factor $a$, that is, $μ\propto a^{-2m}$. We perform simulations on grids containing $8192^3$ grid points, with $m\in[-0.5,0.5]$, during radiation- and matter-dominated epochs. We find that, in our model, a string network forms only when the potential decreases more slowly than the amplitude of field oscillations redshifts due to the expansion of the Universe. Once formed, the network evolves according to the standard scaling behavior predicted by the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model. To interpret these results, we compare the predictions of the VOS model with time-dependent tension to the asymptotic values obtained from the numerical simulations. Overall, we find good agreement between the numerical field-theory simulations and the calibrated VOS model. These results shed light on the evolution of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension and have potential implications for their observational signatures.

papers.title_en: Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
papers.abstract_en: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states support fractionalized excitations and geometric phases, yet experimentally resolving the many-body coherence encoded in their wave functions remains challenging. Here, we prepare a three-electron $ν=1/3$ Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere using seven superconducting qubits and reconstruct its many-body density matrix. Through Read's composite-boson construction, we reveal vortex-dressed coherence that remains appreciable over a larger separation range than electron coherence. The extended profile is suppressed in a Fock-diagonal reference constructed from the measured populations, demonstrating its dependence on off-diagonal many-body coherence. We further prepare a one-flux-added quasihole and characterize its fractional charge response against finite-size benchmarks. Controlled quasihole motion yields an effective geometric-phase signature from the reconstructed dominant-eigenstate trajectory. These complementary measurements provide microscopic access to the coherent structure and quasihole response of a finite fermionic Laughlin state, demonstrating an experimental route to probing strongly correlated FQH wave functions on programmable quantum processors.

papers.title_en: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
papers.abstract_en: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.

papers.title_en: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
papers.abstract_en: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

papers.title_en: Local electronic structure of the Co2+ ions in the disordered perovskite phase of Ba3CoNb2O9: a temperature-dependent X-ray absorption and magnetic circular dichroism study
papers.abstract_en: We performed temperature-dependent X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) measurements on the disordered phase of Ba$_3$CoNb$_2$O$_9$ to determine the local electronic structure of the Co$^{2+}$ ions. We employed the line-fitting inverse partial fluorescence yield (iPFY) method to obtain reliable spectra from this insulating material. From the comparison between the experimental spectra and full multiplet cluster calculations we were able to constrain the local crystal-field environment and assess the spin-orbit-entangled nature of the Co$^{2+}$ ground state. In this chemically disordered system, the Co$^{2+}$ ions retain on average an effectively cubic crystal-field environment that supports a $J_\mathrm{eff} = 1/2$ ground state. These results further establish that Ba$_3$CoNb$_2$O$_9$ is a promising platform for investigating the effect of disorder on $J_\mathrm{eff} = 1/2$ magnetism.

papers.title_en: Small-instanton effects in an atlas of Kim-Shifman-Vainshtein-Zakharov axion models
papers.abstract_en: We investigate small-instanton contributions to the axion potential across a range of KSVZ models containing vector-like quarks~(VQs), using naive dimensional analysis. We consider scenarios containing a single VQ, multiple identical copies, and sets of distinct VQs, requiring in each case that the gauge couplings remain perturbative up to the Planck scale under the two-loop gauge running. The associated fermion zero-mode content varies between these cases, requiring different combinations of mass insertions and scalar--Yukawa contractions for its saturation. Increasing the copies of VQs can render the instanton-size integral dominated by instantons of the smallest size, corresponding to the scale near the ultraviolet~(UV) cut-off. The resulting contribution then becomes sensitive to the UV completion and the induced potential can compete with, or dominate over, the ordinary QCD contribution. Assuming that the QCD and small-instanton potentials are aligned, we determine the resulting axion-mass shift and its consequences for the axion--photon coupling. When the small-instanton induced susceptibility becomes comparable to or larger than the QCD susceptibility, the physical axion mass of $m_a$ is enhanced at fixed decay constant~$f_a$, while the axion-photon of $g_{aγγ}$ coupling remains controlled by $f_a$ and the anomaly ratio of $E/N$. The standard QCD relation among $m_a$, $f_a$ and $g_{aγγ}$ is consequently modified, opening new regions of the $(m_a,g_{aγγ})$ plane for axion searches.

papers.title_en: Evidence of anomalous Hall crystals in moiré rhombohedral graphene
papers.abstract_en: An anomalous Hall crystal (AHC) is a quantum state of matter, in which spontaneous electron crystallization leads to a quantized Hall effect without a magnetic field. The state can emerge in materials with strong Coulomb interaction and large Berry curvatures, such as few-layer rhombohedral graphene. Although the idea of AHCs has been invoked to explain some of the observed Chern insulators in moiré rhombohedral graphene (mRG), direct experimental evidence of AHCs has been missing so far. Here, we report experimental evidence of AHCs in hole-doped mRG through combined electrical transport and noise measurements. We identify a series of distinct Chern insulators spanning a broad and continuous range of doping densities incommensurate with the underlying moiré lattice; the states exhibit current-induced broadband noise and memory effects as well as pronounced gate hysteresis. Systematic magnetic field, temperature and gate dependence studies further support the emergence of a spontaneously charge-ordered state that acts as a parental state for the observed Chern insulators. The absence of Chern insulators at nearby integer fillings also distinguishes the observed state from the reported reentrant or extended quantum (anomalous) Hall states. Altogether, our results establish experimental evidence of AHCs in mRG and open the door for further exploration of the collective dynamics in this new state of matter.

papers.title_en: Tunable quantum Mpemba effect in long-range interacting systems
papers.abstract_en: Symmetry plays a fundamental role in many-body systems, both in and out of equilibrium. The quantum Mpemba effect (QME) -- a phenomenon where systems initially farther from equilibrium can thermalize faster -- can be understood in terms of how rapidly a symmetry, broken by initial conditions, is dynamically restored. In this work, we study the QME in a one-dimensional spin-1/2 XYZ model with power-law decaying interactions in the presence of a magnetic field. In the prethermal regime generated by large field strengths, the system develops a continuous U(1) symmetry, enabling the QME to emerge. However, due to the Hohenberg-Mermin-Wagner theorem, the QME can only arise when interactions are sufficiently short-ranged. This leads to an interplay between the external field, interaction range, and dynamical symmetry restoration. We systematically explore this interplay and analyze the dependence of the QME on the effective temperature set by the initial state. Our results demonstrate the tunability of the QME via long-range interactions, which can be probed in experimental platforms of trapped ions, polar molecules, and NV centers.

papers.title_en: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays require metal-rich sources
papers.abstract_en: The elemental composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) must be evaluated at a given rigidity rather than energy to compare with candidate elemental abundances, such as those of low-energy cosmic rays seeding the acceleration of UHECRs. We determine the UHECR composition from fits to Pierre Auger Observatory data and evaluate the resulting abundances at fixed rigidity. We identify two classes of solutions consistent with measurements above $10^{17.8}$ eV: one in which the hydrogen flux at Earth is dominated by secondary nucleons produced by photodisintegration of heavier nuclei in extragalactic photon fields, and a second in which this contribution is less pronounced. Only the latter, which yields a mixture of primary and secondary protons at Earth, allows a hydrogen abundance at the source comparable to that of low-energy cosmic rays. However, both classes of solutions require an overabundance of nuclei in the silicon-iron group. Other source models from the literature also fail to reproduce the full elemental composition. The metallicity of UHECRs thus differs markedly from that of all candidate seed populations considered, leaving the origin of the heavy-element excess unresolved.

papers.title_en: Gravitational Origin of Black Hole Thermodynamic Geometry from Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract_en: In black hole thermodynamics, Hessian metrics change both their signature and their singularities from one statistical ensemble to another. A negative eigenvalue may therefore signal either a physical instability or only a Legendre transformation. We derive this geometry from the bulk action and boundary terms of four-dimensional Euclidean Einstein-Maxwell-anti-de Sitter gravity. In the bulk, the radial symplectic flux pairs the mass and charge with their asymptotic sources, and horizon regularity selects the equilibrium states. At infinity, the boundary terms determine the ensemble polarization by specifying which reservoir parameters are held constant and which conjugate quantities fluctuate. Fixing the temperature and electric potential gives the Ruppeiner metric, whereas adding the Maxwell boundary term fixes the charge and reverses the corresponding metric sign. Tracking the boundary conditions thus separates true stability boundaries from singularities of the Legendre transform.
