We find that $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and the very existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are tightly controlled by $g$ and the dyonic charges: increasing $g$ or pushing the charges toward extremality raises $σ_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and shrinks the CA-active part of the ergoregion. Unlike Kerr, the spin enters through the normalization factor $Ξ$, and the quartic horizon function $Δ_g$, so geometric effects from the AdS/NUT deformation dominate the usual frame-dragging enhancement. As a result, the extracted power and efficiency are non-monotonic in $a$ and peak at intermediate spin ($a\sim0.8$); near-extremal rotation is not required for high efficiency, provided $g$ is small and $Q$ is moderate. Efficient extraction further demands extreme magnetization and nearly radial outflows, confining the active reconnection layer to a thin shell, just outside the horizon.

papers.title_en: Monodromy Defects and Bulk Renormalization Group Flows on the Fuzzy Sphere
papers.abstract_en: A monodromy around a defect specifies a symmetry transformation, but the low energy properties of the defect depend on its interaction with bulk degrees of freedom and also itself. We study this dependence on the fuzzy sphere. Along an anisotropy flow, an $O(3)$ half-twist approaches the $O(2)$ half-twist when its twisted components stay light and disappears when they become massive. At large $N$, untwisted spectators give a positive correction to the defect entropy, fixed by the conformal weight of the free defect. The surviving $O(2)$ monodromy admits a relevant charged perturbation that pins the line. Pinning before or after the easy-plane bulk flow gives matching infrared junction data. A pin of the untwisted component survives only the opposite, easy-axis flow. Walls between opposite pinnings test the stability of the candidate ordered line. They are relevant on the pinned $O(2)$ monodromy lines studied and favoured to be relevant, with a smaller margin, on the ordinary $O(2)$ line, while the ordinary $O(3)$ and $O(4)$ walls lie close to marginality. We separate the wall dimension into a tilt stiffness and an angular shape, comparing them with a Ward identity, a two-loop expansion and a large-$N$ saddle. In the fully twisted large-$N$ model, winding weakens the condensate and lowers the wall dimension and the entropy released by pinning. The resulting entropy comparison permits disordering into the unpinned line wherever the leading wall estimate is relevant. Finally, we construct the regular half-twist on the fuzzy four-sphere as a starting point for analogous questions in five dimensions.

papers.title_en: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
papers.abstract_en: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection, thermalization and decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The results recover analytical predictions and published benchmarks and demonstrate agreement across numerical schemes. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

papers.title_en: Variational Approach to the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon Equations of Motion for Extended Objects in General Relativity
papers.abstract_en: The exact motion of a finite size object in curved spacetime is captured by the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations. They associate a unique worldline, momentum, and spin to that object and determine the evolution of such in terms of its fully independent multipole moments. We provide a thorough review of this theory and show how to build it directly via a manifestly gauge invariant variational principle well-suited for effective descriptions of relativistic compact objects. We discuss conditions under which the covariant spin supplementary condition can be enforced and identify the natural basis of curvature tensors conjugate to the object's multipole moments.

papers.title_en: The Energy-Momentum Tensor of a Compact Object in General Relativity to all Multipole Orders
papers.abstract_en: In effective field theory approaches to compact object motion in general relativity, spin and tidal effects are encoded by operators formed from the Riemann tensor and its derivatives. Many such operators contribute degenerately to observables, with a single one often affecting several multipole moments of the body. Using the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon formalism, we construct a natural basis of independent tensors which are each canonically conjugate to precisely one multipole. We find the novel exact distributional formula for the energy-momentum tensor of a compact object in terms of its reduced multipole moments and these tensors.

papers.title_en: Radial Oscillations of Viscous Stars at Finite Temperature
papers.abstract_en: We study the radial oscillation spectrum of relativistic stars within Israel-Stewart and Navier-Stokes theories, extending previous analyses to include heat diffusion and a thermodynamically consistent finite-temperature equation of state. The inclusion of heat flux gives rise to a distinct thermal sector in the mode spectrum, whose structure closely mirrors the dispersion relations of an infinite dissipative fluid. Within Israel-Stewart theory, the thermal modes transition from purely damped to propagating behavior above a critical overtone number, providing a finite-size realization of relativistic second sound in compact stars. Remarkably, the finite stellar geometry can push even the fundamental thermal mode into the propagating regime -- a feature with no continuum analogue. For the class of equations of state considered here, where finite-temperature corrections enter as controlled, Sommerfeld-type perturbations of a cold polytrope, the thermal sector couples only weakly to the ordinary fluid oscillation spectrum, with the coupling being of second order in a suitable temperature parameter. We further show that the discrete stellar spectrum is well captured by an analytic ansatz constructed from the flat-spacetime dispersion relations, with the star's finite radius discretizing the continuous mode structure. Our results complete the analysis of radial oscillations of viscous stars by incorporating the last remaining dissipative degree of freedom within the Israel-Stewart framework.

papers.title_en: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract_en: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(δt)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $κ(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.

papers.title_en: Stochastic Acceleration Downstream of Astrophysical Shocks
papers.abstract_en: Generation and evolution of turbulence at shock fronts are crucial aspects of the process of particle acceleration in different classes of sources. Here we aim at describing the fate of non-thermal particles and turbulence in the downstream region of an astrophysical shock, both in the case in which turbulence is solely produced upstream and advected through the shock and in the case in which additional turbulence is injected downstream. In particular we will provide an estimate of the effect of stochastic acceleration on particles accelerated at the shock and then advected behind it. The calculations will be specialized to supernova remnant shocks. The temporal evolution of the particle distribution function downstream of the shock and the power spectrum of the turbulent perturbations are both followed by solving numerically the transport equations for the two quantities, accounting for the damping of waves due to the particles that resonantly interact with them, which makes the problem non-linear. Our calculations show that, if waves are only self-generated upstream via Bell instability, they are not able to significantly modify the particle spectrum in the downstream region. Additionally, turbulent cascading in $k$-space quickly drains their energy, further limiting the stochastic acceleration of particles. If, on the other hand, there are additional sources of turbulence downstream, then these waves can contribute meaningfully to second order Fermi acceleration and alter the spectrum of particles. This may reflect in the spectrum of gamma radiation produced through $pp$ scattering downstream. Although second order Fermi acceleration is typically slower than diffusive shock acceleration, particles are expected to stay downstream of shocks for much longer times during which stochastic acceleration can modify their spectrum and affect the spectra of multi-messenger emissions.

papers.title_en: Configurational Information and Hadron Spectroscopy in Holographic QCD
papers.abstract_en: Based on the concepts of entropy and complexity, Configurational Information Measures (CIMs) are tools capable of extracting information regarding physical systems from their spatially localized energy density, determining properties such as stability limits and phase transitions. In this thesis, CIMs are employed to investigate hadron spectroscopy. By utilizing phenomenological AdS/QCD models in conjunction with CIMs, cataloged meson and baryon resonances are interpolated into structures analogous to Regge trajectories, from which analytical expressions are derived to estimate the masses of higher-order excited states. These estimates are compared with experimental data to search for possible correspondences that may elucidate the properties of particles that have been experimentally detected but remain unidentified. Using this CIM-based AdS/QCD hybrid method, this work analyzes light mesons within a dynamical model, strange vector kaons in a framework that accounts for constituent quark masses, and light-flavor baryons at finite temperature.

papers.title_en: Breathing mode of quantum droplets in dipolar quantum gases: A sum-rule analysis
papers.abstract_en: We investigate theoretically the ground-state properties and breathing-mode collective excitations of three-dimensional dipolar Bose gases in anisotropic harmonic traps incorporating quantum fluctuations. Combining a Gaussian variational ansatz with a sum-rule analysis, we derive explicit analytical expressions for both axial and radial breathing-mode frequencies, which are validated by numerical solutions of the time-dependent extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation. Our theoretical predictions show great agreement with existing experimental data for $^{166}$Er and $^{162}$Dy gases. By constructing comprehensive phase diagrams across the parameter space of the $s$-wave scattering length, atom number, and trap aspect ratio, we reveal both discontinuous first-order phase transitions and smooth crossovers between the dilute Bose-Einstein condensate and dense quantum droplet phases. We confirm that the enhanced incompressibility induced by quantum fluctuations significantly elevates the breathing-mode frequencies in the droplet phase compared with conventional weakly interacting Bose gases. Furthermore, the system undergoes a phase transition and a crossover over the scattering length under the elongated and flattened confinements, characterized by discontinuous jumps and continuous crossovers in peak density and atomic cloud sizes, respectively. Our work offers a useful analytical framework to characterize collective excitations in dipolar quantum gases, providing quantitative insights for forthcoming ultracold atom experiments in lanthanide atoms and polar molecules.

papers.title_en: Pair size versus coherence length and quantum geometry in the spin-orbit coupled BCS-BEC crossover
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the interplay between pairing correlations and quantum geometry in the spin-orbit-coupled BCS-BEC crossover. Working in the helicity basis, we derive the exact pair-size tensor for the two-body bound states and show that it separates into an intraband contribution and a quantum-geometric interband contribution governed by the quantum metric. We extend this decomposition to two distinct many-body length scales at zero temperature: the Cooper-pair size from mean-field BCS theory and the coherence length from Gaussian fluctuation theory. Although the two almost coincide in the BCS regime, the former measures the internal extent of a pair while the latter measures the long-wavelength response of the order parameter. Evaluating both for three-dimensional Rashba, three-dimensional Weyl, and two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit couplings, we find that the pair size decreases monotonically with spin-orbit coupling, whereas the coherence length develops a pronounced minimum, associated with the collapse of the noninteracting Fermi surface onto the ring or sphere of helicity-band minima, before growing again as the composite bosons become weakly interacting. The quantum-geometric contributions reach up to about 30\% of the squared pair size and squared coherence length, tracking the same changes in the helicity Fermi-surface topology.

papers.title_en: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
papers.abstract_en: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordström (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, arising as an exact solution of Einstein gravity. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. We provide several exact completions of this geometry with finite Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) mass. Focusing on the original logarithmic geometry, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Padé approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.

papers.title_en: Klein bottle ratio of two-dimensional ferromagnetic Potts models
papers.abstract_en: The weakly first-order nature of the two-dimensional five-state ferromagnetic Potts model poses challenges for numerical study. Using density-matrix and tensor-network renormalization group methods, we investigate these transitions of the $q$-state Potts model via the Klein bottle ratio $g$ on original and dual lattices. Finite-size scaling of $g$ as a function of transverse system size $L_y$ accurately locates the critical points for $q = 3, 4, 5, 6$. We further examine the transfer-matrix spectra and entanglement entropy, extracting central charges through toroidal and Klein bottle boundary conditions. For $q = 5$, the extracted central charge ($c \approx 1.14811$) is close to the real part of the theoretical value $c_{5\text{-Potts}} = 1.1375 \pm 0.0211 i$ predicted by complex conformal field theories(CFTs). The observed drift in the scaling exponent $b$ effectively distinguishes the continuous transition from the weakly first-order regime. Furthermore, the extrapolated divergence of $g$ confirms the first-order character of the $q=5$ Potts model, while for the $q=4$ model, both the CFT-predicted eigenvalue distribution and the logarithmic corrections are numerically verified.

papers.title_en: Probing the origin of the LHAASO Peanut with a hidden central accelerator
papers.abstract_en: A highly asymmetric, giant Peanut-shaped structure has been detected by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) in ultra-high-energy gamma rays at high Galactic latitude, $b\approx-17.5^{\circ}$, suggesting anisotropic particle transport around a Galactic accelerator. We investigate whether its spectrum and morphology can arise from a hidden central accelerator embedded in a projected anisotropic halo. The baseline model accounts for the diffuse strip and central excess, while a phenomenological prescription for a localized magnetic field reorientation toward the line of sight (LOS), together with a particle-conserved remapping of the electrons downstream of the far excess into an emitting column of prescribed transverse extent, enhances the emission at the far excess position. We explore various source ages, along with different combinations of ambient magnetic field strength and parallel diffusion coefficient, while accounting for radiative cooling when estimating the viewing geometry. The exploration reveals that relatively rapid parallel transport enhances the far component while preserving a dominant diffuse strip. Representative configurations remain compatible with the observed spectral energy distribution, although the fitted far component remains comparatively weaker than the central component above 100 TeV, even in cases where their component fluxes are comparable at 25-100 TeV. These results illustrate the plausibility of a hidden central accelerator as the origin of the LHAASO Peanut, while identifying the remaining difficulty in reproducing the relative brightness of its compact components within the adopted phenomenological framework.

papers.title_en: Charge-Activated Birefringence and Shadow Mimicry around Reissner-Nordström Black Holes
papers.abstract_en: We discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the Einstein tensor around a Reissner-Nordström black hole. Changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. The coupling makes the two parity looks differently. It separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. However changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. They require both nonzero charge and coupling. At weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. Positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. Negative coupling reverses these trends. The backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. It is entirely helicity reversed. For the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. We can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. A comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.

papers.title_en: Sub-Thouless energy scale in interface-dominated unconventional superconductor junctions
papers.abstract_en: We derive the conductance in unconventional superconductor - normal metal - normal metal junctions, taking into account the resistance between the normal metals. We show that applying Tanaka--Nazarov boundary conditions at both superconductor and normal metal interfaces reveals a new characteristic low-energy scale which is sub-Thouless in the experimentally relevant strong-interface regime. This scale governs, among other quantities, the curvature of the local density of states (LDOS) and the width of conductance dips near the zero-bias conductance peak in triplet superconductor junctions, thereby replacing the Thouless energy as the dominant low-energy parameter. We derive universal $s$-wave proximitized diffusive metal expressions for the zero-bias LDOS and differential conductance which solely depend on the interface and bulk resistances, independent of the superconducting gap and Thouless energy scale. This framework provides a possible origin of the anomalous low-bias conductance features observed in unconventional superconductors, offering a refined mechanism for interpreting interface and correlated electron physics in experimental hybrid junctions.

papers.title_en: Identifying Contributions to the Superconducting Diode Effect through Nonreciprocal Superconducting Properties
papers.abstract_en: Nonreciprocal superconducting responses provide a sensitive probe of superconducting states in systems where inversion and time-reversal symmetries are broken. However, in the superconducting diode effect (SDE), where the critical current differs for opposite current directions, nonreciprocity can also arise from vortex-induced contributions caused by minute magnetic field misalignment, complicating its interpretation. Here, we investigate a noncentrosymmetric $[Nb/V/Ta]_{40}$ superlattice and demonstrate nonreciprocity in all three fundamental superconducting properties: the critical current, critical field, and superconducting transition temperature. By measuring the angular dependence of the nonreciprocal critical field $ΔB_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, we separate the contribution of misalignment-induced out-of-plane vortices from the in-plane response. We identify a sharply enhanced SDE emerging near $B_{\mathrm{c} 2}$, accompanied by nonreciprocal responses in $T_{\mathrm{c}}$. These observations exhibit phenomenology similar to that reported in layered superconductors, where an orbital-FFLO state with finite-momentum Cooper pairing has been reported. Our results establish a protocol for assessing out-of-plane vortex contributions to the superconducting diode effect and demonstrate that nonreciprocal responses provide complementary probes of unconventional superconducting states.

papers.title_en: Quadrature magnetoresistance scaling reflects linear field dependence rather than strange metallicity of high-temperature superconductors
papers.abstract_en: The quadrature scaling of magnetoresistance has been widely adopted as a hallmark of the strange metal state. However, whether this scaling signals quantum criticality or reflects conventional transport behavior remains controversial. Here, by systematically investigating the magnetotransport properties of NiTe2 nanosheets, we demonstrate that the quadrature scaling is not a unique signature of strange metallicity. We find that the scaling holds only when the crossover field Bc, marking the transition from quadratic to linear magnetoresistance, is sufficiently small relative to the applied field range. Through controlled simulations, we show that the scaling emerges whenever linear magnetoresistance dominates, irrespective of its origin, and fails when the linear regime is inaccessible. This conclusion is supported by observations in SrTiO3 based heterostructures, where quadrature scaling appears despite the absence of strange metal behavior. Our results establish that the quadrature scaling merely reflects the presence of linear magneto resistance, urging caution in using this scaling as a diagnostic tool for exploring the strange metal state.

papers.title_en: Self-bound quantum dark fermion stars: saturation, a coupling-capped maximum mass, and tidal signatures of a vector dark sector
papers.abstract_en: I show that a dark sector whose fermions couple to both a scalar and a vector mediator saturates in close analogy with nuclear matter: the energy per particle develops a minimum at finite density, cold dark matter of this kind is self-bound, and its stars, computed here in full general relativity, possess the sharp surfaces of strange quark stars. Saturation makes the maximum stellar mass a property of the Lagrangian rather than an inheritance of the Chandrasekhar scaling: it rises eightfold across the saturation window, which a critical vector coupling closes, so the theory caps its own maximum mass, at $3.9\,M_\odot$ for a fermion of $1\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and the fiducial saturation density, a ceiling shared by the whole family of couplings rather than by any single parameter set. Metastable couplings support two disconnected stable families, one dilute and gravitationally bound, the other dense and self-bound. The quantum-pressure correction, confined by saturation to a surface layer a few Compton wavelengths thick, governs the smallest dark nuggets whilst shifting stellar masses by less than one part in $10^{21}$. A $1.4\,M_\odot$ member of the fiducial family has a radius of $13.3\,\mathrm{km}$, a compactness of $0.155$, and a tidal deformability of $1.6\times 10^{3}$, almost an order of magnitude above the measured neutron-star value, so at a given particle mass and couplings a single well-measured inspiral distinguishes these stars from neutron stars and from their scalar-only counterparts, whilst the deformability surviving at the maximum mass separates them, in principle, from black holes.

papers.title_en: Black-hole ringdown at an exceptional point
papers.abstract_en: Black holes ring in damped oscillations. At an exceptional point, photon-sphere and near-horizon modes merge, and their response can acquire a linear time factor. We compute its amplitude from constrained Einstein-Maxwell data for a rotating, charged black hole in de Sitter space. With seven competing modes fixed, the late-time curvature error is 0.00383$\%$ for the pair and 0.01401$\%$ for a refitted exponential. We suppress the linear term by tuning the initial disturbance at fixed geometry. Hence, near coalescence, changing only the initial disturbance can shift the frequency inferred from a short ringdown fit.

papers.title_en: Strong Collective Dynamics Hidden behind a Nearly Free Single-Particle Spectrum
papers.abstract_en: Single-particle spectroscopy has long served as a criterion for the strength of electronic correlations: strong collective motion is expected to shift and broaden spectral peaks and to renormalize the dispersion. Here we show that this correspondence can fail on the same microscopic orbital. The mechanism relies on local interference between two resonant side orbitals: one suppresses low-energy real transitions into the interacting environment, while the other suppresses spectral-weight backflow to the source orbital; virtual mixing nevertheless transfers the environmental spin polarization to the source. We prove a rigorous relative spectral bound that is uniform in environment size and interaction strength and holds for arbitrary stationary states; the protection becomes stronger as the relative frequency resolution improves. In a fully quantum two-cell device, a collective mode softens by 60%, whereas the particle intensity at the free peak changes by only 3.6 parts per million. Quantum Monte Carlo shows that the transferred spin response grows with spatial correlations and is quantitatively predicted by the free-band polarization. These results recast the meaning of a simple particle spectrum and provide a design principle for quantum probes that combine predictable particle spectra with strong collective sensitivity.

papers.title_en: Axion Quality in Warped Extra-Dimension
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the axion quality problem in warped extra-dimensional models in which the QCD axion arises as the Wilson-line mode of a five-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge field compactified on an $S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold. Higher-dimensional gauge invariance severely constrains possible sources of Peccei--Quinn symmetry breaking, implying that non-QCD contributions to the axion potential are predominantly generated by nonlocal effects mediated by $U(1)$-charged fields propagating along the compact dimension. We systematically compute these contributions and examine how both the warped geometry and the orbifold fixed points (branes) affect the resulting axion quality. Finally, we classify the parametric suppression of the induced axion potential, thereby identifying the conditions under which warped extra-dimensional axions can achieve sufficiently high quality.

papers.title_en: Ferromagnetic resonance signatures of edge states for distinguishing chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors
papers.abstract_en: We theoretically investigate ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) modulation at interfaces between ferromagnetic insulators and two-dimensional chiral and helical $p$-wave superconductors. We evaluate the surface dynamical spin susceptibility, including both edge and bulk quasiparticle excitations. For momentum-conserving interfacial exchange at zero temperature, the edge contribution to the Gilbert damping exhibits distinct frequency scalings for the excitation energies well above the spectral broadening, $\hbarω\gg2δ$: $δ/(\hbarω)^{2}$ for the chiral state and $1/\hbarω$ for the helical state. For a clean superconducting boundary, edge-induced Ising spin anisotropy persists even when interfacial exchange disorder randomizes momentum transfer. The low-energy edge response is suppressed when the magnetization aligns with the edge-state spin axis. These results establish FMR modulation as a probe complementary to existing methods for distinguishing the chiral and helical states and constraining their $d$-vector directions.

papers.title_en: Scalar-tensor reconstruction of coherent quantum black holes
papers.abstract_en: We construct a scalar-tensor realisation of spherically symmetric black hole geometries that effectively arise from quantum coherent states characterised by a finite core and finite extension. We determine the non-minimal coupling to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian, kinetic coupling, and scalar potential and show that the kinetic term is positive only in finite domains. For fixed black hole mass, the boundaries of these domains provide a natural mechanism that relates the core size and spatial extension to the dynamics of the scalar-tensor realisation. We further show that the same geometry can also be obtained from a Horndeski action with derivative coupling and determine its domain of validity. Neither reconstruction includes the event horizon nor can it simultaneously reproduce arbitrarily large portions of the interior and exterior of the black hole, whose quantum origin therefore appears to remain partially outside the regime of applicability of semiclassical theories of gravity.

papers.title_en: Generalized Second Law of Thermodynamics in $f(Q)$ Symmetric Teleparallel Gravity
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the validity of the generalized second law (GSL) of thermodynamics on the cosmological apparent horizon in $f(Q)$ symmetric teleparallel gravity, using the Wald-type entropy prefactor $Af_Q/4G$ together with a correction term derived directly from the modified Friedmann equations. We derive, and verify by explicit symbolic computation, a closed-form expression for the apparent horizon entropy in $f(Q)$ gravity and show that its time derivative combines with the matter entropy rate into a remarkably compact master formula, $T_A\dot S_{\rm tot} = 4π\dot H(\dot H f_Q + H\dot f_Q)/H^4$ (in units $8πG=1$), which correctly reduces to the known general-relativistic limit. We apply this formalism to three observationally viable $f(Q)$ models --- power-law, exponential, and logarithmic. We find that the GSL is satisfied throughout cosmic history for all three models, and relate this robustness to a general, theory-independent structural condition: for ordinary pressureless matter obeying the null energy condition, GSL validity reduces to the sign of $\dot H$, i.e., to the absence of a phantom crossing in the total effective expansion history. The geometric sector exhibits model-dependent energy conditions, power-law and exponential models violate only the strong condition, while the logarithmic model violates the null, weak, and dominant conditions for \(z>-1\), and the strong condition for \(z<3.84\).

papers.title_en: Data augmentation by an electro-vibratory feedback improves signal interpretation by neural networks
papers.abstract_en: Data-driven machine learning algorithms represent an alternative to numerical or analytical modeling of vibrating objects for the purpose of extracting their material or geometric properties. Their performance is conditioned by the quality of the training dataset, which should contain all possible production configurations of the object and measurement conditions. In this work, we propose a data-augmentation method based on manipulations of the vibration properties rather than numerical signal post-processing. Instead of modifying the sample’s material or geometry, we connect an additional sensor and actuator to the sample and use low-latency electronics to control the feedback signal. This delivers an electromechanical system with tunable oscillation properties. This signal diversification method is demonstrated on the classification of correct and incorrect adhesion of two aluminum plates. The labeling accuracy of 67% on nine unknown test objects, when trained on a single unchangeable training object, increases to 83% when the variety of the training vibration signals is augmented by varying the parameters of the electrovibratory feedback. This provides advantages for industrial quality control, where a large number of reference training samples are not available.

papers.title_en: Development of Silicon Photo-Multiplier (SiPM) detectors for Muon Scattering Tomography
u-d Quark Matter in the Enhanced pQCD Model and u-d Quark Stars in Gravity’s Rainbow
papers.abstract_en:
Recent studies have revealed that two-flavor u-d quark matter may serve as the true ground state of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Meanwhile, a growing number of supermassive compact stars have been detected observationally, which brings severe challenges to explaining the internal matter composition of these compact objects. In this work, we systematically explore the parameter stability window of u-d quark matter within the enhanced perturbative QCD (EpQCD) model, and further investigate the structural properties of u-d quark stars under the framework of gravity’s rainbow theory.
By constructing a well-defined renormalization subtraction point, the EpQCD model successfully eliminates the thermodynamic inconsistency plaguing conventional perturbative QCD, and partially incorporates the global effect of quark confinement into the theoretical framework. As a quantum gravity candidate, gravity’s rainbow theory can effectively modify gravitational interactions inside compact stars via tuning rainbow function parameters, which provides a feasible theoretical scheme to account for extremely massive compact stars.
The left panel illustrates the stability window of u-d quark matter, while the right panel displays the mass-radius relation of u-d quark stars derived from gravity’s rainbow. The stability diagram indicates that the green stable parameter region is far narrower than the forbidden and phase-transition zones, yet absolute stable u-d quark matter is still theoretically achievable. Selecting representative parameters from the stable region, we compute the equilibrium structure of u-d quark stars and find that the maximum stellar mass rises monotonically with the rainbow function parameter Σ. Under the limit of standard general relativity (Ξ = Σ = 1), the maximum mass of a u-d quark star reaches 2.34 M⊙. Notably, when Σ = 1.2, the peak mass climbs to approximately 2.8 M⊙, consistent with the mass range of the compact companion in the GW190814 gravitational-wave event. Our results provide a novel perspective to interpret the intrinsic nature of ultra-massive compact stars, and advance our physical insights into the low-energy regime of quantum gravity.

papers.title_en: ESC Enables Protection of an Accelerator Superconducting Magnet With -5 kA/mm- Copper Current Density
papers.abstract_en: A new quench protection technique, energy shift with coupling (ESC), has recently been proposed, which is very promising for the protection of high-field magnets. The ESC system includes normal-conducting coils that are highly magnetically coupled to, but galvanically insulated from, the magnet coils. When the system is activated, rapid shift of energy from the magnet to the ESC coils is achieved, which quickly results in a substantial reduction of ohmic loss in the magnet hot spot and a transition of the superconducting coils to the normal state due to transient losses. Furthermore, during the magnet current discharge part of the magnet's stored energy is transferred to the ESC coils. ESC was recently successfully demonstrated at the European Council for Nuclear Research (CERN) on a 400 mm long flat racetrack in a structure without aperture. In this contribution, we present the application of the ESC method to a subscale common-coil magnet named subscale stress-managed common-coil series (subSMCC2), which was designed and manufactured by the magnet development laboratory at the Paul Scherrer Institute. The subSMCC2 is a 300 mm long magnet, including four stress-managed Nb<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$_{3}$</tex-math></inline-formula>Sn common-coils and designed to reach bore and coil peak fields of about 5.3 and 6.4 T, respectively, at a short-sample current of 9.5 kA. Protecting this magnet after a quench without using energy extraction is extremely difficult due to its very high stabilizer current density, which is higher than 5 kA/mm<inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{2}$</tex-math></inline-formula>. The proposed ESC-based quench protection scheme relies on two ESC common-coil-type coils made of rectangular copper conductor, which are located on the outer sides of the magnet coils. Tests were carried out at the CERN magnet test facility, successfully demonstrating ESC performance under various operating conditions. These results show that ESC is an effective and high-performance technology that can protect magnets up to very high current densities.

papers.title_en: Optimization of plastic scintillator based PET devices
Photonic Quantum Gates Using OAM and MPLC
papers.abstract_en: Quantum computing based on photonic platforms offers a promising route toward scalable quantum information processing due to its low decoherence and access to high-dimensional state spaces. A promising approach for realizing photonic quantum computation is to encode quantum information in the Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) states of light, enabling the realization of high-dimensional quantum gates. Implementing such quantum gates requires programmable unitary transformations between selected computational basis states. The fabrication of integrated multi-plane light conversion (MPLC) structures could provide a pathway toward large-scale programmable quantum processors. In this work, we investigate the implementation of photonic NOT-gate transformations using OAM states and MPLC systems with a limited number of phase planes. Unlike conventional MPLC approaches that optimize phase masks for a fixed modal basis, the proposed framework treats the computational basis itself as the optimization variable. To identify suitable computational basis states, a photonic quantum-gate optimization algorithm was developed to systematically evaluate candidate LG mode pairs. For each computational subspace, the three-plane MPLC phase masks were optimized using the wavefront-matching algorithm, and the corresponding modal and gate fidelities were calculated. The results show that conjugate-OAM mode pairs <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${LG_{p}^{l},LG_{p}^{-l}}$</tex-math></inline-formula> and neighboring-radial mode pairs <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${LG_{p}^{l},LG_{p+1}^{l}}$</tex-math></inline-formula> consistently achieve higher gate fidelity than structurally mismatched mode pairs under identical hardware constraints. These findings establish a direct relationship between computational-basis selection and quantum-gate performance, providing practical guidelines for computational-basis engineering in OAM-based quantum information processing, photonic quantum gates, and programmable quantum photonic processors.

papers.title_en: The Big Bang Firewall and the Emergence of Spacetime
Channel structure of joint two-parameter estimation in the generalized MIC–Kepler system
Quantum Key Distribution Network Simulator With Hyperparameter Tuning for Realistic Performance Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Realistic simulation of quantum key distribution (QKD) networks requires a combination of precise models of quantum channels and network functions. Unfortunately, existing QKD network simulators lack either rigorous quantum physics modeling or network key-management and routing protocols, which limit their practical applicability. To address this limitation, we propose a QKD network simulator with hyperparameter tuning (QKDSim-HT), a NetSquid-based simulator specialized for polarization-based discrete-variable QKD networks. Specifically, QKDSim-HT models properties in quantum physics (photon loss, polarization-dependent depolarization, detector inefficiencies, dark counts, and dead times) as well as advanced functionalities in networking algorithms (multi-hop key relay and adaptive routing). Extensive simulations over diverse topologies reveal that the networking performance varied with respect to the fundamental properties of quantum physics, such as depolarization, fiber length, and channel attenuation. As a representative use case of QKDSim-HT, simulation results from QKDSim-HT over simple examples clearly manifest that a design of QKD networks highly affects performance of the networks. Accordingly, QKDSim-HT can serve as a practical platform for performance evaluation and optimization of quantum secured network.

papers.title_en: Suppression of two-stream and Weibel instabilities in ultra-relativistic electron–positron plasma
papers.abstract_en: We present a unified theoretical framework for analyzing both electrostatic two-stream and electromagnetic Weibel instabilities in counterstreaming electron-positron pair plasmas. Through systematic derivation of dispersion relations in non-relativistic and relativistic regimes, we demonstrate how the symmetric mass ratio fundamentally alters instability characteristics compared to electron-ion systems. The two-stream instability, driven by longitudinal electrostatic perturbations parallel to beam motion, exhibits enhanced growth rates in pair plasmas due to equal contributions from both species, with relativistic suppression scaling as γ0−3 for both electrons and positrons. The Weibel instability, arising from transverse electromagnetic modes perpendicular to streaming directions, lacks the heavy-ion stabilization present in electron-ion plasmas, producing broader unstable spectral ranges and modified saturation levels. We derive explicit conditions determining the relative dominance of each mechanism across parameter space defined by drift velocity, wavenumber orientation, and relativistic Lorentz factor. Our analysis shows that longitudinal two-stream modes dominate at small perpendicular wavenumbers and moderate drift velocities, while transverse Weibel modes become prevalent at high perpendicular wavenumbers and large velocity spreads or temperature anisotropies. These findings have direct implications for understanding magnetic field generation, particle acceleration, and energy dissipation in astrophysical pair plasmas including pulsar wind nebulae, gamma-ray burst internal shocks, and active galactic nuclei jets where counterstreaming pair populations naturally arise.

papers.title_en: Developing and validating models of open quantum systems in solid-state nanostructures
papers.abstract_en: Realistic quantum devices are open systems, and their behaviour depends not only on the subsystem of interest but also on how the environment is modelled and how the relevant observables are extracted. This thesis studies that problem in three settings. First, we study cavity-assisted qubit readout beyond the dispersive regime. We show that once coherent excitation exchange and dissipation become relevant, a microscopic treatment is needed to describe the readout quantitatively, and the optimal readout is set by a trade-off between signal accumulation and the distinguishability of the readout states. Second, we compare fermionic and spin baths in non-interacting transport models and show that spin baths reproduce fermionic reduced dynamics only in the large-bath weak-coupling limit, while clear deviations appear for smaller baths and near half-filling. Third, we study charge transport in molecular junctions using Automated Compression of Environments (ACE). There, the main difficulty is not the time evolution itself, but the extraction of the transport current, since this observable depends on system-environment correlations and is therefore not contained in the reduced system density matrix alone. We show that a probe-mode construction provides a viable route to reformulate the current as a system observable. This thesis advances our understanding of what is required for accurate modelling of open quantum dynamics across a range of solid-state settings, from cavity-assisted qubit readout to charge transport in molecular junctions.

papers.title_en: Using Printed Circuit Boards and MOSFET Switch Arrays Toward the Reliable Manufacture of Superconducting Rectifiers
papers.abstract_en: Using superconducting rectifiers to energize high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets is a promising approach to accelerate the uptake of HTS magnet technology. In this work, we start to address two limitations of the HTS superconducting rectifier concepts published to date; their low magnet charging voltages, and the variable properties of their HTS-based switches. Our approach is to test a centre-tapped full-wave transformer–rectifier utilizing HTS secondary windings and switch-arrays of Si <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small>s mounted on a printed-circuit board (PCB). This approach has the advantage of greatly facilitating reproducible and reliable manufacture. The rectifier demonstrated magnet charging voltages exceeding a cycle-averaged 80 mV at 100 A and with typically more than 30% of the power supplied to the primary coils delivered to the magnet. We found it to be resilient to our preliminary thermal-cycling testing, with no degradation in performance observed over eight liquid-nitrogen to ambient (77–295 K) thermal cycles. We compare the impact of voltage- and current-controlled modes for the rectifier’s power supply. Our conclusion is that superconducting rectifiers using <sc xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mosfet</small> switch arrays placed on PCBs is a very promising approach for low-current HTS magnet power supplies.

papers.title_en: Compact High Turns Ratio Superconducting Transformer: Comparison Between Cu and REBCO Winding Materials
papers.abstract_en: Compact high turns ratio superconducting transformers are used to transfer power between low-current copper/ semiconductor-based circuits and high-current superconductor-based circuits. This type of transformer is a key component in devices, such as superconducting transformer rectifiers and superconducting current source inverters. Typically the copper winding and the superconducting winding are arranged with a turn ratio above 100:1, respectively, and are situated entirely within a cryogenic environment. The ohmic losses associated with the high count copper winding is problematic for most cryogenic applications and demands attention even when low currents on the order of 1–10 A are used. To address this problem, a transformer has been made using rare-earth barium copper oxide (REBCO) high-temperature superconductor (HTS) coated conductor for both the primary and secondary windings. The coupling coefficient and power consumption of this transformer were measured and compared to an equivalent transformer consisting of a copper primary winding and HTS secondary winding. The HTS primary was found to provide a significant reduction in transformer power consumption and a slight improvement to transformer coupling at frequencies below <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. An increased transformer core loss and winding AC loss began to negate these efficiency improvements above <inline-formula xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\sim$</tex-math></inline-formula>8 Hz. In addition, cowinding the primary and secondary windings provided a higher coupling coefficient and lower power consumption for all winding combinations and frequencies tested. Finally, a short discussion on the implications of these findings respect to superconducting transformer rectifiers contextualizes the findings.

papers.title_en: Alfvénicity and proximity to parallel-mode marginal stability in the slow solar wind
Mechanical Characteristics of Aluminium-Stabilized Stacked REBCO Tape Cable for the CEPC Detector Magnet
papers.abstract_en: This article investigates the mechanical characteristics and critical current performance of aluminum-stabilized stacked REBCO tape cable (ASTC) for the circular electron-positron collider detector magnet. In-plane bending, torsion, and uniaxial tension tests are carried out, combined by finite element analysis. The correlation between critical current and strain under different loading conditions is systematically analyzed, and key mechanical thresholds are determined. Results show that the minimum allowable in-plane bending diameter is 1200 mm. The critical twist pitch is 327 mm. The critical current degrades to 95% of the initial value when the tensile strain in the REBCO tape reaches 0.37%. This study provides essential experimental data and theoretical support for the structural design and engineering application of ASTC in high-field superconducting magnets.

papers.title_en: Cosmological dynamics in f(R,Lm,T) gravity : A dynamical system perspective
Probing dense QCD with gauge/gravity duality
papers.abstract_en: The study of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at finite density remains one of the most formidable frontiers in the physics of strong interactions. QCD is strongly coupled at intermediate temperatures and densities, rendering perturbative techniques ineffective. Furthermore, first-principles calculations via lattice QCD, which have been highly successful at low densities, are fundamentally hindered by the numerical sign problem when describing dense matter. This leaves the properties of dense QCD matter, such as that produced in heavy-ion collisions or found in neutron stars, difficult to determine with conventional methods.Our research addresses these environments by utilizing the holographic principle, specifically the gauge/gravity duality, to investigate the strongly coupled dynamics of QCD. Originally developed in the context of string theory, the gauge/gravity duality, with the AdS/CFT correspondence as its canonical example, provides a dictionary that relates strongly coupled quantum field theories to gravitational theories in a higher-dimensional spacetime. The quantum field theory, which in our case models QCD, lives on the boundary of this spacetime. Within this framework, complicated problems regarding thermodynamic properties are translated into soluble geometric problems in the gravitational theory. In particular, we use black hole solutions of classical gravity to model the quark-gluon plasma. A central component of this work involves the development and refinement of bottom-up holographic models, which are phenomenologically constructed and tuned to reproduce key features of the boundary theory. Specifically, we focus on models based on the Einstein--Maxwell-dilaton and Dirac--Born--Infeld actions. These models are fitted to lattice QCD data at zero density and are then used to infer properties of QCD matter at finite density. Beyond investigating the transition between hadronic matter and the quark-gluon plasma, we also explore the potential for exotic states of matter that may emerge at finite density. This includes Higgs phases motivated by color superconductivity and spatially modulated inhomogeneous phases.The research offers model-based predictions for the location of the QCD critical point, where the line of first-order phase transitions terminates. We discuss our results in light of data from the Beam Energy Scan II program at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. Furthermore, our findings suggest that dense matter near the critical point may not be homogeneous, but may instead exhibit spatial modulation, in a region of the phase diagram close to that probed experimentally. We also provide an example of how critical behavior depends on the flavor structure of the theory, and find that this behavior may be suppressed by the constraints on flavor composition present in heavy-ion collisions. These results provide new insights into the phase structure of dense QCD matter.

papers.title_en: Broadening the Scope of Axion Searches: Reflector Haloscope Experiments for Broadband Axion Detection and Collider Probes of Supersymmetrized Axion Models
papers.abstract_en: <p>Axions are pseudoscalar particles that are a compelling addition to our theories of high-energy physics as they can solve two long-standing problems in modern physics. Firstly, cosmological and astrophysical observations indicate that the vast majority of the matter content of our universe is made of dark matter, a substance which cannot be described by the existing particles of the standard model of particle physics. A second major problem in modern physics is a lack of charge-parity (CP) symmetry violation in the strong force which could only arise from our current models through fine-tuning. The axion was initially proposed as a mechanism to naturally cancel the CP violation in the strong force, but it also proved to be a promising candidate for particle dark matter. Many experiments search for axion dark matter by measuring the conversion of axions into photons in a strong magnetic field. The Broadband Reflector Experiment for Axion Detection (BREAD) is one such experiment which uses a reflective surface to focus a photon signal onto an antenna or sensor. BREAD ultimately aims to search for axion-photon signals at frequencies as high as the infrared regime, but this work will focus on the instrumentation and analysis for a pilot version of BREAD which searched for axion-like particle and dark photon signals in a frequency range of 10.7 &minus;12.5 GHz. We will also discuss efforts to extend sensitivity of BREAD to the mm-wave range by, for example, exploiting a comb of resonant modes between a BREAD reflector and a secondary parabolic reflector. Finally, we discuss modeling of a supersymmetrized axion model and a sensitivity analysis of the ATLAS experiment to this model. While the axion-photon coupling is a relatively generic probe of axion models, there are some models, like the supersymmetric axion model introduced in this thesis, which can evade direct-detection axion-photon searches like BREAD. We will highlight the importance of complementing direct-detection experiments like BREAD with other probes of axion physics such as the collider sensitivity discussed here.</p>

papers.title_en: Precision Calibration and Cosmic Birefringence with Simons Observatory
papers.abstract_en: <p>Precision cosmology experiments are ushering in an exciting era for fundamental physics by enabling searches for physics beyond the Standard Model and probing the extreme energy scales of the early Universe. Science cases such as identifying viable dark matter candidates, applying tighter constraints on the effective number of light relativistic species, and constraining cosmic birefringence are enabled by the deployment of increasingly sensitive Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) survey experiments like the Simons Observatory (SO). As experiments rapidly achieve large gains in sensitivity, the resolving factors of these ambitious science goals shift to the instrument&rsquo;s absolute calibrations such as its passbands and polarization angle.</p><p>In the first part of this thesis, I design, develop, and validate a novel bandpass calibrator with power variability that is capable of finely resolving bandpass edges. I then present material characterization of metamaterial anti-reflection cuttings and iron-loaded absorptive neutral density filters with varying concentrations that enable an extensive suite of in-lab testing and the necessary spectral corrections. This in-lab testing program is covered in the following chapter where we discuss the testing and integration of an SO small aperture telescope that housed a large aperture telescope&rsquo;s optics tube (&ldquo;camera&rdquo;). We fully populated the optical stack and carried out a range of testing to characterize and mitigate instrument systematics.</p><p>Finally, I discuss my work developing and fielding a bandpass calibrator for the SO small aperture telescopes. &nbsp;I design crossed-Dragonne style coupling optics and implement a mechanized design that permits scans over the full field-of-view of the telescope. Following in-lab testing and integration of the calibrator, we deploy it to the site and measure detector passbands. We confirm broad focal plane coverage and present preliminary passbands. We also offer a characterization of the SO small aperture telescope's polarization modulating half-wave plate's frequency dependence using these passbands. Future investigations are required to resolve a discrepancy with the expected performance. The half-wave plate's frequency dependent phase shift along with the passbands are necessary to properly calibrate the instrument's polarization angle for applications toward a probe of the parity-violating cosmic birefringence rotation angle, which is otherwise degenerate with the instrument's miscalibration angle.</p>

papers.title_en: An evaluation of Geant4-DNA early radiochemical yields
Proton Structure and QCD under the LHC Neutrino Microscope
papers.abstract_en: The LHC produces an abundant flux of high-energy neutrinos and muons in the far-forward rapidity region. The neutrinos reach energies in the TeV range, which makes them the highest-energy neutrinos ever produced in a lab environment.In this thesis, scientific opportunities are explored to exploit the neutrino and muon flux to investigate the substructure of the proton. The impact of neutrino deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) measurements at the ongoing FASERν experiment and the planned detectors at the proposed Forward Physics Facility (FPF) on global Parton Distribution Function (PDF) extractions is assessed.A detailed phenomenological analysis of the DIS process is performed with state-of-the-art Monte Carlo simulation at next-to leading order in QCD expansion.This Monte Carlo simulation pipeline is then used to produce theory prediction that are required for a first machine-learning based extraction of the muon neutrino flux from FASER 2024 data. Fits of the neutrino flux allow to discriminate between different models of forward hadron production, constrain rare beyond the Standard Model decays to neutrinos and potentially provide evidence for the presence or absence of an intrinsic charm component of the proton.In the last part of the thesis, muon DIS is studied, which can probe the charm content of the proton directly, especially in the large-x region. This kinematic region is of special interest when searching for evidence for intrinsic charm. The analysis shows that the FASERν experiment could provide competitive constraints on intrinsic charm. Combining the FASERν emulsion detector with the electronic FASER detector it is also possible to construct a charm-asymmetry observable. A non-zero charm-asymmetrywould provide conclusive evidence for intrinsic charm

papers.title_en: Introduction to Quantum Information Theory
papers.abstract_en: The science of quantum information asks how the laws of nature can be used to manipulate information on a microscopic scale, in ways that have no counterpart in classical physics. Born from a synergy of classical information theory and the foundations of quantum physics, quantum information theory sheds light on fundamental aspects of physics.

papers.title_en: Computational Problems for Physics
papers.abstract_en: Our future scientists and professionals must be conversant in computational techniques. In order to facilitate integration of computer methods into existing physics courses, Computational Problems for Physics offers a large number of worked examples and problems with fully guided solutions in Python (as well as Mathematica, Java, C, Fortran, and Maple on the Web). The book can be used as a self-study guide for learning how to use computer methods in physics. Fully revised, this second edition includes:A chapter on neural networks, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, with the building of simple networks, and the use of machine learning software.A chapter on quantum computing with some problems to be run on the IBM Quantum Computer.A chapter on general relativity with manipulations of the field equations and with computation of GR corrections to classical mechanics.An expanded coverage of principal component analysis.A crucial resource for students beginning their study of computational physics with in-depth and engaging problems and exercises.

papers.title_en: Quantum Matters
papers.abstract_en: Quantum Matters: From Field to Life bridges the gap between the mysterious world of quantum physics and the technologies that shape our daily lives. This innovative book takes readers on a comprehensive journey from fundamental quantum principles to their real-world applications, revealing how the invisible rules governing the smallest particles power everything from global positioning system (GPS) navigation and magneticresonance imaging (MRI) scans to the emerging quantum revolution in computing, communication, and medicine. Rather than treating quantum science as an abstract academic subject, this book demonstrates how quantum mechanics is already woven into the fabric of modern society and explores how quantum technologies promise to transform industries, secure communications, and unlock new possibilities in energy, healthcare, and beyond.This book's unique strengths include its interdisciplinary approach that connects quantum principles across physics, materials, engineering, biology, medicine, and finance, making complex concepts accessible without sacrificing depth. It features clear explanations of everyday quantum technologies like smartphones, lasers, and atomic clocks, showing readers the hidden quantum science behind familiar devices. The text provides comprehensive coverage of emerging quantum frontiers including quantum computing, cryptography, and sensing, while exploring the fascinating field of quantum biology and its role in photosynthesis and animal navigation. Additionally, it offers global perspective on quantum innovation, highlighting international investments and collaborations that are shaping the quantum ecosystem, all presented through an engaging narrative style that combines scientific accuracy with inspiring storytelling.This book serves a diverse readership including graduate students across multiple disciplines who need to understand quantum science's relevance to their fields; interdisciplinary professionals in engineering, computing, biology, and finance seeking practical insights; and curious general readers interested in cutting-edge science. For educators and policymakers, it provides essential context for understanding the strategic importance of quantum technologies in the global economy.  Whether you're a student building foundational knowledge, a professional exploring quantum applications in your industry, or simply someone fascinated by how science shapes the future, Quantum Matters empowers you to see quantum science not as distant theory but as a transformative force already shaping today's world and tomorrow's possibilities.

papers.title_en: Inflation in Metric-affine Modified Gravity
papers.abstract_en: Cosmic inflation is a period of accelerated expansion in the early universe which generates the primordial perturbations that lead to structure formation in the late universe.These perturbations are also imprinted on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and can be parametrised by the spectral index of the scalar perturbations $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, which were measured by the Planck mission, the BICEP/Keck experiments, and by the ACT and SPT experiments.These observables probe energies beyond the reach of terrestrial experiments, and they are sensitive not only to the matter content driving inflation, but also to the underlying theory of gravity.In the metric formulation of general relativity, the connection is a priori assumed to be the Levi--Civita connection.In the metric-affine (or Palatini) formulation, both the metric and the connection are independent variables, and the gravitational degrees of freedom can be carried by nonmetricity and torsion as well as curvature.For the Einstein--Hilbert action with minimally coupled matter the two formulations coincide, but once the inflaton couples non-minimally to the curvature, or higher-order curvature terms are included, they define different theories. The formulation of gravity is then a physical question to be settled by observation.In this thesis we study how inflaton-coupled modifications of gravity in the Palatini formulation predict different CMB observables in three distinct theories and three geometric assumptions. For the unconstrained connection, and when either torsion or nonmetricity is set to zero, we consider: the Chern--Simons term, the Gauss--Bonnet term, and independent distortion terms.In all three studies the modification sources the distortion, which we integrate out to alter the inflaton kinetic term. This reshapes the potential and the predictions for $n_s$ and $r$. The observables may thus discriminate between modifications of gravity, and between the a priori assumptions made about the connection.Forthcoming experiments such as the Simons Observatory and LiteBIRD will sharpen the constraints on $n_s$ and $r$, and probe the theory of gravity underlying inflation.

papers.title_en: Event-driven formulation of cosmic structure formation via Morse-Cerf theory
papers.abstract_en: Cosmic large-scale structure is described by evolving density fields, yet critical-point topology is usually analyzed through snapshots or threshold filtrations. We formulate the physical-time evolution of critical structures for a smooth, positive, coarse-grained density field using <math display="inline"><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></math>. This monotone transformation preserves critical points, Morse indices, generic birth-death locations, and excursion-set topology. The resulting Morse-Cerf framework tracks critical-point worldlines, distinguishes Eulerian birth-death events, fixed-threshold events, and continuous level-set volume fluxes, and yields index-resolved balance laws and Kac-Rice intensities. As an analytically tractable proxy model, we use the Zel’dovich approximation while separating singularities of the Lagrangian map from Eulerian scalar-field bifurcations. The conditions <math display="inline"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> define continuous collapse-crossing hypersurfaces, whereas local minima of <math display="inline"><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></math> define discrete nucleation proxies. For Gaussian initial conditions, we derive one-scale collapse fractions and crossing fluxes from the Doroshkevich distribution and characterize the proxy catalogs numerically at the adopted grid resolution. Their finite-time populations show temporally concentrated activity and ordered median growth factors, <math display="inline"><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>nuc</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>fin</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo><</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>nuc</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>fin</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo><</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">˜</mo></mover><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>nuc</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>fin</mi></mrow></msubsup></math>, over the reported smoothing scales, while their abundances and widths vary with smoothing. These discrete-catalog results are a fixed-resolution proof of concept, with no continuum-resolution claim. Continuous crossing fluxes and discrete proxy rates are complementary observables and provide a controlled basis for measuring exact Eulerian event processes in nonlinear simulations.

papers.title_en: On Family-Separated Seesaw Relations: Exact Reconstruction and Corrections
papers.abstract_en: <jats:p>We examine the family-separated seesaw (FSS) ansatz proposed in arXiv:2605.27049v2. Combining its paired cancellations with exact partial unitarity fixes the light and heavy mixing blocks in terms of one unitary matrix and the paired mass ratios. We classify their unitary completions and reconstruct the Dirac and singlet Majorana mass matrices, distinguishing the physical heavy masses from the singlet mass parameters. This identifies FSS as an exact realization of form dominance whose conventional one-loop leptogenesis cancellation is already established. The particular sum of lepton-number-violating invariants entering the proposed decay asymmetry therefore vanishes; individual CP invariants need not vanish. We also correct the heavy-mass reconstruction formulas and quantify their errors for both light-mass orderings. These formulas are conditional algebraic relations, not independent predictions of the heavy spectrum. Numerical mass–mixing illustrations, explicit chiral projections for double-beta decay, and a leading-logarithmic estimate of radiative misalignment clarify the physical reach and limitations. The contribution is an exact consistency analysis and correction of specific proposed consequences rather than a new mass-generation mechanism or a general prohibition of leptogenesis.</jats:p>

papers.title_en: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract_en: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction. In this paper, we organize decoding algorithms, execution strategies, and code constructions using common classifications and examine their performance and trade-offs under the reported evaluation conditions. We distinguish decoder-level hierarchy, where multiple decoding stages or resources cooperate to decode a single code, from code-level hierarchy, where the code construction itself introduces multiple decoding levels. We first review single-code hierarchical decoders and their cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed implementations. We then study hierarchical and concatenated codes, focusing on how decoding is coordinated across code levels through hard decisions, soft reliability information, or syndrome information. We also examine how qubit modalities shape decoding workloads and timing requirements, and review how different decoding platforms meet these requirements, including central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and cryogenic platforms. By assessing design trade-offs, this paper clarifies connections across the literature and provides a shared foundation for QEC design exploration. It also identifies gaps in performance reporting and system integration to guide future research toward practical quantum error correction.

papers.title_en: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family. Each edge supplies one independent uniform symbol to its endpoints for key relay, or carries one symbol once for network coding. The network code may choose its source terminal, edge orientations, and causal transmission order before execution. In this setting, the standard one-time-pad simulation readily converts every secure network code to key relay. We investigate the reverse conversion to linear network coding. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding over the prescribed field. The proof uses connectivity and flow conservation, related to the binary $st$-flow protocol. However, this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A doubled triangle separates key relay from acyclic coding but admits causal coding on a cyclic orientation. On the four-terminal complete graph, a linear key relay protocol over the ternary field withstands the three perfect-matching wiretap sets, whereas no linear causal network code distributes a source symbol of the same size, even with private randomness at every vertex and its use in decoding. We also establish a linear key relay normal form that removes interaction and private randomness and bounds public communication. All results concern one-shot feasibility with exact agreement and perfect secrecy.

papers.title_en: Exact Quantum Algorithms for Composed Boolean Functions
papers.abstract_en:
We study exact quantum algorithms for block compositions of total Boolean functions. For an outer function $f$ of degree $D$ and an inner function $g$ on $m$ bits, we prove 
$$ Q_E(f\circ g)=O\!\left(mD+Q_E(f)Q_{1/(4D)}(g)\right). $$
 The algorithm combines approximate inner evaluations with a finite exact correction. Its two costs are governed by different parameters of the outer function: exact query complexity determines the cost of simulation, whereas polynomial degree determines the number of inner blocks used in the correction. We first establish the construction with an arity-dependent error threshold and then obtain the degree-dependent threshold above. For recursive ternary not-all-equal, this gives an exact algorithm using $(3/\sqrt2)^{k(1+o(1))}$ queries asymptotically. More generally, for every fixed nonconstant total gadget $h$, we determine the exact recursive rate as $\max\{\textrm{deg}(h),\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(h)\}$ and prove $Q_E(h^{\circ k})=\widetilde O_h(R(h^{\circ k})^2)$.
