Space relevance is documented for more than a quarter of active companies, often alongside defence involvement.

papers.title_en: Why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract_en: Since a strong magnetic field is generated in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, novel phenomena have been predicted to occur in the quark-gluon plasma produced in these collisions. However, these predictions have not yet been convincingly confirmed experimentally. We reanalyze the generation and evolution of the magnetic field which plays a key role in the phenomena. Using the method of one-sided Fourier transformation, we reconcile the description in frequency and wave-vector space, which is required to properly account for the electromagnetic properties of the quark-gluon plasma, with the initial-value nature of the problem arising from the creation of the plasma medium at the moment of collision. We show that the currents induced in the quark-gluon plasma, which sustain the magnetic field, develop with a delay and are consequently less effective than usually assumed. Moreover, because the plasma initially consists predominantly of electrically neutral gluons, while charged quarks emerge at a later stage, the induced currents are further delayed. Consequently, a magnitude of the field present in the quark-gluon plasma is significantly lower than earlier estimates suggested. This may explain why magnetic-field effects are difficult to observe in relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title_en: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state. The analysis is performed for the DUNE setup and extended beyond its baseline to study the interplay between wave-packet decoherence and matter effects over long distances. For the DUNE baseline, finite wave-packet widths suppress and smooth the oscillations relative to the PW case, with smaller widths causing stronger damping, while matter effects modify the amplitudes and positions of the oscillation features. Among the considered measures, residual $l_1$-norm coherence dominates over the entanglement measures. At very long propagation distances, wave-packet decoherence progressively washes out the oscillatory behavior, driving the oscillation probabilities and quantum correlation measures toward averaged values, with smaller wave-packet widths leading to earlier damping. Further, in the $L-δ_{\rm CP}$ plane, residual $l_1$-norm coherence exhibits weak $δ_{\rm CP}$ dependence, while Concurrence Fill and Three-$π$ entanglement show greater sensitivity at the DUNE baseline. Beyond a characteristic baseline in the extended propagation regime, all three measures approach constant values, independent of $L$ and $δ_{\rm CP}$.

papers.title_en: Reduced filtering using classical control hierarchy with linear optimality for continuous quantum error correction
papers.abstract_en: Continuous quantum error correction promises reduced thresholds and hardware overhead compared to the digital paradigm, but its complex model estimation has greatly reduced its practicality. We recast this problem as a classical control-theoretic state hierarchy made of an exact bilinear reduced model, an exact conditional filter, and standard estimation and feedback design. For any $[[n,k,d]]$ stabilizer code whose generators are all continuously monitored and which is driven by a single Pauli recovery channel, we prove that the exact filter closes at dimension $3\cdot2^{\,n-k-1}$. This dimension is set by the syndrome space instead of the Hilbert space and is minimal within invariant-subspace filtering. The reduced model exposes and corrects two failure mechanisms of the feedback loop. Strong monitoring damps the rotational partner through which the controller steers the stabilizer and injects back-action diffusion along the recovery path; lowering the measurement strength during correction raises the entanglement fidelity of partner-steering LQR control by $0.096$ in the three-qubit code with three monitored parities. Linearizing at the codespace leaves the syndrome uncontrollable, so the controller can stall; a gain designed at a shifted operating point removes this degeneracy. In the limit of zero measurement during correction, we prove that a syndrome-only filter is exact at every recovery boundary. The resulting committed-recovery controller needs only $2^{\,n-k}$ class probabilities and gives the highest entanglement fidelity compared among the methods tested in the literature, $0.947$ against $0.920$ for a measurement-based estimator protocol in the three-qubit bit-flip code, and $0.726$ vs at most $0.407$ for continuous controllers in the five-qubit perfect code.

papers.title_en: Detecting non-Hermitian topology from long-time dynamics
papers.abstract_en: We propose a protocol to measure the non-Hermitian topological invariant associated with the Lindbladian spectrum of chiral-symmetric open Gaussian systems from the relaxation of the covariance matrix. Importantly, the method works in the long-time regime and does not rely on isolating edge modes, so it remains applicable even when the Liouvillian skin effect may obscure them. We illustrate the technique on a Kitaev chain with reservoir-induced nonreciprocity, for which we first obtain a fully analytical and previously unknown description of its topological phase diagram. We then show that our protocol reliably distinguishes all the different phases.

papers.title_en: Observation of the $Λ(1520)$ suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV
papers.abstract_en: A suppression of the baryonic $Λ(1520)$ resonance yield relative to the $Λ$ ground state by $0.589 \pm 0.015^{\rm stat} \pm 0.086^{\rm syst}$ is observed in central relative to peripheral Pb-Pb collisions, with a significance of $6.8σ$. The $Λ(1520)$ production at midrapidity is measured in six centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions for the first time at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV with ALICE. The $Λ(1520)$ is a sensitive probe of late-stage hadronic interactions since its lifetime is comparable to that of the hadronic phase in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC. Statistical hadronization model calculations, predicting yields at chemical freeze-out, overestimate the measured ratio. The transverse-momentum spectra and the centrality dependence of the suppression are reproduced by the MUSIC hydrodynamic model only when coupled to the SMASH hadronic transport afterburner, which implements rescattering and regeneration in the late hadronic stage. The measurement, which represents the first observation of resonance suppression within a single collision system, provides a stringent test of the late-stage dynamics and evidence that hadronic interactions substantially modify reconstructible resonance yield.
authors: Ferreira Siqueira Amaral Gomes, Maria Gabriela
Moreira De Godoy Willems, Denise Aparecida

papers.title_en: Communication Supremacy of a Qubit in Holevo Frenkel Weiner Scenario
papers.abstract_en: The prevailing wisdom asserts that in the Holevo Frenkel Weiner (HFW) framework of communication tasks, a qubit offers no advantage over a c bit unless additional quantum resources are supplied or the classical shared randomness (SR) is restricted. In contrast, we establish the supremacy of qubit communication in the HFW framework when additional quantum resources, such as entanglement or measurement incompatibility are not injected and SR is a free resource. We consider a prepare-measure scenario where the sender, Alice, prepares six states subject to a specific cryptographic constraint, and the receiver, Bob, performs a three-outcome measurement. Such a constraint on preparation impacts the power of qubit communication quite differently than that of c-bit communication, ultimately giving rise to the quantum advantage. We introduce a witness capable of distinguishing quantum strategies that lie beyond the set of possible classical strategies and demonstrate the optimal quantum advantage. {As an application, we demonstrate the generation of certified randomness without requiring any seed randomness, since Bob has no input.} We further analyse the robustness of the witness and show that the advantage persists in noisy situations, making it suitable for experimental realisation. Finally, we demonstrate that Bob's three outcome qubit positive operator valued-measure (POVMs) has a distinct capability of detecting coherence, which can be regarded as the non-classical feature responsible for showcasing the quantum advantage.

papers.title_en: A unified reduced-mass parametrization of effective chromoelectric interactions in hadrons
papers.abstract_en: We construct a unified effective mass relation in which a common reduced-mass function describes the flavor dependence of chromoelectric pair contributions, with explicit color factors connecting $q\bar q$ and $qq$ pairs. After subtracting fixed spin-weighted chromomagnetic contributions, we jointly fit fourteen spin-averaged meson and baryon masses using constituent quark masses and an additive constant shared by both sectors, obtaining a root-mean-square (RMS) residual of 4 MeV. The fitted saturating form connects the nearly saturated light-flavor contribution with increasing attraction in the heavy-flavor region. In the common saturation limit, the leading chromoelectric contribution acts as a common mass shift for each constituent and can be absorbed into effective constituent masses; the residual pair term accounts for the flavor dependence away from saturation. With the chromomagnetic interaction included, this single parameter set reproduces the ground-state meson and baryon spectra and yields predictions for multiply heavy baryons outside the calibration set. By diagonalizing the sum of the chromoelectric and chromomagnetic mass matrices, we further obtain the ground-state spectra of $cc\bar c\bar c$, $bb\bar b\bar b$, and $bc\bar b\bar c$. The fully charmed tensor mass is ${6505}{(9)(9)}$ MeV, close to recent lattice QCD results, while the upper scalar mass of {${6562}{(9)(12)}$} MeV lies in the mass region near $X(6600)$. The tetraquark masses remain relatively stable under the examined variations of the $qq$ chromomagnetic couplings. The relative $S$-wave rearrangement-decay weights obtained from color--spin recoupling can be used to identify favored decay channels under the stated spatial-overlap approximation.

papers.title_en: Quantitative Junction Transport Modeling of RHIC Charge and Baryon Stopping
papers.abstract_en: Charge and baryon stopping in Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr isobar collisions are modeled by HIJING with junction. With realistic nuclear geometry and a tuned diquark splitting, it reproduces STAR's net-baryon yield, charge difference, and scaled baryon-to-charge ratio at midrapidity. Junctions set the ratio's magnitude while neutron skins drive its centrality trend. At the LHC, large asymmetric pair production in HIJING obscures junction effects, causing apparent tension with data. This tuned generator reproduces RHIC data and predicts O+O behavior, setting a quantitative benchmark for baryon transport.

papers.title_en: $NΩ$ Dibaryon near Unitarity from Physical-Point Lattice QCD
papers.abstract_en: The $NΩ$ system is a promising dibaryon candidate because its constituents share no valence quarks and therefore avoid valence-quark Pauli repulsion. We determine the $^{5}S_{2}$$NΩ$ interaction in (2+1)-flavor lattice QCD at physical quark masses ($m_π\simeq137~\text{MeV}$) using the HAL QCD method. The interaction is attractive over the resolved range and supports a shallow state near unitarity. A direct $T$-matrix pole analysis gives $B_{nΩ} = 0.61\,(^{+0.41}_{-0.30})\,(^{+0.60}_{-0.18})~\text{MeV}$; including finite-charge-size Coulomb attraction yields $B_{pΩ} = 1.25\,(^{+0.46}_{-0.39})\,(^{+0.69}_{-0.25})~\text{MeV}$. These results provide a first-principles benchmark for future $NΩ$ femtoscopy and dibaryon searches.

papers.title_en: Exploring the Pion Vector Form Factor Beyond the Physical Sheet
papers.abstract_en: Using analyticity and unitarity, we parametrise the pion vector form factor on the first and second Riemann sheets, below the inelastic $πω$ threshold. We fit this model-independent parametrisation to the available $τ^-\toπ^-π^0ν_τ$ data from ALEPH, Belle, CLEO and OPAL, together with spacelike data from NA7 and JLab, and extract the pole position and couplings of the $ρ^\pm$ along with the pion charge radius and low-energy $ππ$ scattering parameters. Our results are independent of external scattering input and agree with the literature; in particular, we find $M_{ρ^\pm} = 762.07\pm 0.63$ MeV and $Γ_{ρ^\pm} = 143.62^{+0.79}_{-0.80}$ MeV. The parametrisation is publicly available in the EOS software.

papers.title_en: Inter-city 18.9 km free-space QKD over a dense urban corridor
papers.abstract_en: Terrestrial free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) provides a flexible complement to fiber-based networks, but its deployment over long horizontal paths in dense metropolitan environments remains challenging, as atmospheric turbulence, demanding pointing and tracking requirements, and operational constraints can substantially increase system complexity. We experimentally demonstrate the operation of a decoy-state BB84 system over an 18.9~km free-space link across a densely populated urban area in the metropolitan region of Barcelona using an aviation-compliant optical architecture. The system operates at 785~nm using room-temperature single-photon detectors and requires no adaptive optics at the receiver. The modular QKD transmitter, based on a deployment-oriented design, is interfaced with a versatile free-space optical terminal and an independent GPS-disciplined synchronization architecture, facilitating its integration into heterogeneous optical infrastructures. We present the transmitter performance and optical-link characteristics, together with a 40-minute field test characterized by an average channel attenuation of approximately 19~dB and a mean QBER of 1.31%. From the measured channel parameters, we estimate an average finite-size secret key rate exceeding 11~kbit/s. These results demonstrate the feasibility of inter-city free-space QKD over dense urban areas using a comparatively simple architecture.

papers.title_en: Solar Neutrinos at the ESSνSB experiment
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the sensitivity of the ESSnuSB large underground water-Cherenkov (WC) detector to two key solar neutrino signatures: the MSW spectral upturn in the $^8$B electron neutrino survival probability $P_{ee}(E_ν)$, and the first direct observation of the rare hep neutrino flux. The analysis incorporates detector systematic uncertainties (energy resolution and flux normalization) and models environmental backgrounds from cosmic-ray muon spallation and $^{222}$Rn contamination. We adopt a shape-driven analysis strategy with a floating overall normalization, so that the discovery power relies on the spectral distortion rather than on the absolute event rate. In a realistic scenario with 90% spallation rejection efficiency, informed by the Super-Kamiokande experience and recent JUNO analyses, residual spallation backgrounds prevent either signal from reaching $5σ$ significance within 20 years of exposure. For the hep flux, we present a detailed sensitivity study to both its discovery and its precision, and quantify how the required spallation veto efficiency and recoil energy threshold jointly determine the achievable significance for both signals. At the adopted thresholds, discovery-level sensitivity for both signals requires approximately 99% spallation rejection over a 20-year exposure.

papers.title_en: Squeezed terahertz light from nonlinear diamagnetism in ultrastrongly coupled two-dimensional electrons
papers.abstract_en: Two-dimensional electron gases in terahertz cavities are among the most mature platforms for ultrastrong light--matter coupling, yet their collective response is captured by the linear Hopfield model, which has an exact classical correspondence. We show that the intrinsic band nonparabolicity of the electrons, recently revealed through nonlinear diamagnetism, turns this system into a quantum Kerr oscillator that squeezes terahertz light. Using a non-rotating-wave theory with ultrastrong-coupling-consistent input--output, an ab initio cavity bath, and a self-consistent model of electron heating, we predict output squeezing of 1.8--2.4 dB with present GaAs samples in weakly confined cavities with quality factors of order $10^2$, and up to $\approx9$ dB with modest improvements in mobility or cavity frequency. Carrier heating sets limits through a material figure of merit, which yields a simple design rule that the optimal cavity quality factor scales inversely with the ultrastrong-coupling strength.

papers.title_en: Explicit Absolutely Maximally Entangled states in dimensions twice a prime power
papers.abstract_en: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states are pure multipartite states with maximally mixed reductions on every set of at most half the parties. We construct explicit families in local dimension $2q$, twice an odd prime power $q$, using an established coupling of qubits and $q$-level systems. The $q$-level states remove interference between branches, so the qubit states need maximally mixed reductions only on average. This gives AME$(9,2q)$ and AME$(11,2q)$ for every odd prime power $q\geq5$, AME$(13,2q)$ for $q\geq17$, AME$(15,2q)$ for $q\geq9$, and AME$(17,2q)$ for $q\geq67$. For every odd $N\geq3$, the same coupling gives AME$(N,2q)$ under the sufficient condition $q\geq\max\{N,2^{N-2}\}$ on the odd prime power $q$. Within this coupling, the smallest such $q$ must grow exponentially with $N$. Combined with known inputs and products, these families complete the nine-party classification: for integer $d\geq2$, an AME$(9,d)$ state exists if and only if $d\geq3$. Choosing the branch pairing also gives AME$(15,2p)$ states with a cyclic shift of the parties compensated by local unitaries, for every prime $p\equiv1\pmod{15}$.

papers.title_en: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
papers.abstract_en: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014. With partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation, we obtain 13.5 bit/s over 109 km, and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB of accumulated loss between two cities without a direct fiber link. Benchmarking against finite-key security bounds shows that the implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound, and that replacing detect-and-discard with error correction would increase the finite-key rate by a factor of 4.1-6.6, and yield a positive finite-key rate on the 142.9 km link where the implemented scheme yields none.

papers.title_en: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions
papers.abstract_en: We explore the close relationship between the processing of data and the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. For example, certain classes of quantum neural networks can be mapped onto dissipative quantum Ising models whose evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation. In these architectures, emergent nonlinearities lead to non-ergodic dynamics under which initial states located in different basins of attraction evolve towards distinguishable stationary states. This mechanism underlies the classification of quantum data. Motivated by this connection, we consider an Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions. Using a combination of mean-field calculations and exact small-scale numerics, we show that the stationary state manifold can be designed to enable multi-class classification. We also investigate the structure of the ensuing basins of attraction, thereby showing that these systems allow for the classification of quantum states with nonlinear decision boundaries.

papers.title_en: Physical Observables and Superselection
papers.abstract_en: It is well-known that a physical state may be represented by a unit vector in a Hilbert space, whilst a physical observable may be represented by a self-adjoint operator on that same space. However, the introduction of a superselection rule on a Hilbert space imposes constraints such that not all self-adjoint operators can represent observables, which has further consequences for the states themselves as well as the physical processes that transform them. In this article, we review the concept of superselection from the view of how such rules would affect what we consider to be physical. Arguments for the existence of a superselection rule due to charge or possibly energy conservation are given and the emergence of effective superselection rules due to decoherence or the lack of a shared reference frame are also discussed.

papers.title_en: Two-loop mixed QCD-EW corrections to bottom-pair production in electron-positron collisions
papers.abstract_en: We present the two-loop mixed strong-electroweak virtual corrections to the production of a massive bottom-antibottom quark pair in electron-positron collisions. The evaluation of all the relevant Feynman integrals, including those with up to five internal massive lines with three different mass values, has been worked out relying on semi-analytical techniques, using complex-valued masses for the electroweak gauge bosons. The ultraviolet-renormalized and infrared-subtracted finite correction contributes to the NNLO QCD-EW cross section of the inclusive production of a bottom-quark pair. The methodology adopted in this calculation can be extended to the study of fully electroweak second-order corrections to benchmark precision calculations relevant to both the high-luminosity phase of the Large Hadron Collider and prospective future lepton colliders.

papers.title_en: Dilution of cosmological relics and gravitational waves from a supercooled electroweak phase transition in classically scale-invariant models
papers.abstract_en: In classically scale-invariant extensions of the Standard Model the electroweak scale is generated radiatively, and the absence of tree-level mass terms keeps the symmetric phase metastable down to very low temperatures. We study the resulting phase transition in a model with a real singlet and several additional scalars coupled to the Higgs doublet and to the singlet, in which electroweak symmetry is broken along a Gildener-Weinberg flat direction and a light dilaton appears in the spectrum. Computing the bounce along the two-dimensional tunnelling path and following the false-vacuum fraction through percolation and completion, we find that the transition proceeds in a single, strongly supercooled step and completes above the QCD scale over a region of parameter space consistent with Higgs measurements and perturbativity. Despite the strong supercooling the transition is fast. The bubble walls reach their terminal velocity early, and almost all of the released vacuum energy goes into bulk motion of the plasma, which thermalises and reheats the universe close to the scale set by the vacuum energy. The resulting entropy injection dilutes pre-existing relics by up to several orders of magnitude. It raises the baryon asymmetry that must be present before the transition, relaxes the unitarity bound on the mass of thermal dark matter, and suppresses earlier gravitational-wave backgrounds. If the acoustic description of gravitational-wave production extends to this regime, the signal peaks in the millihertz band, follows an approximate scaling relation between peak amplitude and frequency set by the vacuum energy, and would be observed by LISA throughout the viable region. The results depend on the multiplicity of the new scalars and their Higgs portal coupling at leading order through a single combination, and require the singlet scale to lie at or above the TeV scale.

papers.title_en: Development of a Cryogenic Anti-Coincidence System Based on Scintillating Crystals Read Out with Kinetic Inductance Detectors for BULLKID-DM
papers.abstract_en: The BULLKID-DM experiment has been proposed to search for WIMP-like dark matter particles with a mass of 1 GeV or lower and with a WIMP-nucleon interaction cross section down to $10^{-43}$ cm$^2$. To achieve this goal, the experiment utilizes a detector consisting of a stack of 16 silicon wafers instrumented with phonon-mediated superconducting Kinetic Inductance Detectors (KIDs), to be operated at the underground facility of the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), Italy. To reduce the residual background arising from $γ$-rays, neutrons, and muons, a cryogenic active anti-coincidence system (veto) operating at mK temperature, surrounding the main detector, is under development. The veto detector consists of segmented scintillating crystals read out by phonon-mediated KID light detectors. Current status and future developments of the veto system are presented. In particular, we focus on cryogenic tests of both bismuth germanate (BGO) and gadolinium aluminum gallium garnet (GAGG) crystals, which had been previously chosen as veto candidate crystals according to our preliminary studies on the dependence of their optical properties (i.e. light yield and scintillation decay time) on temperature. We finally present the operation and preliminary tests of a two-module veto prototype with multiplexed readout.

papers.title_en: Gaussian ergotropy and spatial correlations: accelerated vacuum versus a thermal field
papers.abstract_en: Can the spatial correlations of a quantum environment be revealed through work extraction? We address this question using two harmonic-oscillator detectors coupled to either an accelerated vacuum or a matched inertial thermal field. We establish a quantitative connection between the spatial correlations of the environment and the equilibrium Gaussian ergotropy, showing that the leading extractable work is governed by a response-weighted spatial correlation. Although the two environments have identical local spectra, their different spatial correlations give rise to distinct work responses. We further identify a finite-distance blind point at which a single measurement configuration fails to distinguish the two environments. By reversing the direct coupling between the detectors, we develop a two-setting scheme that removes this ambiguity and reconstructs the underlying spatial correlations from work measurements. This reconstruction remains effective beyond the weak-coupling regime. We also show that spatial correlations can provide additional global work even when the detector pair is separable, demonstrating that entanglement is not a necessary resource for this advantage. Finally, we investigate the transient evolution of Gaussian ergotropy and reveal its oscillatory decay and dependence on acceleration and detector parameters. Our results establish Gaussian ergotropy as an operational probe of spatial correlations in bosonic environments.

papers.title_en: Improved Low-Cost Quantum Error Mitigation with Benchmarked-Noise Zero-Noise Extrapolation (bnZNE)
papers.abstract_en: We theoretically extend and experimentally demonstrate benchmarked-noise zero-noise extrapolation (bnZNE), a simple and low-cost method for quantum error mitigation which aims to outperform the highly popular ZNE method for an equal total shot cost by improving the classical extrapolation step. We recently proposed bnZNE as a new error mitigation method (Harris et al., arXiv:2603.10224 (2026)) and showed that it can mitigate noise to the same order as standard ZNE under gate-wise depolarizing noise. Here, we introduce randomized bnZNE which addresses the case of running multiple random circuits per noise level, allowing for the incorporation of noise-tailoring techniques like Pauli twirling and readout error mitigation, and test the method on the IBM and IQM hardware for a plethora of large-scale applications, observing bnZNE to consistently produce more accurate results than standard ZNE. Our approach enhances the extrapolation process to the zero-noise limit by using classically-simulable and structure-mirroring benchmark circuits, generated from the standard application circuit, to sensitively measure the effective error rate at each scaled noise level beyond simple integer values. We give a new method for generating tailored benchmark circuits for the IQM superconducting devices and test them experimentally. Our results demonstrate that bnZNE presents a versatile alternative to ZNE which can enable more accurate results at utility scales with an equivalent cost.

papers.title_en: The Gator low-background spectrometer: readout upgrade and photomultiplier tube radioassay for XLZD
papers.abstract_en: We report on a readout upgrade of Gator, a low-background high-purity germanium spectrometer operated at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso for material radioassay. The upgraded data acquisition records digitised waveforms, enabling noise rejection on an event-level basis, and offline energy reconstruction. Measurements before and after the upgrade show an improved energy resolution of 17% at the 2614.5 keV line of 208-Tl, with (2.14 +- 0.22) keV at FWHM, and suppression of electronic noise in the low-energy region. We assess the resulting sensitivity for a specified sample geometry, and present a new background measurement. The background rate in the (100-2700) keV range is (86.6 +- 0.5) counts/(kg day). We also show the radioassay results of sixteen Hamamatsu R17317 3-inch photomultiplier tubes with an improved stem design, which reduces the activities from the primordial 238-U and 232-Th chains by a factor of three, making them suitable candidate photosensors for the XLZD experiment.

papers.title_en: Efficient computation of PEPS gradients for optimized quantum state preparation on 2D topologies
papers.abstract_en: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental subroutine for quantum computation. For complex, entangled initial states it is, however, difficult to prepare shallow quantum circuits approximating the state with sufficient accuracy. Tensor networks provide a promising avenue of synthesis of such circuits, but most approaches employ 1D Matrix Products States, which struggle to accurately express entangled states in higher dimensions. Here we present a hardware topology-aware quantum state preparation method based on gradient optimization of 2D projected entangled pair states (PEPS). Our approach combines local disentanglement, with global fine tuning based on PEPS gradient optimization. Towards this end we describe an efficient procedure for PEPS gradient computation. We test the convergence and performance of our method in numerical simulations.

papers.title_en: Noise robust super-Heisenberg scaling in time-dependent quantum sensing by subspace-twirled dynamical decoupling
papers.abstract_en: In quantum parameter estimation, time-dependent Hamiltonians can enable ultraprecise estimates of a physical parameter beyond the standard Heisenberg limit, also called the super-Heisenberg limit. However, achieving optimal scaling of the measurement precision typically requires an adaptive quantum control scheme which is resource-intensive and hard to implement in general. Furthermore, this advantage is often severely eroded by environmental noise. We propose the use of a dynamical decoupling scheme based on subspace twirling -- the averaging of random unitaries over a subspace rather than the entire Hilbert space -- to overcome these two limitations. We first prove necessary and sufficient conditions for subspace twirling to preserve the encoding signal while simultaneously removing environmental noise. We then establish conditions and provide performance guarantees for when time dependent Hamiltonians undergoing subspace twirling can achieve super-Heisenberg scaling without adaptive controls. Finally, we illustrate our results using an explicit example where a qubit sensor undergoing a subspace twirl simultaneously suppresses noise and achieves super-Heisenberg scaling. These results offer guidance for the design of ultraprecise quantum sensors under time-dependent and noisy conditions.

papers.title_en: Scalable Pauli propagation through $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear partitioning
papers.abstract_en: Pauli propagation simulates quantum circuits and many-body dynamics by evolving observables in the Heisenberg picture as sparse sums of Pauli strings. As Pauli-string operations reduce to bit manipulations, its performance is limited by memory bandwidth and capacity rather than computational throughput. Pooling the memory of many cores and nodes is hindered by the deduplication step after every gate, which can require global synchronization. We avoid this bottleneck by partitioning the strings with an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear hash function, which guarantees that a $k$-qubit channel couples each partition to at most $4^k$ partitions fixed by the gate, decomposing gate application into independent tasks with bounded communication. Benchmarks of our open-source implementation demonstrate efficient parallel scaling within and across compute nodes, enabling simulations with over $10^{11}$ Pauli strings and extending the accessible timescales of quantum many-body dynamics.

papers.title_en: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abstract_en: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

papers.title_en: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
papers.abstract_en: Memory effects in open quantum systems do not by themselves imply quantum memory, since non-Markovian dynamics can often be reproduced by classical-memory models. Known criteria certify the presence of quantum memory in the environment by comparing the evolution of the system at two different times. We show that quantum memory can remain hidden from all such pairwise tests and become detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. We derive an analytical three-time witness and use it to certify quantum memory in a minimal qubit example in which every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, thus establishing a strict hierarchy of quantum memory effects. Genuine multi-time quantum memory does not rely on fine-tuned time-dependent Hamiltonians or gate-based evolution. We experimentally demonstrate the hierarchy of quantum memory in a time-continuous realization on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings.

papers.title_en: Non-Convex Optimization via Quantum Tunneling Search on a Photonic Chip
papers.abstract_en: Non-convex optimization plays an important role in modern machine learning since plenty of real-world problems have objective functions or constraints with non-convex properties. The non-convex nature of landscapes gives rise to numerous local minima and saddle points, dramatically hindering the ability of gradient descent-based methods to explore the landscape and obtain global optima. Here we present quantum tunneling search (QTS), an algorithm based on quantum tunneling walk and local annealing, which effectively explores the non-convex landscape by leveraging the quantum tunneling effect. In experiments, we map an objective function to the potential term of the waveguide Hamiltonian by controlling the refractive index with the femtosecond direct laser writing technique. With a proper input state, the average probability distributions on 10-micrometer-spaced 29 x 1 and 21 x 9 waveguide arrays highlight the local minima of various 1D and 2D non-convex landscapes, respectively. By further introducing the varying Hamiltonian approach, more efficient search and even the identification of the global minimum are achieved. Our work experimentally verifies that QTS is a successful and efficient non-convex optimization solver, demonstrating quantum speedups over classical stochastic gradient descent (SGD), which serves as a practical application of near-term analog quantum simulators in the field of machine learning.

papers.title_en: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
papers.abstract_en: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $ππN$ effects on top of the two-body $πN$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $πΔ(1232)3/2^+$, and $πN(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $πN$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $πΔ$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.

papers.title_en: Stiffness in Confined Quantum Walks
papers.abstract_en: We investigate boundary-induced stiffness in discrete-time quantum walks confined to a finite lattice by unitary reflecting boundaries implemented through coin-flip operations. We define a dimensionless spreading stiffness from the instantaneous variation of the spatial width relative to the asymptotic spreading rate of the corresponding unconfined Hadamard walk and compare localized, Gaussian, and truncated-uniform initial states. The long-time response retains a strong dependence on the initial spatial profile: the localized and truncated-uniform states show an overall increase in stiffness with increasing confinement size, whereas the Gaussian state exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence with a broad maximum at intermediate sizes. The first and second stiffness moments satisfy the expected asymptotic consistency relation in the high-stiffness regime. The normalized Kullback--Leibler divergence reveals a slower spatial reorganization and qualitatively different finite-size trends, showing that dynamical stiffness and spatial homogenization are distinct properties. These results indicate that unitary confinement produces an intrinsically nonstationary regime whose long-time properties emerge from the interplay between boundary reflections, system size, and the spatial structure of the initial state.

papers.title_en: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
papers.abstract_en: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.

papers.title_en: Crest factor optimization of multi-tone signals generated for low-temperature sensor readout
papers.abstract_en: Microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKID) are a growing technology of cryogenic detectors and have a great potential in radio-astronomy and cosmic microwave background (CMB) characterization. A review of the general readout performance requirements for experiments requiring the multiplexing of large arrays (~10.000 pixels) of such cryogenic detectors is presented. The focus is on the crest factor optimization process for proper excitation and readout of these large arrays of detectors. It is shown an algorithm to optimize the phase generation of the carriers to obtain a low crest factor, favoring the dynamic range usage of the electronic chain.

papers.title_en: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
papers.abstract_en: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure $N$-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation. To resolve scaling bottlenecks of explicit two-body cumulant methods, we project the two-body cumulant onto its lowest unitary invariant and evaluate a susceptibility-windowed orbital scattering scale via a single Coulomb-exchange contraction. Relaxing onto a hyperbolic-tangent cumulant attractor through Markovian collisional relaxation yields a parameter-free Quantum Boltzmann Equation Cumulant-Kernel that regularizes derivative cusps without thermal smearing. Using the collinear $\mathrm{H}_3$ exchange reaction, the symmetric $D_{4h}$ square $\mathrm{H}_4$ dissociation, the non-adiabatic avoided crossing in $\mathrm{BeH}_2$, the symmetric bond cleavage of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the triple-bond dissociation of $\mathrm{N}_2$, the 11-molecule MR-MGN-BE17 dissociation test set, and the singlet diradical isomers of benzyne as case studies, we show that this kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.

papers.title_en: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
papers.abstract_en: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.

papers.title_en: Entanglement detection from moments of the realigned state: application to continuous-variable quantum systems
papers.abstract_en: Certifying entanglement is a central problem in quantum information sciences, especially for continuous-variable quantum systems where full state tomography is experimentally demanding. We introduce a family of separability criteria based on the singular moments and weak moments of the operator obtained by applying the realignment map to the density operator. In practice, we find that the criterion based on the second-order moments of the realigned operator is already sufficient to witness the entanglement of a wide range of quantum optical states. The realigned moments can be readily accessed using an optical scheme consisting of a linear interferometer that couples several identical copies of the state, similarly to the multicopy technique used to measure the partial-transpose moments of a state [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064 (2026)]. We illustrate the detection capability of the second-order realigned-moment method for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including lossy NOON states.

papers.title_en: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
papers.abstract_en: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.

papers.title_en: Implementation of a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD under finite-size parameter estimation
papers.abstract_en: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is a promising technology for quantum-secure communications, offering high secret-key rates and straightforward integration with coherent optical communication systems. Conventional Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD encodes information in both optical-field quadratures, increasing requirements for state preparation, modulation, and calibration, while potentially introducing additional preparation imperfections. Unidimensional (1D) Gaussian modulation offers a simpler alternative by encoding information in only one quadrature, while the conjugate quadrature constrains the protocol's security. However, an integrated experimental 1D implementation combining independent-laser coherent reception with practical reconciliation, finite-size parameter estimation, and privacy amplification remains challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD system over 12~km of standard single-mode fiber using a local local oscillator (LLO) architecture with independent lasers and an integrated offline classical post-processing chain. The implementation includes coherent detection, digital signal processing, information reconciliation, parameter estimation, physicality-constrained security analysis, and privacy amplification. The 1D system achieves a privacy-amplified rate of $1.421$~Mbit/s under the asymptotic security treatment and $0.364$~Mbit/s under the finite-size scenario. These results establish an experimental baseline for the performance--complexity trade-off associated with unidimensional Gaussian modulation and provide an experimental basis for developing lower-complexity CV-QKD transmitters.

papers.title_en: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
papers.abstract_en: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.

papers.title_en: Particle diffusion in magnetized QCD matter with a realistic equation of state
papers.abstract_en: In this study, we investigate particle number diffusion in an interacting hot QCD medium in the presence of an external magnetic field. Starting from an effective covariant description of the medium in terms of quasiparticle degrees of freedom, we employ a Chapman Enskog-like iterative expansion of the distribution function to derive the second-order relativistic magnetohydrodynamic evolution equation for the number diffusion current. The magnetic field introduces additional tensorial structures into the diffusion dynamics, thereby modifying the transport properties of the medium. We further obtain the corresponding Navier-Stokes limit and examine the influence of medium interactions and the magnetic field on the diffusion current and its associated transport coefficients. Our results show that medium interactions suppress the magnetic field-induced anisotropy in particle diffusion. This study provides a consistent framework for investigating dissipative particle transport in magnetized, interacting QCD matter and may serve as an important ingredient in developing realistic hydrodynamic descriptions of heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title_en: Dissecting and diagnosing the LISA Galactic binary population
papers.abstract_en: LISA will individually resolve thousands of Galactic double white dwarf (DWD) binaries, while the majority stays buried in an unresolved gravitational wave (GW) confusion foreground. Which systems get resolved depends on the binary's parameters, on the global population and on instrumental sensitivity, so the resolved population is not a representative sample of the underlying Galactic population. Interpreting LISA's future catalog therefore requires understanding these selection effects. Here we characterize the resolved and unresolved subpopulations of a simulated Milky Way DWD catalog, using an iterative subtraction pipeline applied over different observation times. Resolvability is driven primarily by chirp mass: higher chirp mass, inspiraling systems are strongly favored over lower mass, outspiraling or monochromatic ones, and this reflects on the rate with which different composition subtypes are resolved. Spatially, resolved sources trace the Galactic bulge, because it is intrinsically the densest region of the Galaxy. The confusion background shows an internal bimodal chirp-mass structure, and is not generated uniformly by the same subpopulation in different frequency bands. We introduce a diagnostic for the minimum number of sources needed to reproduce a given fraction of the confusion power in a frequency band, and show that a residual confusion floor persists even after 100 years of integration. These biases are significant and need to be accounted for when using LISA's resolved DWD catalog and the confusion background to constrain the Galactic DWD population.

papers.title_en: Non-Functional Requirements to Hyperparameter Translation for Quantum Software via LLMs
papers.abstract_en: Quantum software engineering (QSE) lacks validated approaches for translating natural-language non-functional requirements (NFRs) into execution parameters such as shots and transpiler optimization levels. Existing methods emphasize semantic similarity rather than execution outcomes. We evaluate seven large language models (LLMs) against a deterministic heuristic baseline using 540 synthetic and 18 real-world user stories. We assess semantic accuracy and execution outcomes, including time, cost, top-state probability, and two-qubit gate exposure, through Qiskit/Aer simulations. All LLMs significantly outperformed the heuristic in semantic accuracy, achieving 55.6 to 83.3 percent on real-world stories compared to 16.7 percent for the heuristic. However, no LLM demonstrated statistically significant superiority over others on the real-world dataset. Speed- and cost-oriented configurations reduced execution time and cost, but fidelity improvements were not supported. Some failures resulted from provider safety refusals rather than translation errors. Our findings demonstrate the potential of LLMs as middleware for NFR-to-configuration translation in QSE, while emphasizing execution-based validation, human oversight, and careful interpretation of model differences.

papers.title_en: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
papers.abstract_en: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array. Furthermore, we apply these devices to nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), successfully demonstrating external nanoscale nuclear-spin detection. These results establish our SiC nanopillars as robust building blocks for scanning quantum probes and scalable sensor networks.

papers.title_en: Analysis of quasielastic scattering and one-neutron transfer channel in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reaction
papers.abstract_en: The strong interplay between the nuclear structure and reaction dynamics near the Coulomb barrier makes the reaction observables a powerful tool for probing the structural properties. To disentangle the roles of nuclear deformation and positive <math><mi>Q</mi></math>-value neutron transfer channels, the angular distributions for quasielastic scattering and neutron transfer have been measured for <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> system and analyzed in the context of the midshell heavy nuclei <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>176</mn></mrow></math>, where inelastic and transfer couplings compete each other. The measured angular distributions for quasielastic and one-neutron transfer have been interpreted in light of coupled reaction calculations using the <math><mi mathvariant="normal" mathsize="small">FRESCO</mi></math> code. Analysis of the quasielastic angular distribution indicated a strong influence of inelastic excitations arising from the large nuclear deformation of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus. The influence of <math><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>-pickup channel was calculated in the single-step and sequential modes. The analysis suggests that the <math><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>-pickup channel have a feeble impact on the angular distribution and the transfer of <math><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> in step mode more adequately explains the experimental data. Furthermore, the analysis of the angular distribution for one neutron pickup channel suggested a significant contribution from higher energy states compared to lower energy states, which might be due to the large deformation of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus. The present study validates the reported values of deformation parameters and spectroscopic factors, respectively, for the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nucleus. The results show a significant impact of the collective nature on the spectroscopic behavior of the reaction partners <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>14</mn></mmultiscripts><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Yb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>176</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, which is reflected in the experimental observables. These measurements provide important input for separating the contributions of positive <math><mi>Q</mi></math>-value transfer channels and nuclear deformation in governing the fusion dynamics.

papers.title_en: Finite-radius gravitational-wave memory from Jacobi holonomy
papers.abstract_en:
Gravitational-wave memory can be encoded in the Jacobi transfer matrix for nearby freely falling detectors. The exact local system is symplectic in six-dimensional separation–velocity space; restriction and projection to a two-dimensional screen inherit this structure through subleading order after longitudinal leakage is counted. For a smooth vacuum Bondi expansion, we compute the screen tide through inverse-radius order r−2, retaining the finite coordinate-curvature term −qAB∂um. After angular-dyad normalization and the vacuum mass-aspect constraint, the reference contribution is
FB =1STF􏰗D DCN 􏰘, N =∂C . AB 2 q (A B)C AB u AB.
The physical response also contains detector normalization, boost, and proper-time pullback corrections. These are evaluated explicitly for a geodesic that is initially at rest in the Bondi coordinates. After free drift is removed, the transfer blocks organize displacement, velocity, drift, and frame-matched rotation-type responses. The r−2 transfer contains both a local subleading insertion and an ordered quadratic Dyson term; the latter is required by the second-order symplectic identities and can generate a rotational part of the separation map. A compact-support, explicit quadrupolar example includes a nonzero detector correction, exact endpoint conditions, and a numerical error budget. A separate exact plane-wave benchmark tests propagation, while the limitations of these diagnostics as tests of a general asymptotically flat spacetime are stated explicitly.

papers.title_en: QSim-Arena: an evolving developer for quantum simulation advantage
papers.abstract_en: Where practical advantage emerges in quantum dynamics simulation remains a central debate in quantum computing. Claimed advantages can be rapidly narrowed or overturned by stronger classical methods, while progress on both sides can outpace the journal publication cycle. We present QSim-Arena, a research framework in which AI agents combine a closed loop of verification and benchmarking with open exploration. Hamiltonians, initial states and accuracy targets for evolved states or observable expectation values provide explicit specifications for evaluating simulation methods. Agents translate published techniques into executable components, reproduce reported results and benchmark their performance across diverse Hamiltonian families. Competing classical methods are implemented and independently crosschecked, providing credible baselines for end-to-end quantum resource estimates based on rigorous error bounds and empirical calibration. Alongside this closed loop, agents recombine classical simulation techniques and co-design fault-tolerant quantum circuits using knowledge extracted from the literature. Initial applications improve baseline resource estimates through the integration of established techniques. QSim-Arena thus treats quantum advantage assessment as an evolving, reproducible research process that can respond to advances in algorithms, error analysis and hardware.

papers.title_en: Structure-Aware Quantum Circuit Equivalence Checking via Sparse Pauli Propagation
papers.abstract_en: Quantum circuit equivalence checking is essential for validating compiler optimizations, but its computational cost can vary substantially with circuit structure. We present a structure-aware equivalence checker for unitary quantum circuits based on sparse Pauli propagation. It combines two complementary verification strategies: generator propagation compares the conjugation actions of the circuits on Pauli generators, while Cut-Miter exploits cancellation between circuit products at selected cut points. A structure-aware verification procedure uses circuit characteristics to select between these strategies while explicitly accounting for numerical and approximation errors. We evaluate our framework against three existing equivalence checkers on two benchmark suites containing circuit pairs with up to 512 qubits. Across 434 scored circuit pairs, our framework produces reference-consistent decisions for 96.3% of the pairs without any incorrect verdicts, while the evaluated baselines achieve at most 68.7% reference-consistent decisions. It also achieves the lowest aggregate runtime among the evaluated tools, reducing total runtime by 48.5%--76.0% relative to these baselines. Ablation studies confirm the benefits of cut-based verification, Pauli-term pruning, and bounded propagation attempts. These results indicate that structure-aware sparse Pauli propagation, combined with complementary verification strategies and explicit error accounting, can provide an effective approach to practical quantum circuit equivalence checking.

papers.title_en: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
papers.abstract_en: We introduce the multi-head quantum neural network (QNN), a quantum module compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices that can replace transformer blocks inside pre-trained large language models (LLMs) with little loss in accuracy and with far fewer parameters than the blocks it replaces. Encoding a model's $D$ hidden neurons into a qubit register is the obstacle: amplitude encoding scales poorly in circuit depth and angle encoding in qubit count, so neither is practical at production-scale width. We instead partition the hidden space into $k$ disjoint heads, angle-encode each into an $n_q$-qubit register, process the heads in parallel, and couple them through constrained classical linear layers, the mixers. Performing surgery on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, we show that a single multi-head QNN with $145\,281$ trainable parameters ($D=2048$, $k=32$, $n_q=8$, $L=4$) can replace a contiguous span of eight transformer blocks, displacing $16.33\%$ of the model's parameters. Ablations show that, for a single replaced block, the quantum heads (circuits followed by a learned readout), and not the classical mixers alone, recover the displaced function, whereas for fused spans the mixers alone come within $1$-$3\%$ of the full module in perplexity. Whether this benefit is specific to trained, entangling quantum circuits is not established: controls that switch the entangler off (two seeds), or freeze the circuit at its initial or at uniformly random angles (one seed), beat the full module on held-out perplexity, and a parameter-matched classical multilayer perceptron remains a few percent ahead of the full module. We train classically with exact statevector simulation, then execute the quantum heads of our fusion checkpoints on a $156$-qubit IBM Heron processor, showing that NISQ-scale quantum modules can be installed in a production-scale LLM and run on hardware.

papers.title_en: Quantum Recurrent Architectures for Financial Time Series Prediction
papers.abstract_en: This study evaluates quantum classical hybrid recurrent architectures for financial time-series forecasting: a Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) network and Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) with lag-based inputs. Classical lag vectors are encoded into quantum states via amplitude encoding, which compactly represents normalized observations but requires nontrivial state preparation; the QLSTM gates and the QRC reservoir are implemented with parameterized quantum circuits, while classical optimizers train the interface and readout layers. On a monthly revenue series extended to 1056 months by a Gaussian-process--hidden-Markov generator, with a fixed chronological 70/15/15 split and one-step-ahead forecasts, we compare both models against a full-size LSTM, a classical control matched in parameter budget and interface architecture, a small plain LSTM, and classical reservoir computing, over ten seeds and against persistence, seasonal-naive and SARIMA benchmark forecasts. The QLSTM, with 2,105 parameters, is statistically indistinguishable from an LSTM 126 times larger, but equally indistinguishable from the matched classical control and from a plain LSTM of the same budget, so its parameter efficiency cannot be attributed to the quantum circuits. The quantum reservoir is worse than a classical reservoir of equal feature dimension in all ten seeds and worse than SARIMA, whereas all recurrent models and both classical reservoirs improve on SARIMA by about 2% in RMSE. In a 24-month rolling-origin backtest the classical LSTMs degrade more slowly than the QLSTM. We find no evidence of a quantum accuracy or parameter-efficiency advantage in this low-dimensional setting.

papers.title_en: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Optimization for CVRPTW: A Systems Framework with Provable Feasibility and Empirical Hardware Limits
papers.abstract_en: Solving large-scale Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problems with Time Windows (CVRPTW) remains challenging because strict operational constraints and scale limit both exact and heuristic methods. We present a hybrid classical-quantum architecture combining Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) with vehicle-level Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO), solved using Toshiba SQBM+ and QAOA on Rigetti Ankaa-3 and IQM Emerald quantum processors. The decomposition avoids the variable growth and constraint-enforcement difficulties of monolithic CVRPTW QUBO formulations. We evaluate the framework on five realistic benchmarks derived from London traffic and location data, spanning 10--70 customers, using a validation pipeline enforcing feasibility and monotone improvement over classical baselines. SQBM+ achieves verified fleet-distance reductions of 2.80% (7,927 m) for the 25-customer instance and 0.22% (1,186 m) for the 55-customer instance. QAOA experiments establish a current hardware boundary for reliable constraint satisfaction at subproblems of up to 4 customers (16 qubits). Diagnostic results identify assignment-level time-window tightness, rather than local route optimization, as the dominant scalability bottleneck. The results demonstrate a practical near-term role for hybrid classical-quantum optimization while establishing empirical limits for current quantum hardware.

papers.title_en: Full Mesh Dynamic Four-User Entanglement-based Switched QKD Network Integrated with SD-KMS
papers.abstract_en: We demonstrate a reconfigurable, four-user, full-mesh quantum key distribution network using polarization entanglement, integrated with a software-defined key management system to orchestrate dynamic optical switching and real-time key provisioning for quantum-safe applications.

papers.title_en: Subadditivity and the failure of strong subadditivity in the Nichols--Wootters family of entropies
papers.abstract_en: We prove subadditivity for the Nichols--Wootters family of entropies interpolating between the von Neumann entropy and the subentropy, with all spectra evaluated in one common ambient dimension. Beyond the von Neumann entropy, equality holds exactly when at least one marginal is pure. This settles the subadditivity conjecture concerning subentropy. Every member except the von Neumann entropy fails strong subadditivity, already on a maximally entangled two-qubit state tensored with a mixed qubit. Its strong-subadditivity defect takes both signs on quantum Markov states. For a pure bipartite state tensored with an ancillary state, we identify the defect with a separately concave product gap and determine its exact maximum under rank constraints. For arbitrary bipartite states, we obtain an explicit lower bound in the marginal purities. For two-qubit states, we determine the optimal coefficient multiplying the product of the smaller marginal eigenvalues in every common ambient dimension, including the subentropy coefficient $1/3$. A positive representation by Haar averages of compressed matrix entropies gives the pinching inequality underlying these results and also yields entropy-gain bounds for unital quantum channels.As an application, each entropy equals the classical communication capacity retained after a specified isotropic partial projective measurement, at a prescribed average input state, even when entangled block encodings are allowed.

papers.title_en: Local enhancement of finite-strength code preparation: recoverability and Wilson coherence
papers.abstract_en: Stabilizer measurements provide a direct route to preparing quantum error-correcting codes and long-range entangled states. In realistic implementations, however, finite measurement strength can coherently deform the encoding map away from the projective limit. Certain nonlocal signatures associated with long-range order can survive such a deformation, but this alone does not guarantee that the resulting state protects encoded quantum information. We show that, at fixed strength, local logical leakage obstructs asymptotically faithful recovery; along logical operators' supports, its accumulation forces the relevant measurement strength to grow logarithmically with code distance. We then prove that this obstruction can be removed locally: for fixed toric registers under sufficiently weak local-stochastic errors, enhancing only a vanishing fraction of checks near selected logical supports restores recovery while the bulk remains at finite measurement strength. With recoverability restored, we prove a further dimensional distinction in logical operations. In the strict three-dimensional deconfined phase, suitable enhanced tubes restore the equivalence of macroscopically separated representatives, so either representative asymptotically implements the same controlled logical action on a fixed encoding. In two dimensions, recoverability alone does not restore this equivalence: the representatives can remain inequivalent even when both associated encodings are recoverable.

papers.title_en: Cumulants of Operator Semigroups for Hierarchies of Many-Particle Evolution Equations
papers.abstract_en: The paper presents a brief overview of recent advances in the mathematical theory of evolution equations for quantum many-particle systems. The structure of expansions representing non-perturbative solutions to the Cauchy problem for hierarchies of fundamental evolution equations for many quantum particles is outlined. It has been shown that the concept of cumulants of operator semigroups forms the basis for non-perturbative representation of solutions to hierarchies of evolution equations that describe the state and observables. It is proven that the constructed dynamics of correlations underlie the description of the evolution of the state, both for finitely and infinitely many particles, governed by the BBGKY hierarchy for reduced density operators or by the hierarchy of nonlinear evolution equations for reduced correlation operators. In fact, it is demonstrated that the behavior of particle correlations governs the dynamics of states in quantum systems with an infinite number of particles.

papers.title_en: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
papers.abstract_en: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger. While for classical graphs the values of the minimum generalised cut and the minimum ordinary cut coincide---recovering the classical max-flow min-cut theorem---we also show how it is more natural to think of flows as duals of generalised cuts instead of ordinary cuts.

papers.title_en: Entanglement, correlations, and resource costs for symmetry-adapted quantum simulations of light through medium-mass nuclei
papers.abstract_en: Entanglement governs both the classical cost of simulating correlated many-body systems and the quantum resources needed to treat them. In this work, we use nuclear symmetries to investigate the entanglement and correlations in nuclei using \textit{ab initio} symmetry-adapted no-core shell-model nuclear wavefunctions, illustrated here for $^{4,6,8}$He, $^8$Be, $^{12}\mathrm{C}$, $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, and $^{48}$Ca. In this many-body approach, deformation and collectivity naturally emerge from the underlying chiral potential, and we show that the Sp(3,$\mathbb{R}$) basis concentrates the ground state in far fewer basis states than the SU(3) basis. We compute single-mode entropies and two-mode mutual information, and examine the organization of like-particle two-nucleon correlations into symmetry channels. Single-mode entropies are largest in the valence shells, while two-mode mutual information reveals substantial correlations both within and between shells. In all cases considered, the dominant pair correlations are captured by fewer SU(3) channels than angular-momentum channels, which reduces the number of variational parameters. Since the number of operator components within the channels is comparable in the two schemes for the heavier nuclei, this gives the SU(3)-coupling scheme a clear advantage. Fiedler ordering of the correlation graph with local refinement reduces the register ordering cost by a factor of 2 to 3 relative to the original shell ordering, and by 10 when two more shells are included in the register. Together, these measures link nuclear correlations to the selection of active modes and candidate excitation operators and to the design of quantum register layouts, offering guidance for the development of hybrid quantum-classical calculations of nuclei.

papers.title_en: High-precision measurement of level leakage via intelligent coherent control
papers.abstract_en: Level leakage constitutes a dominant error source in quantum state control and necessitates accurate characterization for large-scale quantum computing. Quantum sensing provides a viable route for high-precision estimation of level leakage, but its sensitivity can be limited by non-unitary leakage dynamics and interference between the free Hamiltonian and signal generator. This work proposes a reinforcement learning-based quantum sensing algorithm for Hermitian three-level and effective dissipative two-level systems. The algorithm adopts an experimentally feasible pulse-parameter modulation strategy, enabling high-precision and reliable measurement under the specified control and measurement protocol. In both models, DQN-discovered pulse sequences enhance the measurement-model-specific sensing precision, while joint phase--detuning modulation further improves the performance and yields a CFI close to the corresponding QFI.

papers.title_en: Novel method for measuring the isovector partner of X(3872)
papers.abstract_en: The predicted isovector partner of the $X(3872)$, denoted as $W_{c1}$, is expected to produce only a relatively weak structure near the charged $D \bar{D}^*$ threshold, making its experimental identification challenging. In this work, we explore the triangle singularity (TS) mechanism as a means of enhancing the sensitivity to the $W_{c1}$ in the decays $B^0 \to πK \bar{D}^0 D^{*0}$.
